name: Abandoned PA Turnpike: Rays Hill Tunnel
desc: 13 mi of four-lane turnpike bypassed in 1968, now the unmaintained Old PA Pike Trail. From the US-30/Tannery Rd lot at Breezewood it is 1.3 mi on cracked pavement to the 0.7 mi Rays Hill Tunnel. Pitch dark; strong light, own risk.

name: Abandoned PA Turnpike: Sideling Hill Tunnel
desc: The longest tunnel of the original turnpike, 1.3 mi (6,782 ft) of unlit bore abandoned in 1968. About 1.2 mi walk or ride from the Pump Station Rd parking on the old roadway to the east portal. Rough surface, no services, own risk.

name: Abandoned Pennsylvania Turnpike: Rays Hill Tunnel
desc: Cracked four-lane highway left to the weeds since 1968, now walked and biked as the Old PA Pike Trail. From the Breezewood end it is a short ride to the unlit 3,532-ft Rays Hill Tunnel. Bring lights.

name: Annapolis Rock AT
desc: Appalachian Trail north from the US 40 lot to a west-facing cliff over Greenbrier Lake and the Cumberland Valley. Continue to Black Rock Cliff for the full 7.1-mile out-and-back.

name: Assateague Island National Seashore (Maryland)
desc: Undeveloped barrier island south of the state park: ocean beach for miles, wild horses, bayside paddling and backcountry camping. Start at the visitor center before the bridge.

name: Assateague State Park
desc: Two miles of wide Atlantic beach on a barrier island where wild horses wander through the dunes and parking lots. Lifeguards in summer; the bay side has marsh and a nature center.

facts.fee: $5 per person Memorial Day-Labor Day, $5 per vehicle off season

name: Baltimore & Annapolis Trail
desc: 13.3-mile paved rail trail from Glen Burnie to Boulters Way in Arnold, near Jonas Green Park and the Severn River, shaded for much of its length. The Earleigh Heights ranger station is the usual midpoint parking.

name: Battle Creek Cypress Swamp
desc: One of the northernmost stands of bald cypress in the country: a quarter-mile boardwalk loops among 100-foot trees and cypress knees in a swamp that looks like the Deep South.

name: Bear Rocks Preserve
desc: Wind-carved sandstone outcrops and heath barrens on the rim of the Allegheny Front, looking east over ridge after ridge. Steps from the parking area; Forest Road 75 is gated from about January to April.

name: Bearfence Rock Scramble
desc: Short hands-and-feet scramble over a spine of greenstone to one of the few true 360-degree views in the park. Not for wet days. An easier 1.1-mile route reaches a 180-degree viewpoint.

name: Bethlehem Steel Stacks and Hoover-Mason Trestle
desc: 1,650 ft elevated walkway, 46 ft up on an ore trestle built around 1905, running the length of Bethlehem Steel's rusting blast furnaces. Free and open daily at the SteelStacks campus, with history panels along the way.

name: Beverly-Triton Beach Park
desc: Chesapeake Bay beach on the Mayo peninsula with about 5 miles of natural trails around brackish ponds, a fishing pier and a cartop launch. Unguarded swimming; summer weekends need a free reservation pass.

facts.dogs: leashed; not on beach Memorial Day-Labor Day

name: Big Schloss
desc: Climb from Wolf Gap along the state-line ridge to a white sandstone outcrop at 2,964 ft, reached by a wooden footbridge, with views over Trout Run Valley and the Shenandoah Valley.

name: Billy Goat Trail Section A
desc: 1.75-mile rock scramble along the cliffs of Bear Island above Mather Gorge, including a steep climb up a 50-ft rock face. Hiked one way downstream, returning on the towpath; allow 2-3 hours. No dogs.

facts.fee: $20 per vehicle at the Great Falls Tavern entrance

name: Blackwater Falls State Park
desc: The tea-colored Blackwater River drops 57 ft into its canyon. A long staircase and boardwalk lead to decks at the base; an easier paved path reaches an overlook on the far side.

name: Blackwater National Wildlife Refuge - Wildlife Drive
desc: Four-mile drive, also open to walkers and bikes, across tidal marsh and drowned pine forest with one of the largest bald eagle populations on the East Coast. Short side trails; huge skies at dusk.

name: Blue Ridge Tunnel (Crozet Tunnel)
desc: Claudius Crozet's 4,237 ft railroad tunnel under Rockfish Gap, the longest in the US when finished in the 1850s, now a public trail. Unlit and dripping, bring a flashlight; trailheads at Afton (east) and Waynesboro (west). Free.

name: Bombay Hook National Wildlife Refuge
desc: One of the largest tidal salt marshes in the Mid-Atlantic. A 12-mile gravel wildlife drive passes pools packed with snow geese, avocets and ducks, with five short trails and three towers.

name: Burke Lake Park
desc: 4.7-mile unpaved, mostly flat loop around a wooded lake. Herons and ospreys, fishing, rowboat and canoe rentals at the marina and evening light across the water. Swimming is prohibited.

facts.fee: free for Fairfax County residents; per-vehicle fee for non-residents on weekends, April-October

name: Calvert Cliffs State Park
desc: The 1.8-mile Red Trail runs past a beaver marsh to a quarter-mile Bay beach under Miocene cliffs. Sift the sand and wash line for fossil shark teeth.

name: Cape Henlopen State Park
desc: Delaware's largest park, where the bay meets the Atlantic: a guarded ocean beach with bathhouse, pine forest and dunes, a nature center, a bay fishing pier and miles of bike paths.

name: Catoctin Mountain Park
desc: Full circuit from the visitor center linking Chimney Rock, Wolf Rock, Thurmont Vista, Blue Ridge Summit Overlook and Hog Rock, ending at Cunningham Falls. Signed but unblazed, so carry the park map.

facts.dogs: leashed; not allowed on the rock formations

name: Cedar Run - Whiteoak Canyon Circuit
desc: Down Cedar Run past slides and plunge pools, then up Whiteoak Canyon past six waterfalls. Among the hardest and wettest day hikes in the park, with several stream crossings and many places to swim.

name: Chimney Top (North Fork Mountain)
desc: Relentless climb from Smoke Hole Road up the north end of North Fork Mountain to sandstone towers and a cliff-edge view down the North Fork valley to the Allegheny Front.

name: Chincoteague National Wildlife Refuge - Wildlife Loop
desc: Paved 3.2-mile loop around Snow Goose Pool on Assateague Island, for walkers and bikes all day and cars only after 3 pm. Egrets, shorebirds and the wild ponies grazing the marsh.

facts.fee: $10 per vehicle daily, $25 weekly; free on foot or bike

name: Chincoteague Refuge Beach (Toms Cove)
desc: The wild Atlantic beach at the end of the refuge road: no buildings beyond a small visitor center, lifeguards in summer, and miles of sand to walk south along Toms Cove.

name: Claudius Crozet Blue Ridge Tunnel
desc: Walk through a 4,273-foot railroad tunnel finished in 1858 under Rockfish Gap: brick lining gives way to bare hand-drilled rock, pitch dark and dripping. Bring a strong flashlight.

name: Conowingo Dam (Fisherman's Park)
desc: Shoreline park below the dam on the Harford side where bald eagles gather in large numbers to fish, peaking from November into January. Free; photographers line the fence at dawn.

name: Coopers Rock Overlook
desc: Sandstone promontory with a footbridge and railings high above the Cheat River canyon, with boulder mazes just behind it. The entrance road is closed December 31 to March 31; walk in from the I-68 lot.

name: Crabtree Falls
desc: Five major cascades falling a total of 1,200 ft; a graded trail climbs 1.7 miles beside them to the top, with a paved path to the first overlook. Stay off the slick rock. About 163 miles from Pasadena.

name: Daniels Ghost Town
in: Patapsco Valley State Park Alberton Area
desc: Mill town closed in 1968 and finished off by the 1972 Agnes flood. Flat walk on old Alberton Rd in Patapsco Valley State Park to the stone shell of St. Stanislaus church (burned 1926), a second church, house ruins and buried cars.

name: Downs Park
desc: Bayfront park on the Bodkin peninsula with over five miles of paved and natural trails, a fishing pier, a Chesapeake Bay overlook, Mother's Garden and a dog beach. No swimming beach for people.

name: Eastern Neck National Wildlife Refuge
desc: Island refuge at the mouth of the Chester River reached by a small bridge. Seven short trails and boardwalks reach Bay overlooks and marsh; thousands of tundra swans and ducks in winter.

name: Eastern State Penitentiary
desc: Castle-walled prison that operated 1829-1971 and is kept as a stabilized ruin: long vaulted cellblocks with peeling cells radiating from a central hub. Ticketed, with a self-guided audio tour; Fairmount neighborhood.

facts.access: Open by guided tour or by arrangement only. Check before you go.

name: Fair Hill Natural Resources Management Area
desc: Former du Pont estate of 5,600 acres with about 80 miles of well-marked trails over rolling pasture and woods along Big Elk Creek. Among the best trail-running ground in the state.

name: Flag Ponds Nature Park
desc: Half-mile walk through woods to a wide, quiet Bay beach with shark teeth in the wash line, plus ponds, boardwalks and a fishing pier. Non-county visitors pay a much higher gate fee.

facts.fee: Non-Calvert residents: $20 per vehicle Apr-Oct, $5 Nov-Mar

name: Flat Rock (Colonel Denning State Park)
desc: Rocky climb of more than 900 ft from the park to an outcrop on Blue Mountain with a 180-degree view of the Cumberland Valley. Cool off afterward at the park's small lake beach.

name: Fort Delaware State Park (Pea Patch Island)
desc: Granite Civil War fortress and prison on an island in the Delaware River, reached only by a seasonal ferry from Delaware City. The island also holds a large heron and egret rookery.

facts.fee: Ferry and fort $12 adults; runs late April-September

name: Fort McHenry National Monument (Seawall Trail)
desc: Star fort that inspired the national anthem, on a point in Baltimore harbor. The grounds and the roughly one-mile seawall loop are free and give open views of the port; the fort itself has an entry fee.

facts.fee: grounds free; fee to enter the fort

name: Fort Miles
desc: WWII fort in the dunes of Cape Henlopen State Park: Battery 519 (now a museum), big guns on display, barracks and concrete fire-control towers, one of which you can climb. Park entry fee.

name: Fort Smallwood Park
desc: Peninsula where the Patapsco River and Rock Creek meet the Bay: public swimming beach, 380-foot fishing pier, paved paths, boat ramp and an 1890s gun battery. Opens 5:30 a.m.

name: Franciscan Monastery of the Holy Land
desc: 1898 monastery with full-size replicas of Holy Land shrines and underground catacombs, shown on free guided tours (hourly, Mon-Sat from 10, Sun from 1). Rose gardens and grottoes open daily.

name: Gordons Pond Trail
desc: Crushed-stone trail, 3.2 miles one way, from the north edge of Rehoboth past a salt lagoon full of wading birds and over a raised boardwalk through the dunes. Two WWII towers stand on the beach.

name: Great Falls Overlook (Olmsted Island), C&O Canal
desc: Boardwalk and footbridges cross the rocky side channels of Olmsted Island to a platform facing the main falls. Starts on the towpath just below Great Falls Tavern. No dogs or bikes on the boardwalk.

facts.fee: $20 per vehicle, 7 days (also valid at Great Falls Park, VA)

name: Great Falls Park
desc: Three overlooks a few minutes from the lot face the Potomac dropping through jagged rock into Mather Gorge. The River Trail then follows the cliff edge downstream. No swimming or wading.

facts.fee: $20 per vehicle, 7 days (also valid at C&O Canal Great Falls, MD)

name: Gunpowder Falls State Park - Hereford Area
desc: The wildest stretch of the Gunpowder, below Prettyboy Dam: narrow trails on both banks through hemlock and laurel beside a cold, clear trout river. Lots at Falls Road, Masemore Road and Bunker Hill Road.

name: Harpers Ferry Lower Town and The Point
desc: Restored 19th-century streets of John Brown's raid ending at The Point, where the Shenandoah meets the Potomac under the cliffs of Maryland and Loudoun Heights. Park at the visitor center and ride the shuttle.

facts.fee: $20 per vehicle or $10 per person, valid 3 days

name: Hawksbill Summit
desc: Highest point in Shenandoah (4,050 ft). A stone platform at the top gives a 360-degree view over the valley, Massanutten and the Piedmont. 1.7 miles direct, or a 2.9-mile loop using the AT.

name: Hoopers Island - Tylers Cove
desc: Public landing on Upper Hooper Island, the start of a narrow road that runs between the Honga River and the open Bay past crab houses and over a high causeway bridge. Water in every direction at sunset.

name: Humpback Rocks
desc: Steep mile (800 ft) from Blue Ridge Parkway milepost 6 to a jutting greenstone outcrop with views of the Shenandoah Valley and Shenandoah National Park. Loop back on the AT. About 150 miles from home.

name: Huntley Meadows Park
desc: Half-mile boardwalk across a large freshwater marsh with an observation tower. Beavers, herons, egrets and turtles are seen at close range; flat forest paths lead in. No dogs on the boardwalk.

name: Janes Island State Park
desc: Marsh island on Tangier Sound with seven marked water trails starting at the park marina. Paddle through the guts to miles of empty beach that can only be reached by boat.

facts.fee: No day-use fee; boat ramp $7 MD residents, $9 out-of-state

name: Jug Bay Wetlands Sanctuary
desc: Over 1,700 protected acres on the tidal Patuxent: forest trails, marsh boardwalks and an observation deck over freshwater wetlands full of ospreys, herons and wild rice. Open Wed, Fri, Sat, Sun, 9-5.

name: Kilgore Falls (Falling Branch Area)
desc: Maryland's second-highest free-falling waterfall, a 17-foot drop into a wading pool, a short walk from a 28-car lot. Free reservations are required on weekends and holidays, Memorial Day to Labor Day.

facts.fee: free; reservation on summer weekends and holidays

name: King and Queen Seat (Rocks State Park)
desc: 190-foot rock outcrop high above Deer Creek, reached by a short steep climb. Bare ledges with unfenced drops and a wide view over the wooded valley; also a rock-climbing spot.

name: Ladew Topiary Gardens
desc: 22 acres with 15 garden rooms built by Harvey Ladew from the 1930s, including a topiary fox hunt and clipped swans, plus a nature walk. Open April through October; admission charged.

name: Leesylvania State Park
desc: Sandy Potomac shoreline with picnic lawns, a 300-ft fishing pier and a car-top boat launch. Lee's Woods Trail climbs past a Civil War gun battery and old home sites. Fills early on summer weekends.

name: Lindy Point
desc: Railed platform on a rock tower jutting into Blackwater Canyon, reached by a short flat path through rhododendron. The standard sunset spot in the park.

name: Lions Head (Dolly Sods Wilderness)
desc: Sandstone prow on Breathed Mountain overlooking the Red Creek canyon. Usually climbed from the Red Creek trailhead at Laneville; the last pitch is an unmarked path among boulders.

name: Loch Raven Reservoir
desc: Forested Baltimore reservoir with miles of fire-road and shoreline trails. Loch Raven Drive has traditionally closed to cars on weekends (10-5) for walkers and cyclists; confirm that it still does.

name: Luray Caverns
desc: The big one: paved paths through rooms of columns, draperies and mirror pools, plus the Great Stalacpipe Organ, which taps stalactites to play notes. Discovered 1878; open daily.

name: Mallows Bay Ghost Fleet
desc: The largest shipwreck fleet in the Western Hemisphere: wooden WWI steamships burned and sunk in a Potomac cove, now hull-shaped islands. Outlines show from the county park shore; paddle among them from the free ramp at low tide.

name: Mallows Bay Park
desc: The "Ghost Fleet": more than 100 wooden WWI steamships scuttled in a Potomac cove, now islands of trees and osprey nests. See hulls from the shore trail at low tide or paddle among them.

name: Maryland Heights Stone Fort and Naval Battery
desc: Civil War works on the mountain facing Harpers Ferry: the Naval Battery, gun pits and the unfinished 1862 Stone Fort, the park's largest stone Civil War structure, on the 1,448 ft crest. Steep 4.5-6.5 mi round trip from Lower Town.

name: Maryland Heights Trail
desc: Steep climb to a cliff straight above Harpers Ferry and the two rivers; the longer loop adds the Civil War stone fort. Fall 2026: Lower Town footbridge closed for repairs, NPS shuttle runs to Lock 34.

facts.fee: $20 per vehicle or $10 per person, valid 3 days

name: Marys Rock
desc: Steady climb on the Appalachian Trail from Panorama at Thornton Gap to a bare rock summit with a wide westward view. The shorter Meadow Spring route (mile 33.5) is 2.9 miles.

name: Mason Neck State Park
desc: Peninsula park on Belmont Bay known for bald eagles. Six miles of dirt trails and three paved, with elevated walkways over the marsh; canoe, kayak and paddleboard rentals from Memorial Day to Labor Day.

name: Mount Vernon Trail
desc: 18-mile paved trail along the Potomac from Theodore Roosevelt Island to Mount Vernon, passing Gravelly Point, Old Town Alexandria, Jones Point and Dyke Marsh. River views most of the way.

name: Muddy Creek Falls
desc: Maryland's tallest free-falling waterfall, a 54-ft drop reached by a short walk through old hemlocks, with decks at top and bottom. Summer weekends need a day-use reservation.

facts.fee: $3 per person MD residents, $5 out of state in season and on May, Sept and Oct weekends; $3 per car other times; reservation required weekends and holidays Memorial Day-Labor Day

name: North Point State Park
desc: Bayfront park on the site of the Bay Shore amusement park (1906-1947): the restored trolley station and fountain, a long pier, a small wading beach, and trails through the Black Marsh wildland.

name: Old Rag Mountain
desc: The park's most popular hike: a mile of granite scrambling through cracks and over boulders to a 360-degree summit, then down the Saddle Trail and fire road. Very strenuous; allow 7-8 hours.

facts.fee: $30/vehicle park entry (7 days) plus $2 Old Rag day-use ticket per person, required Mar 1-Nov 30 (recreation.gov, 800/day)

name: Patapsco Valley State Park - Avalon/Orange Grove Area
desc: The park's busiest area, in the river gorge below Elkridge: trails to Cascade Falls, the swinging bridge at Orange Grove, Lost Lake and the paved Grist Mill Trail. Entrance on South Street; fills on weekends.

name: Patuxent River Park: Jug Bay Natural Area
desc: Tidal freshwater marsh on the Patuxent: boardwalks, an observation tower, wooded trails and group campsites. Canoe and kayak rentals at Jackson's Landing on weekends and holidays, April to October.

name: Paw Paw Tunnel
desc: 3,118-ft brick-lined canal tunnel you walk through by flashlight on the old towpath, with a rock gorge at the far end. Return over the top on the steep 2-mile Tunnel Hill Trail.

name: Piscataway Park and National Colonial Farm
desc: Quiet Potomac shoreline preserved to protect the view from Mount Vernon, directly across the river. Fishing pier, riverside and woodland trails, a marsh boardwalk and a colonial-era farm.

name: Point Lookout State Park
desc: The tip of Southern Maryland, where the Potomac meets the Bay: swimming beach, fishing pier, an 1830 lighthouse and the remains of a Civil War prison camp. Water on both sides of the road.

facts.fee: $5 per vehicle; $7 per person on weekends and holidays May-Sep

name: Prince William Forest Park
desc: About 15,000 acres of piedmont forest with 37 miles of trails along Quantico Creek and its small falls, 1930s cabin camps, an old pyrite mine site and a hilly scenic loop road for cycling.

name: Quiet Waters Park
desc: 340 acres between the South River and Harness Creek: miles of paved forest trails, the South River Overlook, a dog beach, kayak rentals in season, gardens and outdoor sculpture.

name: Reddish Knob
desc: Drive-up summit at 4,397 ft on Shenandoah Mountain: a narrow paved road ends at a small lot with a full 360-degree view into Virginia and West Virginia. Open to both sunrise and sunset.

name: Riprap Hollow - Wildcat Ridge Loop
desc: Long wilderness loop past Calvary Rocks and Chimney Rock, down a hollow with a small waterfall and a deep, cold swimming hole, then back up Wildcat Ridge and the AT.

name: Sandy Point State Park
desc: State park at the western foot of the Bay Bridge with a long sandy swimming beach, views of the bridge and Sandy Point Shoal Light, jetties for fishing and winter waterfowl. Fills on summer weekends.

facts.fee: $4 weekdays, $5 weekends per person in summer

name: Scott's Run Nature Preserve
desc: Steep, rooty trails through hemlock and beech ravines to a small waterfall where Scott's Run drops into the Potomac, plus bluff-top river views. Two small lots fill early; no wading or swimming.

name: Seneca Rocks
desc: Blade of white quartzite standing 900 ft over the North Fork. A graded trail with switchbacks and steps climbs to a platform near the top; the exposed summit ridge beyond is a scramble.

name: Shenandoah Pulp Factory Ruins (Virginius and Hall's Islands)
desc: Massive stone piers and sluiceways of a pulp mill built 1887-88 on the old Hall's Rifle Works island, run until 1935 and wrecked by the 1936 flood. On the flat Virginius and Hall's Islands trail (up to 2 mi round trip) off Shenandoah St.

name: Sky Meadows State Park
desc: Open pastures climbing the east face of the Blue Ridge to the Appalachian Trail; the Piedmont Overlook looks back across rolling farm country. Historic Mount Bleak farm and an International Dark Sky Park.

name: Soldier's Delight Natural Area
desc: 1,900 acres of serpentine barrens: stunted pines, prairie grasses and rare wildflowers on thin green rock that looks nothing like the rest of Maryland. About 7 miles of trails pass old chromite mines.

name: Spruce Knob
desc: West Virginia's highest point at 4,863 ft: drive to the top, then walk the half-mile loop through wind-bent red spruce and boulder fields to a stone lookout tower.

name: Strickler Knob
desc: Unofficial spur off the Massanutten Trail along a narrow rock spine, ending in a hands-on scramble to a pinnacle with a 360-degree view of Page Valley and New Market Gap. Blazes may be missing.

name: Sugarloaf Mountain
desc: Privately owned 1,282-ft mountain standing alone above the farmland, open daily 8 to sunset (entrance gate shuts at 4). Short steep trails climb from the upper lots to cliff-top views; longer loops circle it.

name: Susquehanna State Park
desc: Wooded hills dropping to the lower Susquehanna: about 15 miles of trails, the working Rock Run Grist Mill, a canal toll house, big old trees and a riverside path upstream to Conowingo Dam.

name: Terrapin Nature Park
desc: 276 acres at the foot of the Bay Bridge: a 3.25-mile oyster-shell trail through meadow, tidal ponds and woods to a long, quiet Bay beach with driftwood and bridge views.

name: The Pinnacle Overlook
desc: Rocky bluff 380 ft above Lake Aldred on the Susquehanna, with picnic tables at the rim and trail links to Kelly's Run and Tucquan Glen. Now part of Susquehannock State Park.

name: Torrey C. Brown Rail Trail (NCR Trail)
desc: Crushed-stone rail trail running 19.7 miles from Ashland to the Pennsylvania line along the Gunpowder and Little Falls. The restored Monkton Station is the hub; tubers put in on the river there in summer.

name: Trap Pond State Park
desc: The northernmost natural stand of bald cypress on the East Coast, rising out of a millpond. Paddle among the trees or walk the 4.5-mile Bob Trail around the pond.

name: Turkey Point Lighthouse (Elk Neck State Park)
desc: Easy gravel walk along 100-foot bluffs to an 1833 lighthouse at the tip of Elk Neck, where the Elk and North East rivers meet at the head of the Bay. Hawk-watch platform in fall.

name: U.S. National Arboretum (Capitol Columns)
desc: 446-acre arboretum above the Anacostia. Twenty-two sandstone columns removed from the Capitol in 1958 stand in an open meadow; also azalea hillsides, Fern Valley and a bonsai museum.

name: Upper Falls of Seneca Creek
desc: Seneca Creek Trail drops gently through spruce and old meadows, with stream crossings, to the Upper Falls and a run of cascades. A long day hike or a classic overnight.

name: White Cliffs of Conoy
desc: Chalk-white bluffs of limestone quarry waste dumped beside the Susquehanna. Walk or bike 1.5 flat, paved miles south from Koser Park on the river trail.

name: Wye Island Natural Resources Management Area
desc: Low island of fields and old woods wrapped by the Wye River. Flat lanes and trails pass a holly tree nearly 300 years old and Schoolhouse Woods, one of the Shore's last old-growth stands.

name: Assateague Island
desc: Barrier island with wild ponies, pristine beaches, and undeveloped seashore.

name: Beachwood Park
desc: Small wooded county park with natural trails down to the water, a cartop boat launch and fishing. Open sunrise to sunset; restrooms on site.

name: Billy Goat Trail
desc: Rugged rock-scramble trail along the Potomac River near Great Falls.

name: Blackwater National Wildlife Refuge
desc: Tidal marsh refuge on the Eastern Shore — eagles, migratory birds, eerie tidelands.

name: C&O Canal Towpath
desc: 184.5-mile flat towpath from DC to Cumberland along the Potomac River. This pin is the Great Falls Tavern access in Potomac, MD.

name: Cascade Falls
in: Patapsco Valley State Park Orange Grove Area
desc: Small stepped waterfall on a side stream a short rocky walk uphill from the Orange Grove lot and swinging bridge, with a longer loop trail continuing above it. Wading pool at the base.

name: Chesapeake Bay Bridge Viewpoint
desc: Sandy Point beach gives the best ground-level view of the twin Bay Bridge spans.

name: Crystal Grottoes Caverns
desc: Maryland's only show cave: guided walks through narrow passages crowded with formations. Privately run with paid admission; check hours before driving out.

name: Cunningham Falls
desc: Maryland's tallest cascading waterfall, 78 ft down a rock face on Big Hunting Creek. Walk in from the Hunting Creek Lake lot or take the boardwalk from the MD 77 roadside lot.

facts.fee: William Houck Area: $3-5 per person in season for MD residents (+$2 out of state); $3 per vehicle off-season

name: Cunningham Falls Manor Area
desc: Lower section of Cunningham Falls SP with Hunting Creek Lake and fishing.

name: Dolly Sods Wilderness
desc: High-elevation plateau wilderness in WV — wind-sculpted spruce, red bogs, and sweeping heath barrens unlike anywhere else in the region.

name: Easton Point Park
desc: Small park at Easton Point, the head of the Tred Avon River a mile west of downtown Easton, beside the public landing. Benches and open water views; an easy place to read by the river.

name: Edgar Allan Poe House
desc: The poet's childhood Baltimore home, now a small museum in the Poe neighborhood.

name: Gambrill State Park
desc: Stone overlooks built by the CCC in the 1930s on High Knob: one looks east over Frederick, another west across the Middletown Valley to South Mountain. Trail loops start nearby.

facts.fee: $3 per vehicle MD residents, $5 out of state

name: Gathland State Park
desc: Ruins of a Civil War correspondent's mountaintop estate and his stone War Correspondents Memorial Arch, right on the Appalachian Trail at Crampton's Gap.

name: Gunpowder Falls State Park
desc: Long river corridor park north of Baltimore with swimming holes and trails.

name: High Rock
desc: Graffiti-covered cliff on South Mountain, a former resort observatory site and now a hang-glider launch, with a wide view west over the Cumberland Valley. Parking is right beside it.

name: Hooper's Island Overlook
desc: Remote Eastern Shore peninsula where the Honga River meets the Bay — wide open water views, working watermen docks, and some of the best sunsets in Maryland. Feels like the edge of the world.

name: Kinder Farm Park
desc: 288-acre former farm with a 2.4-mile paved perimeter loop, several miles of natural trails, farm animals, a 1925 farmhouse museum and fishing ponds.

name: Lake Waterford Park
desc: 108-acre park around a 12-acre lake with paved and natural trails, shoreline fishing and waterfowl. Free. A dredging project was limiting fishing and trail access in 2026.

name: Merkle Wildlife Sanctuary
desc: Fields and ponds on the Patuxent that hold the largest wintering flock of Canada geese on the Bay's western shore. Trails and a driving-tour road; grounds open sunrise to sunset, visitor center by reservation.

name: National Harbor
desc: Waterfront development on the Potomac with sweeping river views and the Awakening statue.

name: North Beach Town Beach
desc: Small Chesapeake Bay beach town with a public boardwalk and sandy beach — good sunset spot, vintage feel, easy drive south from Pasadena.

name: Patapsco Valley State Park
desc: Sprawling state park along the Patapsco River with miles of trails.

name: Piney Orchard Nature Preserve
desc: 45-acre wetland forest preserve with large ponds and 5 miles of hiking and biking trails, bordered by the Little Patuxent River and the Patuxent Research Refuge. Connects to the WB&A Trail.

name: Pot Rocks
in: Gunpowder Falls State Park Sweathouse Area
desc: Smooth potholed rock ledges and pools in the Big Gunpowder, about a mile's walk upstream from the Belair Road (US 1) lot. A long-standing local wading and swimming spot with swift current in places.

name: Prettyboy Dam
desc: 1930s concrete dam in a steep wooded gorge at the head of the Gunpowder. A road crosses the top with a view down the face; rough trails lead to the river below and into the reservoir watershed.

name: Prettyboy Reservoir
desc: Remote reservoir north of Baltimore — quiet trails and undeveloped shoreline.

name: Roaches Run Waterfowl Sanctuary
desc: A hidden tidal marsh full of herons and ducks sitting directly beneath Reagan Airport's flight path — planes roar 200 ft overhead while egrets fish below. Surreal.

name: Robinson Nature Center
desc: County nature center above the Middle Patuxent with about a mile of wooded trails down to the river and the remains of Simpsonville Mill. Trails are free; the exhibit building charges admission.

name: Rock Creek Park
desc: Urban national park running through DC with forested trails and creek.

name: Rocks State Park
desc: Dramatic rock outcrops in the Deer Creek valley, including the King and Queen Seat.

name: Seneca Creek State Park
desc: The 3.7-mile Lake Shore Trail circles 90-acre Clopper Lake; boat rentals in season. The park's 50+ miles of trails include the 16.5-mile Seneca Creek Greenway down to the Potomac.

facts.fee: $3 per person MD residents, $5 others (weekends and holidays, Apr-Oct)

name: Severn Run Natural Environment Area
desc: About 1,700 acres of undeveloped state land along Severn Run, the headwaters of the Severn River. No facilities; unmarked woods trails and stream fishing from small roadside pull-offs.

name: Shenandoah National Park
desc: Blue Ridge Mountains with Skyline Drive, 500+ miles of trails, and wildlife.

name: Sideling Hill Road Cut
desc: I-68 passes through a 340-ft-deep notch blasted out of Sideling Hill, exposing rock layers bent into a giant U. Pull into the rest area and walk up to the viewing platforms.

name: Smoke Hole Canyon
desc: Narrow road following the South Branch Potomac through a 20-mile gorge walled by Cave Mountain and North Fork Mountain, ending at Big Bend Campground inside a loop of the river.

name: South Mountain State Park
desc: AT corridor and Civil War battlefield ridge with long mountain views.

name: Swallow Falls State Park
desc: The Youghiogheny drops over broad sandstone ledges; people wade and swim in the pools below in summer. Part of the canyon loop through hemlocks more than 300 years old.

facts.fee: same day-use charge as Muddy Creek Falls

name: The Magothy Greenway Natural Area
desc: 369 acres of woods and wetlands near the Magothy River with about 4 miles of natural-surface trails. Park at Loopers Field on North Shore Road. Closes until 1 p.m. on deer-management days.

name: Weverton Cliffs
desc: Switchbacks on the Appalachian Trail from the Weverton Road lot lead to open cliffs high above the Potomac, looking upriver toward Harpers Ferry. Short and steep.

name: Wildflower Trail
desc: Wooded trail in Kinder Farm Park in Millersville, off the park's paved loop. It links with the Blackberry and Bunks Pond trails.

name: Winkler Botanical Preserve
desc: 44-acre native-plant preserve hidden among the Mark Center office blocks: woodland paths, a pond, streams and a built waterfall. Run by NOVA Parks; open daily 8:30 to 4.

name: Benjamin Rush State Park
desc: Benjamin Rush State Park is a 275-acre (111 ha) Pennsylvania state park in Philadelphia, Philadelphia County, Pennsylvania, in the United States. The park is undeveloped and is the site of community gardens, believed to be one of the largest in the world.

name: Blue Knob State Park
desc: Blue Knob State Park is a 6,128-acre (2,480 ha) Pennsylvania state park in Kimmel, Lincoln, and Pavia townships in Bedford County, Pennsylvania, in the United States. The average annual snowfall at the park is about 12 feet (370 cm).

name: Canoe Creek State Park
desc: Canoe Creek State Park is a 961-acre (389 ha) Pennsylvania state park in Frankstown Township in Blair County, Pennsylvania. It is 12 miles east of Altoona, the nearest city. Canoe Lake, at 155 acres (63 ha), is the focus of recreation at the park and is open for fishing year-round.

name: Cunningham Falls State Park
desc: Cunningham Falls State Park is a Maryland state park located west of Thurmont, Maryland, in the United States. The state park is the home of Cunningham Falls, the largest cascading waterfall in Maryland, a 43-acre (17 ha) man-made lake, and the remains of a historic iron furnace.

name: Delaware Seashore State Park
desc: Delaware Seashore State Park is a public recreation area located near Dewey Beach in Delaware, United States. It is bounded on the east by the Atlantic Ocean and on the west by Rehoboth Bay and Indian River Bay. The park covers 2,722 acres (1,102 ha).

name: Elk Neck State Park
desc: Elk Neck State Park is a Maryland state park located between the Chesapeake Bay and the Elk River near the southern tip of the Elk Neck Peninsula in Cecil County, Maryland. The park is home to the historic Turkey Point Light and offers land-based and water-based recreation.

name: Fort Washington State Park
desc: Fort Washington State Park is a 493-acre (200 ha) Pennsylvania state park in Springfield and Whitemarsh Townships in Montgomery County, Pennsylvania. The park is noted for the springtime flowering of dogwood trees, and is popular with families for picnics and hiking.

name: French Creek State Park
desc: French Creek State Park is a 7,730-acre (3,130 ha) Pennsylvania state park in North Coventry and Warwick Townships in Chester County and Robeson and Union Townships in Berks County, Pennsylvania. It straddles northern Chester County and southern Berks County along French Creek.

name: Keystone State Park
desc: Keystone State Park is a 1,200-acre (486 ha) Pennsylvania state park in Derry Township, Westmoreland County, Pennsylvania in the United States. Located off U.S. Route 22 near New Alexandria, the park opened in 1945. Its main attraction is the man-made 78-acre (32 ha) Keystone Lake.

name: Laurel Hill State Park
desc: Laurel Hill State Park is a 4,062-acre (1,644 ha) Pennsylvania state park in Jefferson and Middlecreek townships, Somerset County, Pennsylvania in the United States.

name: Laurel Mountain State Park
desc: Laurel Mountain State Park is a 493-acre (200 ha) Pennsylvania state park in Ligonier Township, Westmoreland County and Jenner Township, Somerset County, Pennsylvania in the United States.

name: Laurel Ridge State Park
desc: Laurel Ridge State Park is a 13,625-acre (5,514 ha) Pennsylvania state park that with parcels in Cambria, Fayette, Somerset, and Westmoreland counties, Pennsylvania in the United States.

name: Linn Run State Park
desc: Linn Run State Park is a Pennsylvania state park on 612 acres (248 ha) in Cook and Ligonier Townships, Westmoreland County, Pennsylvania in the United States. The park borders Forbes State Forest.

name: Marsh Creek State Park
desc: Marsh Creek State Park is a 1,705 acres (690 ha) Pennsylvania state park in Upper Uwchlan and Wallace Townships, Chester County, Pennsylvania in the United States. The park is the location of the 535-acre (217 ha) man-made Marsh Creek Lake.

name: Matthew Henson State Park
desc: Matthew Henson State Park is a Maryland state park and greenway situated along a tributary of Rock Creek in Montgomery County, Maryland. The park is managed by Montgomery County under an agreement with the Maryland Department of Natural Resources.

name: Ohiopyle State Park
desc: Ohiopyle State Park is a Pennsylvania state park situated on 20,500 acres (8,300 ha) between Chestnut Ridge and Laurel Hill in Dunbar, Henry Clay, and Stewart Townships, Fayette County, Pennsylvania, in the United States.

name: Pine Grove Furnace State Park
desc: Pine Grove Furnace State Park is a protected Pennsylvania area that includes Laurel and Fuller Lakes in Cooke Township of Cumberland County.

name: Prince Gallitzin State Park
desc: Prince Gallitzin State Park is a 6,467-acre (2,617 ha) Pennsylvania state park with acreage in both Chest and White Townships in Cambria County of West Central Pennsylvania in the United States, near both Gallitzin Borough, & Gallitzin Township in the greater Altoona, Pennsylvania area.

name: Ridley Creek State Park
desc: Ridley Creek State Park is a 2,606-acre (1,055 ha) Pennsylvania state park in Edgmont, Middletown, and Upper Providence Townships, Delaware County, Pennsylvania in the United States.

name: Shawnee State Park
desc: Shawnee State Park is a 3,983-acre (1,612 ha) Pennsylvania state park in Juniata and Napier Townships, Bedford County, Pennsylvania in the United States. Shawnee Lake, a 451-acre (183 ha) warm water reservoir, is at the center of the park as its main attraction.

name: Tyler State Park
desc: Tyler State Park is a day-use Pennsylvania state park on 1,711 acres (692 ha) in Newtown and Northampton Townships, Bucks County, Pennsylvania, United States. Park roads, trails, and facilities are nestled within the original farm and woodland setting.

name: Wolf Trap National Park for the Performing Arts
desc: Wolf Trap National Park for the Performing Arts (originally known as the Wolf Trap Farm Park for the Performing Arts and simply known as Wolf Trap) is a performing arts center located on 117 acres (47 ha) of national park land in unincorporated Fairfax County, Virginia, near the town of Vienna.

name: Yellow Creek State Park
desc: Yellow Creek State Park is a Pennsylvania state park on 2,981 acres (1,206 ha) in Brush Valley and Cherryhill Townships, Indiana County, Pennsylvania in the United States. The park encompasses parts of Yellow Creek and Little Yellow Creek. The old Kittanning Path goes through the parkland.

name: Belle Isle State Park
desc: Belle Isle State Park is located in Lancaster County, Virginia, on the Rappahannock River. It sits between Deep Creek and Morattico Creek and is currently under public ownership. The park has an area of 892 acres (3.61 km2) and has facilities for camping, fishing, boating and picnics.

name: Lost River State Park
desc: Lost River State Park is a state park located in Hardy County, West Virginia near the community of Mathias. The park encompasses 3,712 acres (15.02 km2) managed by the West Virginia Division of Natural Resources.

name: Nockamixon State Park
desc: Nockamixon State Park is a Pennsylvania state park on 5,286 acres (2,139 ha) in Bedminster and Haycock Townships in northern Bucks County, Pennsylvania, in the United States. The park is one of the most popular in southeastern Pennsylvania, with most tourists visiting in the summer months.

name: Pocomoke River State Park
desc: Pocomoke River State Park is a Maryland state park lying on both banks of the Pocomoke River between Snow Hill and Pocomoke City in Worcester County, Maryland.

name: Wills Mountain State Park
desc: Wills Mountain State Park is a Maryland state park on Wills Mountain overlooking the Cumberland Narrows in Allegany County, Maryland. The park occupies 470 acres (190 ha) on the northwest edge of the City of Cumberland. It is under the control of the Maryland Department of Natural Resources.

name: Allegheny Portage Railroad National Historic Site
desc: The Allegheny Portage Railroad was the first railroad constructed through the Allegheny Mountains in central Pennsylvania.

name: Blackwater National Wildlife Refuge
desc: The Blackwater National Wildlife Refuge was established in 1933 as a waterfowl sanctuary for birds migrating along the critical migration highway called the Atlantic Flyway.

name: Chesapeake and Ohio Canal National Historical Park
desc: The Chesapeake and Ohio Canal National Historical Park, located in the District of Columbia and the state of Maryland, encompasses a canal and towpath trail extending 184.5 miles (296.9 km) along the Potomac River from the Georgetown section of Washington, D.C. to Cumberland, Maryland.

name: Eisenhower National Historic Site
desc: Eisenhower National Historic Site preserves the home and farm of Dwight D. Eisenhower, the 34th president of the United States, and its surrounding property of 690.5 acres (279.4 ha). It is primarily located in Cumberland Township, Adams County, Pennsylvania, just outside Gettysburg.

name: First State National Historical Park
desc: First State National Historical Park is a National Park Service unit which lies primarily in the state of Delaware but which extends partly into Pennsylvania in Chadds Ford.

name: Glenn Martin National Wildlife Refuge
desc: Glenn Martin National Wildlife Refuge includes the northern half of Smith Island (in Somerset County, Maryland), which lies 11 miles (18 km) west of Crisfield, Maryland, and Watts Island (in Accomack County, Virginia), which is located between the eastern shore of Virginia and Tangier Island.

name: Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad National Historical Park
desc: Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad National Historical Park is a 480-acre (190 ha) National Park Service unit in the U.S. state of Maryland. It commemorates the life of former enslaved Harriet Tubman, who became an activist in the Underground Railroad prior to the American Civil War.

name: Hopewell Furnace National Historic Site
desc: Hopewell Furnace National Historic Site in southeastern Berks County, near Elverson, Pennsylvania, is an example of an American 19th century rural iron plantation, whose operations were based around a charcoal-fired cold-blast iron blast furnace.

name: John Heinz National Wildlife Refuge
desc: The John Heinz National Wildlife Refuge at Tinicum is a 1000-acre (4.05 km2) National Wildlife Refuge in Philadelphia and Tinicum Township, Pennsylvania. Adjacent to Philadelphia International Airport, the refuge protects the largest remaining freshwater tidal marsh in Pennsylvania.

name: Mason Neck National Wildlife Refuge
desc: Elizabeth Hartwell Mason Neck National Wildlife Refuge is a National Wildlife Refuge of the United States located in Virginia. It is part of the Potomac River National Wildlife Refuge Complex. It is on Mason Neck, a peninsula in the Potomac River that forms part of the shoreline of Belmont Bay.

name: Rappahannock River Valley National Wildlife Refuge
desc: The Rappahannock River Valley National Wildlife Refuge is a National Wildlife Refuge in Warsaw, Virginia, United States that was established in 1996. It is managed by the United States Fish and Wildlife Service.

name: Valley Forge National Historical Park
desc: Valley Forge National Historical Park is the site of the third winter encampment of the Continental Army during the American Revolutionary War from December 19, 1777 to June 19, 1778. The National Park Service (NPS) preserves the site and interprets the history of the Valley Forge encampment.

name: Big Spring State Park
desc: Big Spring State Park is a 45-acre (18 ha) Pennsylvania state park in Toboyne Township, Perry County, Pennsylvania in the United States. The park is on Pennsylvania Route 274, 5.5 miles (8.9 km) southwest of New Germantown. Big Spring State Park is a hiking and picnic area.

name: Colonel Denning State Park
desc: Colonel Denning State Park is a 273-acre (110 ha) Pennsylvania state park in Lower Mifflin Township, Cumberland County, Pennsylvania in the United States. The park is in the Doubling Gap of Blue Mountain on Pennsylvania Route 233 between Newville and Landisburg.

name: Fowlers Hollow State Park
desc: Fowlers Hollow State Park is a 104-acre (42 ha) Pennsylvania state park in Toboyne Township, Perry County, Pennsylvania in the United States. The park is 0.25 miles (400 m) from Blain just off Pennsylvania Route 274.

name: Greenwood Furnace State Park
desc: Greenwood Furnace State Park is a 423-acre (171 ha) Pennsylvania state park in Jackson Township, Huntingdon County, Pennsylvania, in the United States. The park is near the historic iron making center of Greenwood Furnace.

name: Kooser State Park
desc: Kooser State Park is a 250-acre (100 ha) Pennsylvania state park in Jefferson Township, Somerset County, Pennsylvania, in the United States.

name: Memorial Lake State Park
desc: Memorial Lake State Park is a Pennsylvania state park on 230 acres (93 ha) in East Hanover Township, Lebanon County, Pennsylvania in the United States. The park is surrounded by Fort Indiantown Gap Military Reservation, headquarters of the Pennsylvania National Guard.

name: Reeds Gap State Park
desc: Reeds Gap State Park is a 220 acres (89 ha) Pennsylvania state park in Armagh Township, Mifflin County, Pennsylvania in the United States. The park is largely a wilderness area with large white pine and hemlock trees. Honey Creek flows through the park, providing a habitat for trout.

name: Warriors Path State Park
desc: Warriors Path State Park is a Pennsylvania state park on 349 acres (141 ha) in Liberty Township, Bedford County, Pennsylvania, in the United States. It is named for the Great Indian Warpath that was used by the Iroquois in war raids with the Cherokee and other tribes.

name: Whipple Dam State Park
desc: Whipple Dam State Park is a Pennsylvania state park on 256 acres (104 ha) in Jackson Township, Huntingdon County, Pennsylvania in the United States.

name: Abandoned Pennsylvania Turnpike: Sideling Hill Tunnel
desc: The longer abandoned tunnel, 6,782 ft and pitch dark in the middle, toward the eastern end of the old turnpike. No services, rough pavement, cold air pouring from the portals.

name: Adkins Arboretum
desc: 400-acre native-plant garden and preserve inside Tuckahoe State Park, with five miles of paths through meadow, bottomland forest and wetland. Best for spring wildflowers and fall color.

name: Alapocas Run State Park
desc: Wooded park above the Brandywine with an old blue-rock quarry face that is Delaware's only natural rock-climbing wall, the Northern Delaware Greenway path and the stone Blue Ball Barn.

name: American Chestnut Land Trust - North Side Trails (Double Oak Farm)
desc: Trailhead at Double Oak Farm for miles of wooded ravine trails down to Parkers Creek, an undeveloped tidal creek that runs to the Bay. A hand-pulled raft crosses the creek.

name: American Chestnut Land Trust - South Side Trails
desc: Loop trails through mature forest, old farm sites and stream valleys in the Parkers Creek Preserve, starting from the trust's south trailhead off Scientists Cliffs Road.

name: Anacostia Riverwalk Trail (Yards Park)
desc: Paved riverfront trail, 16.5 miles so far, on both banks of the Anacostia. From the boardwalk and footbridge at Yards Park it passes the Navy Yard and Kingman Island on the way north to Bladensburg.

name: Annmarie Sculpture Garden
desc: Quarter-mile paved path through 30 acres of woods lined with outdoor sculpture, including pieces on loan from the Smithsonian and National Gallery. Calm, shaded walk.

name: Antietam National Battlefield
desc: Preserved 1862 battlefield of farm lanes, rail fences and stone bridges along Antietam Creek. Walk the Cornfield and Bloody Lane trails or follow the tour road.

name: Aquia Landing Park
desc: 32-acre park with a sand beach on a point where Aquia Creek meets the Potomac. Swimming, shoreline fishing and picnic shelters; a marsh along the entrance road is good for birds.

name: Ashland Nature Center
desc: Delaware Nature Society's home base in the Red Clay Creek valley: loop trails over meadow, marsh and wooded hills, and a hilltop hawk watch staffed during fall migration.

name: Assateague Lighthouse
desc: Red-and-white striped 1867 lighthouse, 142 feet tall, on a wooded dune inside the refuge. A short loop trail climbs to its base; the tower is open for climbs in season.

name: Assateague Nature Trails (Life of the Marsh, Forest and Dunes)
desc: Three short walks inside the national seashore, each about half a mile: a marsh boardwalk on the bay, a pine forest walk and a sand trail through the dunes. Horses are common.

name: Assawoman Wildlife Area
desc: Pine woods, ponds and salt marsh on Little Assawoman Bay behind Fenwick Island, with an observation tower and small landings at Mulberry, Sassafras and Strawberry for paddling or sitting.

facts.fee: Delaware Conservation Access Pass may be required to park

name: Bacon Ridge Natural Area
desc: 1,100 acres of mature forest and wetland at the head of the South River with over 20 miles of natural-surface trails shared by hikers and mountain bikers. Lots on Bacon Ridge Road and Hawkins Road.

name: Ball's Bluff Battlefield Regional Park
desc: Wooded trails along a steep bluff above the Potomac where the 1861 battle ended, with one of the country's smallest national cemeteries in a clearing. Paths drop to the riverbank.

name: Baltimore Waterfront Promenade
desc: Continuous brick-and-boardwalk path along the harbor's edge linking Canton, Fells Point, Harbor East, the Inner Harbor and Federal Hill. Flat, traffic-free waterfront running.

name: Banshee Reeks Nature Preserve
desc: 699 acres of meadows, ponds and forest along Goose Creek with 15 miles of mown and wooded trails. Closed Mondays and Fridays; few visitors and good birding.

name: Barboursville Ruins
desc: Brick walls and columns of Governor James Barbour's mansion, designed by Thomas Jefferson and burned on Christmas Day 1884. Stabilized on the grounds of Barboursville Vineyards; open to winery visitors.

name: Battery Park, New Castle
desc: Riverfront green at the foot of colonial New Castle's cobbled streets, with a paved path running along the Delaware River and its marshes. Start of the Markell Trail.

name: Beach Plum Island Nature Preserve
desc: Undeveloped barrier spit between Delaware Bay and the Broadkill River, managed by Cape Henlopen State Park. Walk north on empty sand; surf-fishing vehicles also use the beach.

name: Bear Church Rock (Graves Mill)
desc: Follows the Rapidan and Staunton rivers past cascades and swimming holes, then climbs steeply through laurel to an open rock ledge. The side trail to the rock is unmarked; the lot is small.

name: Bears Den Overlook
desc: Jumble of rock ledges on the Appalachian Trail facing west over the Shenandoah Valley, a quarter mile from the Bears Den lodge lot. One of the most-used sunset spots in Northern Virginia.

facts.fee: Small parking fee at the Bears Den day-use lot

name: Beaver Dam Swimming Club
desc: Privately run swim club at a flooded quarry about 50 feet deep, with a rope swing, diving board and rolling log, plus two shallower pools. Open to the public in summer for paid daily admission.

name: Bellevue State Park
desc: A du Pont estate turned park above the Delaware River: a 1 1/8-mile fitness track on the former horse-training oval, a fishing pond, gardens and paved and woodland paths.

name: Ben Cardin C&D Canal Trail (Chesapeake City)
desc: Paved 1.8-mile path along the Chesapeake & Delaware Canal from Chesapeake City to the state line, where it joins Delaware's Castle Trail. Ocean-going ships pass at eye level.

name: Berkeley Springs State Park
desc: Warm mineral springs in a small town-center park that George Washington first visited in 1748. Wade in the stone-lined channels for free or book a soak in the 1815 Roman Bathhouse.

name: Betterton Beach
desc: Five-acre park where the Sassafras River meets the Bay: 300 feet of swimming beach in low-salinity water, a bathhouse, boardwalk and stone fishing jetty below an old resort town.

name: Big Devils Stairs
desc: From Gravel Springs Gap, a descent through mountain laurel to ledges on the rim of a deep, sheer-walled gorge. Narrow footing near the second overlook; the trail ends at the park boundary.

name: Big Meadows
desc: Open high-elevation meadow at mile 51 of Skyline Drive with deer at dusk, summer wildflowers and dark skies for stargazing. Byrd Visitor Center, wayside, lodge and campground are alongside.

name: Big Mountain Overlook
desc: Open ledge and stone shelter on the Tuscarora Trail at the high point of Tuscarora Mountain, reached by a gravel forest road and a short walk south of Cowans Gap.

name: Big Savage Tunnel (Great Allegheny Passage)
desc: The longest tunnel on the Great Allegheny Passage, lit inside, with a wide valley view just outside its southern portal. Closed roughly December 15 to April 10 each winter.

name: Big Slackwater (C&O Canal at McMahon's Mill)
desc: Where canal boats once left the canal for the river, the towpath now runs on a concrete walkway under limestone cliffs at the Potomac's edge. Start at the old mill and walk downstream.

name: Billy Goat Trail Section C (Carderock)
desc: 1.6-mile mostly wooded riverside trail from the Carderock Recreation Area with river views, a small waterfall and the cliffs that are the area's main climbing crag. Loop back on the towpath.

name: Bird Knob and Emerald Pond
desc: Steep rocky start from New Market Gap on US 211 to ledges over the valley, then a ridge walk to a clear spring-fed pond used as a swimming hole.

name: Black Hill Regional Park
desc: More than 2,000 acres on the wooded peninsulas of Little Seneca Lake, with over 20 miles of paved and natural trails, a visitor center above the water and canoe, kayak and rowboat rentals.

name: Black Rock Cliff (Appalachian Trail)
desc: Wide west-facing cliff with a talus field below, about a mile past Annapolis Rock on the AT and usually much quieter.

name: Black Walnut Point Natural Resources Management Area
desc: The southern tip of Tilghman Island, with the Bay on one side and the Choptank on the other. Park at the county lot and walk in; a short loop trail runs through the woods. Gate open 9 am-5 pm.

name: Blackrock Summit
desc: A level mile on the AT to a huge field of broken quartzite boulders with open views over the Shenandoah Valley, Massanutten and Trayfoot Mountain. Good at sunset with little effort.

name: Blair Limestone Company Kilns
desc: Tall bank of early-1900s lime kilns of the Blair Limestone Co. with abandoned quarries behind, on the trails of Canoe Creek State Park. Short walk from the park road; free.

name: Blockhouse Point Conservation Park
desc: More than 7 miles of forest trails leading to rock outcrops high above the C&O Canal and the Potomac, with long views up and down the valley. Site of Civil War blockhouses; rarely busy.

name: Bollman Truss Railroad Bridge
desc: The only surviving Bollman truss, a red 160-foot iron railroad bridge built in 1852 and moved in 1887 to the Little Patuxent at Savage Mill. Open to walk across.

name: Bowers Beach
desc: Small fishing town between the St. Jones and Murderkill rivers with a free public bay beach, large parking area, boat ramp and a little maritime museum.

name: Brandywine Creek State Park
desc: Former du Pont dairy farm: more than 14 miles of trails over open hilltop meadows lined with blue-gneiss stone walls, down through 190-year-old tulip poplars to the Brandywine.

name: Brandywine Park
desc: Wilmington's old riverside park along both banks of the Brandywine: mill races, stone bridges, a rose garden and a ring of cherry trees around the Josephine Fountain.

name: Breezy Point Beach & Campground
desc: Half mile of sandy Bay beach with a netted swim area, a 200-foot fishing and crabbing pier and shark-tooth hunting. County-run; open May 1 to Oct 31 only.

facts.fee: Per person: non-residents $12-$20 adults, Calvert residents $6-$10

name: Broadkill Beach
desc: Low-key Delaware Bay beach town reached through the Prime Hook marshes. Calm, shallow water and a long strand; public access is small, with only a few parking spaces.

name: Broadneck Peninsula Trail
desc: Paved 10-foot-wide path along College Parkway across the Broadneck peninsula toward Sandy Point, about 8 miles as planned. The last phases were reported open in spring 2026.

name: Brookside Gardens
desc: 50-acre public garden inside Wheaton Regional Park: two conservatories, a Japanese-style tea house on a pond, and azalea, rose and perennial gardens. Free; no dogs.

name: Buck Hollow and Marys Rock Loop
desc: The hard way up Marys Rock, from a small lot on US 211: up the Buck Hollow stream valley, on to the summit view, and down Buck Ridge on hundreds of steep log steps.

name: Bull Run Mountains Natural Area Preserve
desc: South section open Friday to Sunday only: about 7 miles of trails on the easternmost ridge of the Blue Ridge foothills, past quartzite outcrops, old home sites and cemeteries. No dogs.

name: Bull Run Regional Park (Bluebell Trail)
desc: The 1.5-mile Bluebell Trail loops through a floodplain that turns blue with Virginia bluebells in mid-April. Northern trailhead of the Bull Run-Occoquan Trail; campground.

facts.fee: $12 weekdays, $14 weekends and holidays per vehicle for non-jurisdiction residents ($8/$10 for NOVA Parks jurisdictions)

name: Bull Run-Occoquan Trail
desc: Blue-blazed 19.7-mile footpath through woods along Bull Run and the Occoquan Reservoir, from Bull Run Regional Park to Fountainhead. Rolling singletrack with creek crossings; mid access at Hemlock Overlook.

name: Burnside Bridge (Antietam)
desc: Stone arch bridge of 1836 over Antietam Creek, fought over for hours in 1862. An overlook sits above it and creekside trails loop out from the bridge.

name: Burton Island Nature Preserve
desc: Loop trail on a wooded island behind the Indian River Marina, reached by a causeway. Sand, packed earth and boardwalk with constant views over salt marsh and the inland bays.

name: Buzzard Rock (north approach)
desc: Moderate climb to a knife-edge of tilted sandstone above Passage Creek gorge, looking into Fort Valley and across to Signal Knob. Lot holds about 15 cars; roadside parking gets towed.

name: BWI Trail
desc: 12.4-mile asphalt-and-boardwalk loop that fully circles BWI Airport, passing the Dixon observation area and linking by spur to the B&A Trail and the Linthicum light rail stop. Mostly flat.

name: C&O Canal Towpath at Widewater (Angler's access)
desc: Lot opposite Old Angler's Inn puts you on the 184.5-mile towpath beside Widewater, a lake-like stretch of canal in an old river channel. Flat running north to Great Falls or south to Carderock.

name: Cacapon Resort State Park
desc: 6,115-acre park on the east slope of Cacapon Mountain with a small lake and beach, lodge and miles of ridge trails.

name: Caledon State Park
desc: National Natural Landmark of old-growth forest on the Potomac, summer home to many bald eagles. The 2-mile Boyd's Hole Trail leads to the river shore; six primitive hike-in or paddle-in campsites.

name: Caledonia State Park
desc: 1,125-acre park on US 30 around the site of Thaddeus Stevens's iron furnace: reconstructed stack, creekside trails, a swimming pool and the Appalachian Trail passing through.

name: Calvert Marine Museum & Drum Point Lighthouse
desc: An 1883 screwpile cottage lighthouse you can walk through, moved here from Drum Point, plus a fossil hall of Calvert Cliffs finds, river otters and a marsh walk.

name: Camp Michaux ruins
desc: Foundations, a stone barn wall and other remains of a secret World War II camp where German prisoners were interrogated, later a church camp. Self-guided walk in the state forest.

name: Canaan Valley National Wildlife Refuge
desc: The Canaan Valley National Wildlife Refuge (CVNWR) in Tucker County, West Virginia, was the 500th National Wildlife Refuge (NWR) to be established in the United States. The refuge preserves a moist valley with unique wetlands and uplands at a relatively high elevation in the Allegheny Mountains.

name: Canaan Valley Resort State Park
desc: State park in a high, bathtub-shaped valley of wetlands and spruce: easy meadow and boardwalk trails, deer everywhere, and a chairlift ride up to Bald Knob for the view.

name: Capital Crescent Trail
desc: Paved rail trail from the Georgetown waterfront to Bethesda: along the Potomac and canal, over the Arizona Avenue trestle, through the brick Dalecarlia Tunnel and uphill under a tree canopy.

name: Cat Rock (Cunningham Falls State Park)
desc: Steep climb from MD 77 to a pile of quartzite blocks; scramble on top for a view in every direction. Far fewer people than the national park side of the road.

name: Cathedral State Park
desc: 132 acres of old-growth hemlock right beside US 50, the largest stand of virgin timber left in West Virginia. Flat loop trails along Rhine Creek.

name: Catoctin Furnace
desc: Stone stack of an iron furnace that shut down in 1903, with the ruined ironmaster's house and a footbridge trail over US 15 into the state park's Manor Area.

name: Cedar Hill Park
desc: County marina park on the wide lower Nanticoke with a small beach, kayak launch, pavilions and swinging benches on a hill above the river. Faces west for sunset.

name: Cedar Run Falls and Natural Waterslide
desc: Steep descent from Hawksbill Gap past small pools to a smooth rock chute used as a waterslide, then a taller waterfall with a swimming hole just below. The climb back is 1,500 ft in 1.7 miles.

name: Cedarville State Forest
desc: Flat pine and holly forest at the headwaters of Zekiah Swamp with 19.5 miles of marked trails, a small fishing pond, an old charcoal kiln and a seasonal campground.

name: Centennial Park
desc: Howard County's flagship park: a paved loop of about 2.6 miles circling 54-acre Centennial Lake with rolling hills, boat rentals in season, fishing and plenty of waterfowl.

name: Chapman State Park
desc: Mature hardwood forest and meadows around the Mount Aventine manor, with trails dropping to a quiet Potomac shoreline that looks across to Virginia. Few visitors.

name: Chapman's (Beverley) Mill ruins
desc: Stone shell of a five-and-a-half-story gristmill dating to 1742, squeezed between I-66 and the railroad at Thoroughfare Gap. Gutted by fire in 1998 and stabilized; grounds open on weekends.

facts.access: You can only look at this one from outside (road, trail or water). The site itself is closed or fenced.

name: Chesapeake Bay Environmental Center
desc: 510-acre marsh peninsula near Kent Narrows with miles of flat trails, observation towers and blinds, a raptor aviary and kayak launches onto Marshy Creek. Non-members pay admission.

name: Chesapeake Bay Maritime Museum
desc: Eighteen-acre waterfront campus with the 1879 Hooper Strait screwpile lighthouse, which you can walk through, a working boatyard and a floating fleet of Bay workboats.

name: Chickies Rock
desc: Quartzite cliff above the Susquehanna north of Columbia, described as the largest exposed anticline on the East Coast. A short overlook trail leads from the PA 441 lot; Breezyview Overlook is nearby.

name: Chimney Rock (Catoctin Mountain Park)
desc: Stack of quartzite ledges with an open view south over the Catoctin ridges. A steady climb from the visitor center or the Park Central Road lot; usually paired with Wolf Rock.

facts.dogs: leashed; not allowed on the rock formations

name: Chimney Rocks (Michaux State Forest)
desc: Appalachian Trail climb from Old Forge to a jagged outcrop on Buzzard Peak, looking out over the Waynesboro Reservoir and the folds of South Mountain.

name: Chincoteague National Wildlife Refuge
desc: The Chincoteague National Wildlife Refuge is a 14,000-acre (57 km2) wildlife preserve operated by the U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service.

name: Codorus State Park
desc: 3,500-acre park around 1,275-acre Lake Marburg, with boat rentals, sailing, long shoreline trails and a large swimming pool in summer.

name: Coketon Coke Ovens
desc: Long banks of stone beehive coke ovens from the Davis Coal and Coke era lining the Blackwater Canyon rail trail (USFS Trail 115) between Thomas and Douglas, near Douglas Falls. Flat grade; streams run orange with mine drainage.

name: Compton Peak (columnar jointing)
desc: AT climb from Compton Gap to a west-facing view, then a rough spur below the east viewpoint to a wall of hexagonal basalt columns, a prime example of columnar jointing.

name: Conquest Preserve
desc: 758 acres of fields, woods and shoreline between the Corsica and Chester rivers with more than four miles of trails. The sandy beach is run by the county and may need a reservation.

name: Coplay Cement Kilns (Saylor Park)
desc: Nine tall red-brick Schoefer vertical kilns built in 1892-93 for Portland cement and soon obsolete, standing in a row in a small park. Exteriors only; free.

name: Cornwall Iron Furnace
desc: The only intact charcoal blast furnace complex left in the Western Hemisphere, in blast 1742-1883, with its casting house and blowing engine. State historic site; inside by guided tour for a fee on open days.

facts.access: Open by guided tour or by arrangement only. Check before you go.

name: Cove Road Beach
desc: Small county beach on the Nanticoke River at the end of Cove Road, reached by a short ramp and a few steps. Room for a handful of cars; locals come with a blanket for sunset.

name: Cowans Gap State Park
desc: Mountain lake with a sand beach in a gap of Tuscarora Mountain, surrounded by Buchanan State Forest. Steep trails climb from the shore to ridge overlooks.

name: Cranesville Swamp Preserve
desc: Boreal bog in a frost pocket on the Maryland-West Virginia line, with plants normally found far to the north. Five short trails and a 1,500-ft boardwalk over the wettest part.

name: Cranny Crow Overlook (Lost River State Park)
desc: Rock ledge at 3,200 ft on Big Ridge with a view over five counties. The climb starts at the White Oak trailhead by the stables; a longer loop adds Cheeks Rock and the old fire tower.

name: Crescent Rock Overlook
desc: West-facing overlook at 3,550 ft looking straight at Hawksbill, the park's highest peak, with Nakedtop beside it.

name: Cromwell Valley Park
desc: Old farm valley along Minebank Run near Towson: meadow and wooded hill trails, restored 19th-century lime kilns, a fall hawk watch and paths that climb toward Loch Raven.

name: Cross Island Trail
desc: Paved 6.5-mile trail across Kent Island from Terrapin Nature Park to Kent Narrows, over creeks and marsh on wooden bridges and through pine woods.

name: Crow's Nest Natural Area Preserve
desc: 3,344 acres of mature hardwood forest on a ridge between Accokeek and Potomac creeks. Raven Road lot (18 cars, Thu-Sun) reaches 9+ miles of trails; Brooke Road access is open daily with a kayak launch.

name: Curtis Creek Ship Graveyard
desc: Rotting hulls of wooden ships left along Curtis Creek beside the I-695 bridge, including World War I-era vessels and the schooner William T. Parker. Seen only from the water; paddle in by kayak.

facts.access: You can only look at this one from outside (road, trail or water). The site itself is closed or fenced.

name: Cushwa Basin and Conococheague Aqueduct
desc: Canal hub at Williamsport: a re-watered stone aqueduct, turning basin, lift lock and warehouse visitor center within a short walk on the towpath.

name: Cylburn Arboretum
desc: City arboretum on a wooded estate above the Jones Falls: formal gardens and tree collections around a stone mansion begun in 1863, with woodland trails beyond. Free; closed Mondays.

name: Dan's Rock Overlook
desc: Painted rock outcrop at 2,895 ft, the highest point in Allegany County, with a long view east over the Potomac valley. A paved road goes to the top.

name: Dark Hollow Falls
desc: Short, steep, rocky descent beside Hogcamp Branch to a 70-foot stepped cascade near Big Meadows. The park's most-walked waterfall trail; go early or late to avoid crowds.

name: Deal Island Wildlife Management Area
desc: Thousands of acres of tidal marsh with a big impoundment circled by a flat dike trail of more than seven miles. Herons, ibis and waterfowl in every season; no shade.

name: Deep Creek Lake State Park
desc: Public beach, boat launch and discovery center on the northeast shore of Maryland's big mountain reservoir, with trails climbing Meadow Mountain behind.

facts.fee: $3-5 per person in season; $3 per vehicle MD residents off-season

name: Deer Creek at Rocks State Park
desc: Three and a half miles of Deer Creek run through the park, with picnic areas on the bank used for wading, tubing and swimming holes, and stocked trout in spring.

name: Delaware Botanic Gardens at Pepper Creek
desc: Young public garden on Pepper Creek with a two-acre meadow designed by Piet Oudolf, woodland paths down to the tidal creek and an inland-dune garden. Seasonal hours.

name: Delaware Seashore State Park - Tower Road
desc: Guarded ocean beach south of Dewey beside a WWII observation tower. Cross the highway to the bay side for calm, shallow water, kayak launching and sunset over Rehoboth Bay.

name: Devil's Den (Gettysburg)
desc: Hill of house-sized boulders with passages and crevices to climb through, used by sharpshooters on the second day of the battle. Faces Little Round Top across the valley.

name: Difficult Run
desc: Trail follows a rocky stream past cascades and pools for about a mile to its mouth in Mather Gorge. Climb to the Ridge Trail in Great Falls Park to make a loop. Roadside lot on Georgetown Pike.

name: Douglas Falls
desc: Broad fall on the North Fork of the Blackwater pouring over ledges stained orange by old mine drainage, below Thomas on the Blackwater Canyon rail trail, past rows of coke ovens.

name: Doyles River Falls
desc: Trail from mile 81.1 follows a clear stream down to the upper and lower Doyles River Falls. Link it with Jones Run Falls from Browns Gap for a 6.5-mile three-waterfall circuit.

name: Druid Hill Park
desc: 745-acre park opened in 1860 with Druid Lake, wooded northern trails, the Rawlings Conservatory, the Moorish Tower and the Maryland Zoo. The Jones Falls Trail passes through it.

name: Dumbarton Oaks Gardens
desc: Terraced formal gardens by Beatrix Farrand on a Georgetown hillside: rose garden, pebble mosaic pool, orchard and cherry hill. Open Tue-Sun afternoons from 2 pm; tickets sold online in season.

name: Dumbarton Oaks Park
desc: 27-acre 'wild garden' laid out by Beatrix Farrand below the Dumbarton Oaks estate: a stream stepped with small stone dams, meadows and old stonework. Enter by Lovers' Lane off R Street.

name: Duncan Knob
desc: Short, steep hike ending in a scramble up a pile of sandstone blocks to a pointed summit with views of the valley and New Market Gap. Crisman Hollow Road is often gated in winter and spring.

name: DuPont Nature Center at Mispillion Harbor
desc: Deck over the harbor mouth where, each May, thousands of red knots and other shorebirds feed on horseshoe crab eggs. Free state center with scopes and live cameras; open seasonally.

name: Dyke Marsh Wildlife Preserve
desc: Flat Haul Road trail and boardwalk lead about three-quarters of a mile into a freshwater tidal marsh on the Potomac. Ospreys, eagles and marsh wrens; park at Belle Haven and walk south.

name: Elakala Falls
desc: First of four falls on Shays Run as it tumbles into Blackwater Canyon, a few minutes from the lodge with a footbridge across its lip. The lower falls need a steep scramble.

name: Elizabeth Furnace
desc: Stone stack of a 19th-century blast furnace and a restored cabin in George Washington National Forest, with short interpretive loops from the picnic area on VA-678; the old pig-iron road is now the trail up Massanutten. Free.

name: Elizabeth Furnace Recreation Area
desc: Picnic area and campground on Passage Creek with the stone stack of an 1836 iron furnace, short Pig Iron and Charcoal interpretive trails, a swinging bridge and stocked trout water.

name: Elk Neck State Park - North East Beach
desc: Sandy freshwater-tidal swimming beach on the North East River side of the Elk Neck peninsula, with picnic shelters, grills and wooded trails nearby. State park day-use fee.

name: Elliott Island Road (Fishing Bay marshes)
desc: Dead-end road running nearly 20 miles from Vienna across the vast Fishing Bay marsh to the hamlet of Elliott. Almost no buildings, open horizon, famous among birders. It can flood at high tide.

name: Elliott Knob via Falls Hollow
desc: Climb past the cascades of Falls Hollow, then a steep, shadeless gravel road to a grassy 4,463-ft summit with an old fire tower. About 162 miles from Pasadena, at the edge of range.

name: Elms Beach Park
desc: County beach on the open Chesapeake south of Lexington Park: a long sandy shoreline with unsupervised swimming, fishing, crabbing and picnic tables under the pines.

facts.fee: Weekends and holidays: $7 county residents, $25 out-of-county

name: Enchanted Forest at Clark's Elioak Farm
desc: Storybook houses and figures rescued from the Enchanted Forest park on US-40, which closed in 1989 and sat rotting behind a fence; restored from 2005 on and set out on a farm. Paid admission ($8-13 in fall 2026), seasonal.

facts.access: Open by guided tour or by arrangement only. Check before you go.

name: Featherstone National Wildlife Refuge
desc: The Featherstone National Wildlife Refuge is a National Wildlife Refuge located along the Potomac River in Virginia, at the point where it meets Neabsco Creek.

name: Federal Hill Park
desc: Grassy hilltop on the south side of the Inner Harbor with the classic postcard view of the downtown skyline and harbor. Short climb from Key Highway; best near dusk.

name: Fenwick Island State Park
desc: Three miles of undeveloped barrier beach between Bethany and Fenwick, with a guarded swimming area and bay-side access to Little Assawoman Bay for kayaks.

name: Ferry Park (Rock Hall Beach)
desc: Small public swimming beach and gazebo on Beach Road looking west across the widest part of the upper Bay toward the Western Shore. Known locally for sunsets.

name: Ferry Point Park
desc: Marsh peninsula at Kent Narrows: a one-mile unpaved trail from the Chesapeake Heritage and Visitor Center ends at a shallow, sandy cove on the Chester River.

name: First State National Historical Park - Beaver Valley
desc: About 1,100 acres of rolling woods, pasture and old farm lanes along the Brandywine on the Delaware-Pennsylvania line, with a web of unmarked but well-worn trails. No entrance fee.

name: Fletcher's Cove
desc: Boathouse on a Potomac cove between the C&O towpath and the Capital Crescent Trail. Rowboat, canoe and kayak rentals in season, spring shad fishing and picnic tables under sycamores.

name: Forks of Red Creek (Dolly Sods Wilderness)
desc: Loop from the Blackbird Knob trailhead down to where the forks of Red Creek meet in a run of small waterfalls and swimming holes, with campsites beside the water.

name: Fort Armistead Park
desc: Graffiti-covered concrete gun batteries of a coastal fort active 1901-1920 on Hawkins Point, with a fishing pier and boat ramp on the Patapsco beside the Key Bridge site. Unmaintained; go in daylight.

name: Fort Carroll
desc: Hexagonal artificial-island fort in the middle of the Patapsco, abandoned and overgrown, with an 1898 lighthouse. Private; landing is trespassing. View it from the shore at Fort Armistead Park or from a boat.

facts.access: You can only look at this one from outside (road, trail or water). The site itself is closed or fenced.

name: Fort DuPont
desc: Coast-defense post that guarded the Delaware River from 1900 to 1942: overgrown concrete gun batteries and old Army buildings along a riverside trail in Fort DuPont State Park. Free; parts of the post are being redeveloped.

name: Fort Frederick State Park
desc: Massive stone fort from the French and Indian War with restored walls and barracks, beside the Potomac, the C&O Canal and Big Pool.

facts.fee: $3 per vehicle MD residents, $5 out of state

name: Fort Howard Park
desc: Tip of the North Point peninsula where the Patapsco meets the Bay. Walk through Spanish-American War-era concrete gun batteries half taken back by woods, then out to a pier and shoreline picnic spots.

name: Fort Mifflin
desc: Stone-and-brick fort on Mud Island, besieged in 1777, with casemates, magazines and a torpedo casemate, right under the airport flight path. Run by a nonprofit; paid admission on open days.

facts.access: Open by guided tour or by arrangement only. Check before you go.

name: Fort Miles and Observation Tower 7
desc: WWII coastal defense fort inside Cape Henlopen: a gun battery buried in the Great Dune, big guns on display and a 75-foot concrete fire-control tower you can climb for a bay-and-ocean view.

name: Fort Washington
desc: Intact early-1800s masonry river fort with a dry moat, surrounded by abandoned concrete gun batteries (Decatur, Emory, White, Humphries and more) scattered through the woods and along the Potomac. NPS park; entry fee.

name: Fort Washington Park
desc: Intact masonry fort completed in 1824 on a bluff over the Potomac, with a small light at the point, shoreline fishing and a riverside trail. Views upriver toward Alexandria and DC.

name: Fountainhead Regional Park
desc: 2,000 wooded acres on the Occoquan Reservoir with kayak, paddleboard and jon-boat rentals, a fishing pier and the southern trailhead of the Bull Run-Occoquan Trail. Separate mountain-bike loops.

name: Frick's Lock Village
desc: Canal village emptied in the late 1900s next to the Limerick nuclear plant; eleven historic buildings now belong to East Coventry Township. Fenced; the township runs free tours part of the year, otherwise look from the road.

facts.access: Open by guided tour or by arrangement only. Check before you go.

name: Fridley Gap
desc: Loop in the southern Massanutten with stream crossings, two ridge climbs, a vista over the Harrisonburg valley and a deep swimming hole about halfway. Some sections are overgrown.

name: Fuller Lake (Pine Grove Furnace State Park)
desc: Small, cold, clear lake filling the old iron-ore pit of Pine Grove Furnace, with a sand beach a short walk from the furnace stack, the general store and the AT.

name: Furnace Town and the Paul Leifer Nature Trail
desc: A 35-foot brick iron furnace from the 1830s stands in the forest beside a rebuilt village. The one-mile Paul Leifer Trail starts here and runs on boardwalk into the cypress swamp.

name: G. Richard Thompson WMA Trillium Trail
desc: Upper slopes of the Blue Ridge carpeted with large-flowered trillium in spring, crossed by the Appalachian Trail. Visitors need a Virginia hunting or fishing license or a DWR access permit.

facts.fee: DWR access permit or VA hunting/fishing license required

name: George Washington National Forest
desc: The George Washington and Jefferson National Forests is an administrative entity combining two U.S. National Forests into one of the largest areas of public land in the Eastern United States.

name: Gifford Pinchot State Park
desc: 2,338-acre park around Pinchot Lake with a lake swimming beach, boat rentals and trails through fields of rounded diabase boulders.

name: Glendening Nature Preserve
