desc: Part of Jug Bay: sandy pine-barrens trails, meadows and riverside forest down to the Patuxent marshes, with entrances on Wrighton Road and Plummer Lane. The marsh boardwalk was closed in 2026.

name: Glenstone
desc: Art museum spread over nearly 300 acres of meadow and woodland, with outdoor sculpture and walking paths between pavilions. Always free, but visits must be scheduled online in advance.

name: Government Island
desc: Boardwalk across marsh to a wooded island quarry that supplied Aquia sandstone for the White House and Capitol in the 1790s. Cut marks remain in the rock faces along the 1.5-mile trail.

name: Government Island Quarry
desc: Island quarry that supplied the Aquia sandstone for the White House and US Capitol; cut faces and tool marks remain. County park since 2010 with 1.5 mi of trail and boardwalk across the marsh. Free.

name: Governor Dick Observation Tower
desc: Concrete tower on a wooded hilltop; climb the ladders inside to a caged platform above the trees with views over several counties. Reached by forest trails from the nature center.

name: Grand Caverns
desc: America's oldest show cave, giving tours since 1806. A National Natural Landmark for its rare shield formations; the tall main rooms carry signatures left by Civil War soldiers.

name: Gravelly Point
desc: Open lawn a few hundred feet from the north end of National Airport's main runway; jets pass low overhead. The Mount Vernon Trail runs through. Reached from the northbound parkway only.

name: Great Allegheny Passage: Brush Tunnel
desc: The rail trail climbs out of Cumberland through the Narrows, past the Cumberland Bone Cave, then through the 914-ft Brush Tunnel, which it shares with a steam tourist train.

name: Greenbrier State Park
desc: 42-acre lake under South Mountain with a long sand swimming beach, boat rentals and trails that link to the AT. Summer weekends need a day-use reservation.

facts.fee: $3-5 per person in summer for MD residents (+$2 out of state); $3 per vehicle off-season; reservation required weekends and holidays Memorial Day-Labor Day

name: Greenbury Point Conservation Area
desc: Navy-owned peninsula at the Severn River mouth with flat nature trails, three old radio towers and wide views of the Bay and Annapolis. Closed without notice when the range is in use (red light flashing).

name: Greenwell State Park
desc: 596 acres of farm fields and woods on the Patuxent with about 10 miles of trails, a small sandy swimming beach, a fishing pier and a kayak launch below the old Rosedale manor.

name: Grist Mill Trail
in: Patapsco Valley State Park Glen Artney Area
desc: Paved, nearly flat riverside trail up the Patapsco gorge from Lost Lake past the swinging bridge and the former Bloede Dam site to Ilchester. About 2.5 miles one way, closed to cars.

name: Gunpowder Falls State Park - Hammerman Area
desc: 1,500 feet of guarded swimming beach on the tidal Gunpowder River with picnic groves, kayak and paddleboard rentals and the Dundee Creek marina next door. Entry fee in season.

name: Gunpowder Falls State Park - Sweet Air Area
desc: 1,250 acres of farm fields, pine plantations and woods on the Little Gunpowder with a web of quiet trails, river fords and Barley Pond. Shared with horses; the lot is at the end of Dalton Bevard Road.

name: Gwynns Falls/Leakin Park
desc: 1,216 acres of wooded stream valley in west Baltimore: miles of dirt trails along the Gwynns Falls and Dead Run, the old Crimea estate and the Carrie Murray Nature Center.

name: Hagley Museum (du Pont powder yards)
desc: 235 acres along the Brandywine where the DuPont company began in 1802: stone gunpowder mills open to the river, a working water wheel and the family's first home and garden.

name: Hagley Powder Yards
desc: Stone roll mills, races and ruins of the du Pont black powder works that ran along the Brandywine from 1802 to 1921. A museum property since 1957; paid admission.

facts.access: Open by guided tour or by arrangement only. Check before you go.

name: Hains Point loop (East Potomac Park)
desc: Flat paved loop on Ohio Drive around the tip of East Potomac Park, with the Potomac on one side and Washington Channel on the other. Planes land across the river; cherry trees line the road.

name: Halfmoon Lookout
desc: Loop up Halfmoon Mountain to a rocky point with the stone base of an old fire lookout and a sweeping view down Trout Run Valley.

name: Harpers Ferry National Historical Park
desc: Harpers Ferry National Historical Park, originally Harpers Ferry National Monument, is located at the confluence of the Potomac and Shenandoah rivers in and around Harpers Ferry, West Virginia.

name: Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad State Park
desc: Visitor center and short paths set in the marsh and farm country where Harriet Tubman was enslaved and later led people north. The landscape around it has changed little.

name: Hart-Miller Island State Park
desc: Man-made island off the mouth of Back River reached only by boat. The western shore has a 3,000-foot sandy beach with wade-in anchoring; open May through September.

name: Hashawha Environmental Center and Bear Branch Nature Center
desc: 320-acre county environmental campus north of Westminster with five miles of loop trails through woods, meadows and wetlands, Lake Hashawha, a raptor mews and a nature center.

name: Havre de Grace Promenade and Concord Point Lighthouse
desc: Boardwalk of about three-quarters of a mile along the shore where the Susquehanna opens into the Bay, from Tydings Park to the 1827 Concord Point Lighthouse.

name: Hawk Rock (Duncannon)
desc: Steep Appalachian Trail climb up stone steps on Cove Mountain to a ledge over Duncannon and the meeting of the Juniata and Susquehanna rivers.

name: Hazel River Falls and Cave
desc: From Meadow Spring parking (mile 33.5), Hazel Mountain and White Rocks trails lead to a steep side path down to a small waterfall with a rock-shelter cave beside its pool.

name: Hemlock Gorge
desc: Narrow ravine on the upper Gunpowder above Prettyboy Reservoir lined with old hemlocks, rock ledges and deep pools, more like the mountains than Baltimore County. Footpath from Gunpowder Road.

name: Herrington Manor State Park
desc: 53-acre Herrington Lake with a sand beach, boat rentals and log cabins, ringed by pine forest a few miles from Swallow Falls.

facts.fee: $3 per person MD residents, $5 out of state in summer and on weekends; $3 per vehicle off-season

name: High Knob Fire Tower
desc: Short climb from US 33 at the state line to a stone fire tower built in 1939-40 on Shenandoah Mountain, with a platform view west to Spruce Knob and east to the Blue Ridge.

name: Highpoint Scenic Vista
desc: Bald grass hilltop with a paved path spiraling to the summit and a full-circle view of the Susquehanna and the Wrightsville bridges.

name: Historic London Town and Gardens
desc: Site of a colonial port town on the South River: the 1760s William Brown House, reconstructed buildings and woodland and ornamental gardens stepping down to the water. Admission charged.

name: Historic St. Mary's City
desc: Outdoor museum on the site of Maryland's 1634 capital: rebuilt State House, a tall-ship replica, a tobacco plantation and miles of footpaths along the St. Mary's River.

name: Hogback Overlook
desc: The longest overlook on Skyline Drive (0.2 mile), facing north at 3,385 ft over Gimlet Ridge and Browntown Valley; the Alleghenies show on clear days.

name: Holts Landing State Park
desc: Small, uncrowded park on the south shore of Indian River Bay with a crabbing pier, a bayshore beach, a boat ramp and the 1.3-mile Sea Hawk Trail through woods and meadow.

name: Hopewell Furnace
desc: Restored iron-making village that went cold in 1883: furnace stack with water wheel, charcoal house, ironmaster's mansion and workers' houses. National historic site beside French Creek State Park; free.

name: Hoye-Crest (Maryland high point)
desc: Maryland's highest point, 3,360 ft on Backbone Mountain, reached only from West Virginia: a steep mile up an old road from roadside parking on US 219 to a cairn, mailbox and view east.

name: Hunting Creek Lake (Cunningham Falls State Park)
desc: 43-acre mountain lake with sand swimming beaches, boat rentals and picnic lawns, in the William Houck Area. The trail to Cunningham Falls starts from the beach lot.

facts.fee: $3-5 per person in season for MD residents (+$2 out of state); $3 per vehicle off-season

name: Indian Echo Caverns
desc: Limestone show cave in a bluff above Swatara Creek near Hershey, open daily for guided tours.

name: Indian Head Rail Trail
desc: 13 miles of flat, paved trail on a former Navy rail line between White Plains and Indian Head, passing through the Mattawoman Creek wetlands with almost no road crossings.

name: Indian River Inlet
desc: Rock jetties where Indian River Bay pours into the Atlantic under a cable-stayed bridge with a walkway. Surfers on the north side, anglers on the rocks, guarded beaches on both sides.

name: Jack A. Markell Trail
desc: Paved 5.5-mile trail from the Wilmington Riverfront to New Castle's Battery Park, starting on a long boardwalk over the Peterson wildlife refuge marsh and a bridge over the Christina.

name: James Farm Ecological Preserve
desc: County preserve on Indian River Bay run by the Center for the Inland Bays: two-plus miles of trails through forest, meadow and marsh to a sandy bay beach half a mile from the lot.

name: Jefferson Patterson Park & Museum
desc: 560 acres of fields and woods on the Patuxent with shoreline trails, a recreated Woodland Indian village and the site of the 1814 Battle of St. Leonard Creek. State archaeology park.

name: Jefferson Rock
desc: Shale slabs on the Appalachian Trail above Lower Town looking down the Shenandoah to the water gap, the view Thomas Jefferson praised. Short climb up stone steps past church ruins.

facts.fee: $20 per vehicle or $10 per person, valid 3 days

name: Jerusalem Mill Village and Jericho Covered Bridge
in: Gunpowder Falls State Park Jerusalem Mill Area
desc: Restored 18th-century Quaker mill village on the Little Gunpowder, now Gunpowder Falls State Park headquarters, with a 1772 grist mill, a blacksmith shop and trails to the 1865 Jericho Covered Bridge.

name: Jewell Hollow Overlook
desc: Faces north-northwest at 3,320 ft where the Blue Ridge drops into Page Valley past Leading Ridge; Morning Star Lake is visible below. The Appalachian Trail runs just below it.

name: Jonas Green Park
desc: Small park under the Naval Academy Bridge on the Severn River: a strip of sand, a fishing pier on the old bridge abutment, a cartop launch and views of the Academy. Southern end of the B&A Trail.

name: Jones Point Park
desc: 1856 river lighthouse at the tip of Alexandria, with the 1791 south cornerstone of the District of Columbia set in the seawall below it. Fishing piers and lawns under the Wilson Bridge.

name: Junction & Breakwater Trail
desc: Six-mile crushed-stone rail-trail between Lewes and Rehoboth Beach through woods, farm fields and over an old railroad bridge across the Holland Glade marsh.

name: Kelly's Run Nature Preserve
desc: Steep loop into a boulder-filled ravine with several stream crossings, on a national recreation trail that doubles as the Conestoga Trail.

name: Kendall Trail (Youghiogheny River)
desc: 1890s railroad grade heading upstream along the wild Youghiogheny to the site of the logging town of Kendall, with many places to reach the river and swim. Water rises fast on dam-release days.

name: Kenilworth Park & Aquatic Gardens
desc: Ponds of lotus and water lilies (peak bloom late June to July) beside the Anacostia, with a boardwalk and river trail into one of the city's last tidal marshes. Herons, turtles, beavers.

name: Kennedy Peak
desc: Ridge walk on the Massanutten Trail to a small stone-and-timber lookout shelter with a 360-degree view of Page Valley, the bends of the South Fork and the Blue Ridge. No water on route.

name: Killens Pond State Park
desc: A 66-acre millpond on the Murderkill River ringed by the 2.6-mile Pondside Trail through hardwood forest. Canoe rentals, campground and a summer water park.

name: Kings Gap Environmental Education Center
desc: Stone mansion on top of South Mountain with a terrace view over the Cumberland Valley, a walled garden, and quiet trails across 2,531 acres of oak and pine.

name: Kings Landing Park
desc: 260-acre county park on the Patuxent River and Cocktown Creek with a long fishing pier, marsh boardwalk, wooded trails and a kayak launch. Quiet on weekdays.

name: Lake Anna State Park
desc: Sandy swimming beach on Lake Anna (in season), shoreline trails, a fishing pier and the site of the Goodwin Gold Mine, where gold was found in 1829.

name: Lake Artemesia
desc: 1.35-mile paved loop around a 38-acre lake with fishing piers and gazebos, dug during Metro's Green Line construction. Connects to the Paint Branch, Indian Creek and Northeast Branch trails.

name: Lake Elkhorn
desc: 37-acre Columbia lake with a paved 2-mile loop under trees, a dam-top stretch with open views and a link to the Patuxent Branch Trail toward Savage.

name: Lake Montebello
desc: City reservoir in northeast Baltimore ringed by a flat paved loop of about 1.35 miles with separate lanes for walkers and cyclists. Connects to Herring Run Park.

name: Lake Roland
desc: Wooded park around an 1860s reservoir just north of the city line: a stone dam, boardwalk from the Falls Road light rail stop, lakeside and ridge trails, and serpentine barrens at Bare Hills.

name: Laurel Fork South Wilderness
desc: Laurel Fork South Wilderness is a U.S. Wilderness Area located in the Greenbrier Ranger District of Monongahela National Forest in West Virginia. The Wilderness protects high-elevation lands along Laurel Fork (Cheat River) and is bordered by Middle Mountain to the west.

name: Lewes Beach
desc: Town beach on Delaware Bay with small waves, lifeguards in summer and views of the ferry and the breakwater lighthouses. Metered parking in season.

facts.fee: beach free; paid parking in season

name: Lewis Falls
desc: Loop from the Big Meadows amphitheater down to a walled observation point over an 81-foot waterfall, returning on the Appalachian Trail past west-facing ledges.

name: Little Bennett Regional Park
desc: Montgomery County's largest natural area: 3,700 acres of forest, meadow and creek valley with over 25 miles of natural-surface trails, the Kingsley one-room schoolhouse, Hyattstown Mill and a campground.

name: Little Devils Stairs
desc: A steep, rocky gorge trail that climbs beside Keyser Run between sheer walls, crossing the stream repeatedly, with a return on a fire road past the Bolen family cemetery.

name: Little Round Top (Gettysburg)
desc: Rocky hill at the Union left flank with paths among boulders and monuments and the widest view over the battlefield, west toward South Mountain.

name: Little Stony Man Cliffs
desc: Greenstone cliffs on the Appalachian Trail north of Stony Man with a long view down to Luray and across to Massanutten. A 3.4-mile loop links them to Stony Man via the Passamaquoddy Trail.

name: Lock 12 Historic Area
desc: Intact stone lock of the Susquehanna and Tidewater Canal with lime kilns and sawmill ruins, in a shady picnic grove below Holtwood Dam.

name: Lock Ridge Furnace Park
desc: Stone arches, walls and stacks of the Lock Ridge Iron Works, left as landscaped ruins in a 59-acre county park opened in 1976. Paved paths run through the furnace complex; free.

name: Long Pine Run Reservoir
desc: Quiet reservoir ringed by pine and oak in Michaux State Forest, with a boat launch. Popular for paddling, fishing and walks along the shore.

name: Long Wharf Park and Choptank River Lighthouse
desc: Cambridge's waterfront green on the broad Choptank, with a replica six-sided screwpile lighthouse at the end of the pier holding a small free museum. The skipjack Nathan docks here.

name: Lostland Run Trail (Potomac State Forest)
desc: Trail following Lostland Run down to the North Branch Potomac, passing Cascade Falls, a swinging bridge and a rock overlook of the river. Reached on gravel forest roads.

name: Loudoun Heights and Split Rock
desc: Cross the Shenandoah on the AT and climb the Blue Ridge to Split Rock, a ledge looking straight at Harpers Ferry and Maryland Heights. Quieter than its neighbor across the river.

facts.fee: $20 per vehicle or $10 per person, valid 3 days

name: Lower Susquehanna Heritage Greenway Trail
desc: Flat crushed-stone path on an old rail bed along the Susquehanna from Stafford Road at Deer Creek to Conowingo Dam, past the Stafford flint furnace. About 2.2 miles each way.

name: Lower Whiteoak Falls (boundary trailhead)
desc: Easy walk from the park-boundary lot near Syria to the base of the lower falls, with deep pools along the creek that fill with swimmers in summer. The park entrance fee still applies.

name: Lums Pond State Park
desc: The largest freshwater pond in Delaware, circled by the 6.4-mile Swamp Forest Trail through hardwood wetland. Boat rentals, fishing and a campground; no swimming.

name: Ma & Pa Heritage Trail
desc: Rail trail on the old Maryland & Pennsylvania Railroad bed through Bel Air and Forest Hill, 6.25 miles in sections, with paved and fine-gravel surfaces and wooded stretches.

name: Manassas National Battlefield Park
desc: Open rolling fields and woods preserved from two Civil War battles. The 5.4-mile First Manassas loop runs from Henry Hill past the Stone Bridge and Stone House; wide skies at sunset.

name: Marshy Point Nature Center
desc: County nature center on Dundee and Saltpeter creeks with easy trails through upland woods to tidal marsh, a pier and canoe launch, and live animal exhibits. Good for ospreys and winter ducks.

name: Maryland World War II Memorial Overlook
desc: Open-air granite memorial on a hillside on Route 450 just north of the Naval Academy Bridge. The whole Naval Academy, the State House dome and the Annapolis skyline lie across the Severn. Free parking.

name: Masonville Cove
desc: Reclaimed industrial shoreline on the Patapsco in south Baltimore, now an urban wildlife refuge partnership: walking trails, a fishing pier, kayak access and an education center. Bald eagles are regulars.

name: Matapeake Clubhouse & Beach
desc: Public swimming beach on the Bay below the old ferry clubhouse, with a Bay Bridge view, a mile of wooded trail and a separate dog beach.

facts.fee: No entry fee; county parking fee or permit may apply (sources differ)

name: Matoaka Beach
desc: Privately owned Bay beach below the Calvert Cliffs that sells day access: a quiet stretch of sand known for Miocene shells and shark teeth. Cash only; call ahead, it closes at capacity.

name: Maxwell Hall Park
desc: About 14 miles of trails for hikers and horses across fields and woods above the Patuxent, with paths that drop to a sandy river beach near Benedict.

name: Mayo Beach Park
desc: Sandy beach where the South River meets the Bay, with shallow wading water, shaded picnic tables and a cartop launch. Free, but a managed-access park: summer weekends and holidays need a free reservation pass.

facts.fee: free; reservation pass on summer weekends

name: Meadowlark Botanical Gardens
desc: 95 acres of gardens around three lakes, including a Korean Bell Garden with a carved pavilion and bronze bell, native plant collections and paved loop paths. Dogs only on the outer Perimeter Trail.

name: Menokin
desc: Partly collapsed stone house of Declaration signer Francis Lightfoot Lee, being rebuilt with glass in place of the missing walls; its original woodwork is shown in the visitor center. Check menokin.org for hours and tours.

name: Michael Castle C&D Canal Trail
desc: Paved 12.4-mile trail along the north bank of the Chesapeake & Delaware Canal from Delaware City to the Maryland line, under several high bridges with ships passing beside you.

name: Middle Creek Wildlife Management Area
desc: 6,000 acres of lakes and fields managed by the Game Commission. In late winter the main lake can hold up to 200,000 migrating snow geese; a driving loop and trails cover the rest of the year.

name: Middle Patuxent Environmental Area
desc: 1,021 acres of forest, meadow and river floodplain between Columbia and Clarksville with over 5 miles of quiet natural trails, including the Wildlife Loop and South Wind trails. Park on Trotter Road.

name: Monocacy Aqueduct
desc: Seven-arch stone aqueduct that carries the canal towpath across the mouth of the Monocacy River, the largest of the canal's 11 aqueducts. Boat ramp, picnic tables and flat towpath walking.

name: Mount Calvert Historical and Archaeological Park
desc: 1780s brick house on a bluff where Western Branch meets the Patuxent, on the site of colonial Charles Town. The lawn gives a wide view over the marshes; grounds open daily 8 to sunset.

name: Mount Moriah Cemetery
desc: Huge Victorian cemetery of 1855 that fell into abandonment and is being cleared by volunteers: mausoleums and monuments in young forest, and a crumbling brownstone gatehouse on Kingsessing Ave. Open in daylight; stay in cleared sections.

name: Mt. Cuba Center
desc: Botanic garden devoted to native plants of the Piedmont, with woodland paths, ponds and meadow on a former du Pont estate. Known for spring trilliums. Open seasonally.

name: Myrtle Point Park
desc: Wooded peninsula on the Patuxent across from Solomons with easy trails leading to several small sandy beaches. Unsupervised swimming, fishing and crabbing.

facts.fee: Weekends and holidays: $7 county residents, $25 out-of-county

name: Nanjemoy WMA - Purse Area (former Purse State Park)
desc: A quarter-mile path from a roadside pull-off on MD 224 leads to a wild Potomac beach on Wades Bay with Paleocene shark teeth in the gravel. Go at low tide; the beach floods at high water.

name: NASA Wallops Flight Facility Visitor Center
desc: Free visitor center on the road to Chincoteague with real sounding rockets on the lawn and a viewing area for launches from the island pads a few miles away. Limited open days; check hours.

name: Nassawango Iron Furnace (Furnace Town)
desc: Bog-iron furnace stack built in 1830 and cold by 1849, last relic of a company town swallowed by the Pocomoke swamp forest. Now an outdoor museum with a boardwalk trail; paid admission, open seasonally.

facts.access: Open by guided tour or by arrangement only. Check before you go.

name: National Capitol Columns
desc: Twenty-two sandstone Corinthian columns taken off the US Capitol's east portico and stood up in an open meadow at the National Arboretum. Free; walk or drive to the Ellipse Meadow during arboretum hours.

name: National Park Seminary (Forest Glen)
desc: Former girls' school whose sorority houses were built as a Japanese pagoda, Dutch windmill, Swiss chalet and castle, now restored as homes. Walk the public streets; Save Our Seminary leads tours.

facts.access: You can only look at this one from outside (road, trail or water). The site itself is closed or fenced.

name: Natural Chimneys
desc: Seven limestone towers 65 to 120 feet tall standing in a field beside the North River, in an Augusta County park. A 1.9-mile loop climbs behind and above them. Day use is free.

name: Neabsco Creek Boardwalk
desc: Three-quarter-mile boardwalk across the tidal marsh of Neabsco Creek with a two-story observation deck. Part of the Potomac Heritage Trail, linking Rippon Lodge and the Metz Wetlands.

name: New Germany State Park
desc: Small lake in a hemlock valley with a swimming area, cabins and a web of easy forest trails that turn into ski trails in winter.

name: Newtowne Neck State Park
desc: Undeveloped 794-acre peninsula between Breton Bay, St. Clements Bay and the Potomac. Farm lanes lead to several quiet sandy beaches and soft kayak launches.

name: Nicholson Hollow and Corbin Cabin
desc: Dog-friendly alternative from the Old Rag lot: follow the Hughes River upstream past deep swimming holes and several crossings to Corbin Cabin, an early-1900s mountain homestead.

name: No. 9 Trolley Line Trail
desc: Paved path on an old streetcar line that drops from Catonsville through a deep rock cut on a boardwalk to Oella, ending a short walk from Ellicott City's Main Street.

name: North Beach Boardwalk and Beach
desc: Seven-block Bay boardwalk with a fishing pier and a small town beach. Walking the boardwalk is free; the sand has a daily fee in season that is far higher for visitors from outside Calvert County.

facts.fee: Boardwalk free; beach about $17-$25 per adult for out-of-county visitors in season

name: Northwest Branch gorge (Burnt Mills)
desc: Below the old dam at Colesville Road the Northwest Branch drops over a waterfall into a boulder-filled gorge. A rough, rocky trail on the Rachel Carson Greenway follows the cascades downstream.

name: Occoquan Bay National Wildlife Refuge
desc: Grassland and tidal marsh where the Occoquan meets the Potomac. About 4 miles of flat gravel roads on foot plus a 2-mile wildlife drive; eagles, ospreys and meadow birds. No pets inside the gates.

name: Ocean City Inlet and Boardwalk
desc: South end of the nearly three-mile boardwalk, where the inlet cut by a 1933 hurricane separates Ocean City from Assateague. Wide beach, jetty fishing and boats running the inlet.

name: Old Mill Park and Rappahannock River Heritage Trail
desc: Riverside park with a canoe launch on the Rappahannock. The paved 1.6-mile Heritage Trail passes old mill sites and joins the Canal Path for a loop of a little over 3 miles around the north end of town.

name: Orange Grove Swinging Bridge
in: Patapsco Valley State Park Glen Artney Area
desc: Cable suspension footbridge over the Patapsco at the site of the Orange Grove flour mill, linking the Grist Mill Trail to the Cascade Falls trailhead. It bounces underfoot.

name: Oregon Ridge Park
desc: 1,000-acre county park on old iron-ore and marble workings: wooded ridge trails, a nature center, a grassy ski-slope overlook and a quarry lake. Swimming at the lake is no longer allowed.

name: Otter Creek and Urey Overlook
desc: Mason-Dixon Trail through a rocky hemlock glen along Otter Creek, then a climb to Urey Overlook above the Susquehanna. Rough, strenuous footing and limited parking.

name: Otter Creek Wilderness
desc: Roadless bowl between McGowan and Shavers mountains with 45 miles of unblazed trails. The 11-mile Otter Creek Trail follows the stream past cascades and deep pools, with several fords.

name: Overall Run Falls
desc: Hike from Mathews Arm into wilderness to ledges facing the park's tallest waterfall (93 ft) with Massanutten and the valley behind it. The falls shrink to a trickle in dry spells.

name: Patapsco Female Institute Historic Park
desc: Stabilized granite shell of an 1837 girls' boarding school on the hill above old Ellicott City, with Greek Revival columns open to the sky. Gated; open on limited tour days.

facts.access: Open by guided tour or by arrangement only. Check before you go.

name: Patapsco Valley State Park - Daniels Area
desc: Ghost of a mill town emptied in the late 1960s and wrecked by the 1972 flood. Flat water above Daniels Dam for paddling and fishing, and trails upriver past church ruins and abandoned cars in the woods.

name: Patapsco Valley State Park - McKeldin Area
desc: Where the North and South branches of the Patapsco meet: the Switchback and Rapids trails loop past McKeldin Falls, a wide rock ledge the South Branch pours over. Quieter than Avalon.

name: Patowmack Canal and Matildaville ruins
desc: Remains of George Washington's canal around the falls, begun in 1785: a lock chamber cut through the cliff, stone walls and the foundations of the canal town Matildaville. Inside Great Falls Park.

name: Patterson Park
desc: East Baltimore's big 19th-century park: a four-story Victorian observation pagoda, a boat lake that draws birds, War of 1812 earthworks on Hampstead Hill and loops of paved path.

name: Patuxent Research Refuge: South Tract
desc: Five miles of flat walking trails around two lakes, plus the National Wildlife Visitor Center (Wed-Sat 10 to 4). Seasonal fishing on Cash Lake; waterfowl, beavers and bald eagles.

name: Pemberton Historical Park
desc: 262 acres on the Wicomico River around the 1741 Pemberton Hall, with several miles of trails through pine woods, meadow and tidal marsh on boardwalks.

name: Pendleton Point Overlook
desc: Drive-up overlook at the deepest, widest part of Blackwater Canyon, looking across to the lodge and down to the river.

name: Pickering Creek Audubon Center
desc: 400-acre working farm and sanctuary on Pickering Creek with four miles of trails through forest, meadow and restored wetlands, viewing platforms and a creekside dock.

name: Pine Grove Furnace
desc: Stone stack of a charcoal iron furnace built about 1770, with the ironmaster's mansion, old works buildings and a water-filled ore pit now used as a swimming lake. At the Appalachian Trail midpoint; state park, free.

name: Piney Point Lighthouse Museum & Historic Park
desc: Squat 1836 Potomac lighthouse you can climb, with a pier, boardwalk and kayak launch. A captured WWII German U-boat, U-1105, lies sunk just offshore as a state dive preserve.

name: Piney Run Park
desc: 550 acres of woods and fields around a 300-acre lake: over five miles of shoreline and forest trails, boat rentals, fishing piers and a nature center. Open seasonally, with a per-vehicle fee.

name: Pinnacles Overlook
desc: South view at 3,320 ft down Hannah Run to Old Rag Mountain, with Pinnacles Ridge on the right and Hot Mountain on the left.

name: Pocomoke River State Park - Shad Landing
desc: Park on the dark, tannin-stained Pocomoke River, lined with bald cypress. Marina, canoe rentals, a pool and the short Trail of Change through the swamp forest.

name: Pocosin Mission Ruins
desc: Stone and timber remains of an Episcopal mountain mission from the early 1900s, with a small cemetery nearby. About 1 mi down the Pocosin fire road from Skyline Drive mile 59.5 (2 mi round trip). Park entry fee.

name: Pohick Bay Regional Park
desc: NOVA Parks campground and boat launch on a sheltered bay off the Potomac. Kayak, canoe and paddleboard rentals in season, eagles and ospreys overhead, wooded trails along the shore.

facts.fee: $12 weekdays, $14 weekends and holidays per vehicle for non-jurisdiction residents ($8/$10 for NOVA Parks jurisdictions)

name: Pole Steeple
desc: Short, steep trail from Railroad Bed Road to a quartzite cliff nearly 500 ft above Laurel Lake, with the whole Pine Grove Furnace valley below.

name: Port Mahon
desc: A road that runs along the very edge of Delaware Bay to a fishing pier and the pilings of a vanished oyster port. In May horseshoe crabs and migrating shorebirds crowd the shoreline.

name: Potomac Heritage Trail (Roosevelt Island to American Legion Bridge)
desc: Rough 10-mile footpath along the Virginia bank from Roosevelt Island to the American Legion Bridge. Boulder scrambles, stream crossings and small falls at Windy Run, Donaldson Run and Dead Run.

name: Potomac Power Plant and Armory Canal
desc: Pulp mill of 1888 that ran as a hydroelectric plant from 1899 to 1991, with stone and brick mill remains along the old armory canal. The building is closed; see it from the 1.5 mi Armory Canal Trail off Potomac St, ending at Dam No. 3.

facts.access: You can only look at this one from outside (road, trail or water). The site itself is closed or fenced.

name: Prime Hook National Wildlife Refuge
desc: 10,000 acres of marsh and woods on the bay. Short trails start at the visitor center, including a half-mile marsh boardwalk and a dike walk; a canoe trail follows Prime Hook Creek.

name: Prospect Peak (Panorama Overlook)
desc: Roadside pull-off on WV 9 west of Berkeley Springs looking down on the Potomac and Cacapon rivers with Maryland and Pennsylvania ridges behind. No walking needed.

name: Ramsey's Draft Wilderness
desc: Ramsey's Draft Wilderness is a designated wilderness area in the North River Ranger District of the George Washington and Jefferson National Forests of Virginia in the United States. The wilderness area was established in 1984 and comprises 6,518 acres (26.38 km2).

name: Range View Overlook
desc: Looks south at 2,810 ft down the spine of the park, from Keyser Mountain in front all the way to Old Rag and Stony Man in the distance.

name: Rapidan Camp (Hoover's retreat)
desc: Walk from Milam Gap down Mill Prong, past Big Rock Falls and three stream crossings, to President Hoover's 1929 fishing camp, where three original cabins stand at the head of the Rapidan.

name: Rausch Gap Ghost Town
desc: Once the largest coal and railroad town in St. Anthony's Wilderness (1830-1910): stone foundations, a well and a small cemetery in the woods. Roughly 3.5 mi each way on the flat Stony Valley Rail Trail from Gold Mine Rd; game lands.

name: Raven Rocks
desc: Out-and-back on the Appalachian Trail's 'Roller Coaster' from Snickers Gap: three rocky climbs and descents to a cliff just over the West Virginia line with a wide view west.

name: Red Creek Trail (Laneville trailhead)
desc: Low-elevation way into Dolly Sods that stays reachable when the forest roads are gated for winter. The trail follows Red Creek upstream past pools and fords toward the Forks and Lions Head.

name: Red Rock Wilderness Overlook Regional Park
desc: Short loop trails through woods to bluffs with views up and down the Potomac. Brick and stone ruins of a 19th-century farm (ice house, carriage house, granary) stand by the small parking lot.

name: Rehoboth Beach Boardwalk
desc: Mile-long wooden boardwalk along a wide, guarded Atlantic beach. Best early in the morning or off season, when it is a quiet oceanfront walk or run.

facts.fee: beach free; paid parking in season

name: Riley's Lock and Seneca Aqueduct
desc: The only place on the canal where a lock and an aqueduct are one structure, built of red Seneca sandstone over Seneca Creek. Flat water at the creek mouth for kayaks; aqueduct recently restored.

name: Riverbend Park
desc: Calm stretch of the Potomac above the falls with a boat launch, visitor center deck and flat riverside trail. Bluebells carpet the floodplain in April; walk downstream into Great Falls Park.

name: Roaring Plains West Wilderness
desc: The high, wet plateau just south of Dolly Sods: 6,820 acres of spruce, bog and rim-edge rock with long canyon views and far fewer people. Trails are faint and partly unmarked; carry a map and GPS track.

name: Roaring Point Park
desc: County park where the Nanticoke opens into Tangier Sound, with a sandy shoreline and the mile-long Bell Island Trail out to a wooden pier. Feels like the end of the map.

name: Robertson Mountain
desc: Old Rag's quiet neighbor: a very steep trail (about 1,700 ft in 1.5 miles) to a rocky summit looking straight across at Old Rag, with a fire-road return. No ticket needed and few people.

name: Rock Creek Park: Beach Drive (car-free section)
desc: Three sections of upper Beach Drive are closed to cars seven days a week (Broad Branch to Military Road, Picnic Grove 10 to Wise Road, West Beach Drive to the DC line), leaving a paved creekside road to run.

name: Rock Creek Park: Boulder Bridge loop
desc: 1902 arch bridge faced with rounded boulders over Rock Creek. The Valley Trail and Western Ridge Trail link it with Rapids Bridge and Pulpit Rock for wooded loops beside the creek's rapids.

name: Rock Maze (Garrett State Forest)
desc: Field of house-sized sandstone blocks split by passages wide and narrow that you can wander through. Short path from Snaggy Mountain Road, near Swallow Falls.

name: Rocky Gap State Park (Lake Habeeb)
desc: 243-acre Lake Habeeb at the foot of Evitts Mountain with three public sand beaches, boat rentals and a trail around the shore. Summer weekends need a day-use reservation.

facts.fee: $2 per vehicle to $4 per person depending on season; reservation required weekends and holidays Memorial Day-Labor Day

name: Rocky Point Beach and Park
desc: County waterfront park where Back River and Middle River meet the Bay: 300 feet of swimming beach open Memorial Day to Labor Day, a fishing pier, two boat ramps and shaded picnic groves.

name: Rohrbaugh Cliffs (Dolly Sods Wilderness)
desc: Mostly level walk through spruce, rhododendron and rocky meadows to open cliffs above the Red Creek basin, facing Lions Head across the canyon.

name: Rose River Falls Loop
desc: Loop from Fishers Gap down to a 67-foot waterfall, then along Rose River's cascades and pools and back up Hogcamp Branch near Dark Hollow Falls. Mostly in designated wilderness.

name: Round Top Cement Mill ruins
desc: Brick chimney, kilns and mine openings of a 19th-century cement works squeezed between the rail trail and the canal, a few miles west of Hancock.

name: Safe Harbor Trestle (Enola Low Grade Trail)
desc: Former railroad trestle high over the mouth of the Conestoga River, now decked for walkers and cyclists, with Safe Harbor Dam and the Susquehanna in view.

name: Saint Mary's Wilderness
desc: Saint Mary's Wilderness is a U.S. Wilderness Area in the George Washington and Jefferson National Forests. The wilderness area is located next to the Blue Ridge Parkway near the Parkway's northern terminus and consists of 9,826 acres (39.76 km2).

name: Samuel S. Lewis State Park
desc: 85-acre hilltop park on 885-ft Mt. Pisgah. Open lawns look out over the Susquehanna River valley; popular for kites, picnics and sunsets.

name: Sassafras Natural Resources Management Area
desc: More than four miles of farm-lane and woodland trails across 1,200 acres to high bluffs and a sandy beach on the Sassafras River. Bald eagles are regular.

name: Saunders-Monticello Trail
desc: Two-mile graded path from Kemper Park around Carter Mountain to Monticello's visitor center, carried across ravines on ten curving wooden boardwalks. Wheelchair-friendly grade.

name: Savage Mill Trail
desc: Level 0.8-mile path on an old rail spur beside the Little Patuxent as it drops through boulders and rapids below the historic Savage cotton mill. Starts at the Bollman bridge.

name: Seneca Quarry and stone-cutting mill ruins
desc: Roofless red-sandstone mill in the woods just west of Riley's Lock, where stone for the Smithsonian Castle was cut. Overgrown quarry faces lie behind it; the path is unmarked and brushy in summer.

name: Seneca Quarry and Stonecutting Mill
desc: Roofless red-sandstone stonecutting mill and overgrown quarry faces (quarrying ended by 1901) beside the C&O towpath, just west of Riley's Lock and the damaged Seneca Aqueduct. Unmarked paths; thick brush in summer.

name: Shenandoah Caverns
desc: Mile-long guided tour through 17 rooms, including the striped 'bacon' formations and Diamond Cascade. The only Virginia cavern with elevator access; 54 degrees year-round.

name: Shenandoah River State Park
desc: 1,619 acres along the South Fork Shenandoah with river access for tubing, paddling and fishing, wooded trails, and Cullers Overlook above a wide bend with Massanutten behind.

name: Shenks Ferry Wildflower Preserve
desc: Sheltered ravine along Grubb Run with more than 70 species of wildflowers; best from late March into May. An easy path follows the stream.

name: Shepherdstown Cement Mill Ruins (Potomac Mills)
desc: Stone mill foundations, a warehouse shell and a battery of six kilns built 1829-30 to make C&O Canal cement; closed 1901. Beside River Rd about 1 mi east of town on the Battle of Shepherdstown site. County-owned; do not climb.

name: Sherando Lake Recreation Area
desc: Sandy beach on a 25-acre spring-fed lake below the Blue Ridge Parkway, with a campground, picnic grounds and trailheads up to Torry Ridge and White Rock Falls. About 157 miles from Pasadena.

name: Sherwood Gardens
desc: Six-acre neighborhood garden in Guilford known for tens of thousands of tulips that peak in late April, followed by summer annuals. Free and open, with street parking.

name: Signal Knob
desc: Rocky loop to the north tip of Massanutten, a Civil War signal station with a view over Strasburg and the valley. Extra vistas at Buzzard Rock Overlook and Fort Valley Overlook on the way up.

name: Skyline Caverns
desc: Guided cave tour a mile south of Front Royal, close to the north entrance of Skyline Drive; known for its anthodites, rare needle-like white crystal clusters. Discovered 1937; open year-round.

name: Slaughter Beach
desc: Quiet bay town and official horseshoe crab sanctuary with a public beach, pavilion and seasonal restrooms. The Marvel Saltmarsh Preserve boardwalk is at the north end of town.

name: Smith Island (Ewell)
desc: Maryland's only inhabited island with no bridge, 45 minutes by passenger ferry from Crisfield's city dock. Three crabbing villages, marsh in every direction and a distinct island dialect.

name: Smithsonian Environmental Research Center
desc: Research campus on the Rhode River with public trails: the 1.3-mile Java History Trail loop past the Java mansion ruins and a marsh boardwalk, plus the 1735 Woodlawn house. Sign in on arrival.

name: Solomons Riverwalk
desc: Boardwalk along the Patuxent on Solomons Island with benches, a gazebo and a public pier. Faces west across the river mouth, so it is one of the better sunset walks in Calvert County.

name: South River Falls
desc: From South River Picnic Grounds (mile 62.7) the trail drops to an overlook of an 83-foot waterfall that splits into two streams; a spur continues to the base. Circuit returns by fire road and AT.

name: South River Farm Park
desc: Rustic county park on the Mayo peninsula with 3 miles of natural-surface trails through woods and fields to views of the South River and Limehouse Cove. Small lot, picnic tables, no bikes on trails.

name: Spruce Knob-Seneca Rocks National Recreation Area
desc: Spruce Knob–Seneca Rocks National Recreation Area is a national recreation area in the Monongahela National Forest of eastern West Virginia.

name: St. Ignatius Church Overlook, Chapel Point
desc: Hilltop churchyard of a parish founded in 1641, looking down the Port Tobacco River to the Potomac. One of the widest water views in Southern Maryland.

name: St. John's Episcopal Church Ruins
desc: Roofless stone walls of a church built 1851-52, used as a Civil War hospital and barracks and abandoned in 1895. On the stone-step path from Church St up toward Jefferson Rock, a few minutes above Lower Town. Do not climb the walls.

name: St. Mary's River State Park
desc: A 250-acre fishing lake ringed by a 7.5-mile wooded loop trail shared by hikers, runners and mountain bikers. No swimming; electric motors only, so it stays quiet.

name: Staple Bend Tunnel
desc: First railroad tunnel in the US: 901 ft, bored 1831-33 for the Allegheny Portage Railroad, with dressed-stone portals. Walk or bike about 2 mi each way on the old grade from the NPS trailhead near Mineral Point. Free.

name: State Arboretum of Virginia (Blandy Experimental Farm)
desc: Over 5,000 trees on a UVA research farm, including a grove of 300-plus ginkgos that turns gold in late October, a native plant trail and a 3-mile loop drive. Open dawn to dusk every day.

name: Stony Man
desc: Easy walk from near Skyland to cliffs at 4,011 ft looking west over the Shenandoah Valley and Massanutten. A big sunset view for very little effort.

name: Sugar Hollow: Blue Hole and Big Branch Falls (Moormans River)
desc: Two easy river trails from one lot: the South Fork road reaches the Blue Hole, a deep pool with a jump rock, in 1.5 miles; the North Fork trail fords the river to swimming holes and Big Branch Falls.

name: Sunset Rocks
desc: Loop from Pine Grove Furnace on the Appalachian Trail and a boulder-scramble spur along Little Rocky Ridge to a south-facing ledge, passing the AT halfway marker and the turn for Camp Michaux.

name: Susquehannock State Park (Hawk Point)
desc: Overlooks on a wooded plateau high above the Susquehanna and Conowingo Reservoir. Hawk Point looks down on river islands where bald eagles nest; Wissler Run Overlook is a short walk away.

name: Table Rock (Canaan Mountain)
desc: Flat sandstone ledge on the rim of Canaan Mountain with a huge view over the Dry Fork valley. A short, rooty trail from Canaan Loop Road, which is rough gravel.

name: The Point at Cape Henlopen
desc: The sand spit where Delaware Bay meets the ocean, with two offshore lighthouses in view. The overlook lot is always open; the tip itself closes for much of the year for nesting birds.

name: The Point Overlook
desc: West-northwest view at 3,235 ft over Powell and Grindstone mountains to the valley; a short, steep path below the wall leads to open rocks. Works well at sunset.

name: The Strand Beach, Oxford
desc: Narrow strip of town beach along The Strand in Oxford, facing the Tred Avon River and the ferry dock. Calm, shallow water and a walkable colonial-era village behind it.

name: Theodore Roosevelt Island
desc: Wooded 88-acre island in the Potomac reached by footbridge from a GW Parkway lot (northbound side only). The Swamp Trail boardwalk loops through tidal marsh; memorial plaza in the middle.

name: Thomas A. Dixon Jr. Aircraft Observation Area
desc: Lawn and playground under the approach to a BWI runway where airliners pass low overhead on landing. Sits on the BWI Trail loop, with parking off Dorsey Road.

name: Thomas Point Park
desc: Narrow spit at the mouth of the South River with open Bay views and Thomas Point Shoal Lighthouse offshore. Very limited parking: April-October you need a pre-bought daily ($8) or monthly pass.

facts.fee: $8 daily parking pass Apr-Oct, bought online

name: Thomas Viaduct
in: Patapsco Valley State Park Deep Run Area
desc: Curved eight-arch granite railroad bridge over the Patapsco, finished in 1835 and still carrying trains. Seen from the park road just inside the Avalon entrance of Patapsco Valley State Park.

facts.access: You can only look at this one from outside (road, trail or water). The site itself is closed or fenced.

name: Thousand Steps
desc: More than 1,000 stone steps laid by quarry workers in the 1930s, straight up Jacks Mountain from a US 22 pull-off to quarry ledges and views over the Juniata River.

name: Three Ridges Loop
desc: Hard Appalachian Trail and Mau-Har Trail loop from Reeds Gap: repeated ridge-top overlooks, then a rough creek valley of cascades and pools. About 156 miles from home; lot fills early.

name: Three Ridges Wilderness
desc: Three Ridges Wilderness is a U.S. Wilderness Area in the Glenwood/Pedlar Ranger District of the George Washington and Jefferson National Forests. The wilderness area is located just east of the Blue Ridge Parkway between the Tye River and Wintergreen Ski Resort.

name: Tibbet Knob
desc: The other hike from Wolf Gap: shorter, with two steep rock scrambles near the top and a wide ledge looking north and west over Trout Run Valley. Fewer people than Big Schloss.

name: Trough Creek State Park
desc: Narrow gorge with a run of oddities along one road: Balanced Rock perched on a cliff edge, Rainbow Falls, a suspension bridge and the Ice Mine, a pit that holds ice into summer.

name: Trout Pond Recreation Area (Rockcliff Lake)
desc: Forest Service lake with a sand swimming beach, next to tiny Trout Pond, West Virginia's only natural lake. Campground and trails up Long Mountain.

name: Trussum Pond
desc: Small pond a few miles from Trap Pond where the bald cypress crowd right up to the launch, so you are paddling through a swamp within a minute. Roadside ramp only.

name: Tuckahoe State Park
desc: Wooded stream-valley park with a 60-acre lake and flooded forest to paddle, plus 20 miles of hiking, biking and horse trails along Tuckahoe Creek.

name: Tucquan Glen Nature Preserve
desc: Ravine of rhododendron and hemlock where Tucquan Creek tumbles to the Susquehanna. The Conservancy lists the River Road lots as closed: hike in from Pinnacle Overlook, 4 miles round trip.

name: Tunnel Parking Overlook and Marys Rock Tunnel
desc: East view at 2,510 ft toward Sperryville between Oventop and Skinner Ridge, beside the 12-ft-8 rock tunnel blasted through Marys Rock in 1932. Drive through with headlights on.

name: Turkey Run Park
desc: Parking areas off the GW Parkway sit on a wooded bluff; steep switchbacks drop to the Potomac Heritage Trail on the riverbank. Big sycamores, spring wildflowers and little foot traffic.

name: Turner's Creek Park
desc: Bluff-top county park on a sheltered creek off the Sassafras River, with a public landing, an old granary, short trails and the Knocks Folly house. Lotus blooms fill the creek in summer.

name: U.S. Naval Academy Yard and Seawall
desc: The Academy grounds are open to walk-in visitors with government photo ID: seawall walks where the Severn meets Spa Creek, Triton Light at the point, the chapel and John Paul Jones crypt.

name: Union Canal Tunnel Park
desc: Hand-dug canal tunnel from the 1820s, counted as the oldest transportation tunnel still standing in the country, with a towpath walk beside a watered stretch of the old Union Canal.

name: Upper Pocosin Mission Ruins
desc: Walk a fire road from Skyline Drive mile 59.5, past the PATC's Pocosin Cabin, to the stone steps and collapsing frame building of an early-1900s Episcopal mission in the woods.

name: Virginius Island Cotton and Flour Mill Ruins
desc: Foundations of a four-story 1848 cotton mill, later a flour mill, given up after the 1889 flood, with arched water intakes and turbine pits. Same loop trail as the pulp mill, past the foundations of a vanished mill village.

name: Waggoner's Gap Hawk Watch
desc: Rock pile on the spine of Kittatinny Ridge, a short walk from the PA 74 summit lot, where counters tally migrating hawks and eagles from August through December.

name: Walking Dunes Trail
desc: A 2.6-mile route in Cape Henlopen linking Herring Point to the Great Dune, through pine forest that the slowly migrating "walking dunes" are burying, with a spur out to the salt marsh.

name: Washington & Old Dominion Trail
desc: 45-mile paved rail trail from Shirlington in Arlington to Purcellville in Loudoun, mostly shaded, with a gravel horse path alongside. Popular access points at Vienna, Reston and Leesburg.

name: Washington Monument State Park
desc: The first monument to George Washington, a 40-ft stone tower built by Boonsboro townspeople in 1827 on South Mountain. Climb the inside stairs for a valley view; the AT passes the base.

facts.fee: $2 per vehicle MD residents, $4 out of state

name: WB&A Trail (Anne Arundel section)
desc: Paved rail trail running 5.7 miles from Odenton to the Patuxent River, where a bridge built in 2025 joins the Prince George's section for 11.7 miles in all.

name: Western Maryland Rail Trail
desc: 28 miles of paved rail trail between Fort Frederick and Little Orleans, shadowing the C&O Canal and the Potomac through Hancock.

name: White Clay Creek State Park
desc: More than 37 miles of trails through a wooded creek valley and old farm fields north of Newark. The most varied trail system in Delaware for hiking, running and mountain biking.

name: White Cliffs of Conoy and Billmyer Ruins
desc: Bright white bluff of limestone and dolomite waste dumped over the Susquehanna by a vanished quarry town, with concrete ruins of the works along the Northwest Lancaster County River Trail. About 1.5 mi flat walk from Bainbridge.

name: White Rocks (Great North Mountain)
desc: Loop from Waites Run to a white quartzite cliff on the crest of Great North Mountain; on a clear day the view reaches Shenandoah National Park. Blazes near the overlook are faded.

name: Whiteoak Canyon Upper Falls (from Skyline Drive)
desc: Steady descent from Skyline Drive mile 42.6 to a rock ledge facing the 86-foot upper falls of Whiteoak Canyon. All the climbing is on the way back.

name: Widewater State Park
desc: State park on the peninsula between Aquia Creek and the Potomac. Two day-use areas with canoe and kayak launches, short trails, shoreline access and paddle-in campsites; usually uncrowded.

name: Winterthur Garden
desc: Henry Francis du Pont's 1,000-acre estate with a 60-acre naturalistic woodland garden. Peak color runs from the March bank and azalea woods in spring through fall foliage.

name: Wolf Rock (Catoctin Mountain Park)
desc: Long tilted slab of quartzite split by deep crevices that you scramble across. There is no wide view; the rock is the attraction. Half a mile along the ridge from Chimney Rock.

facts.dogs: leashed; not allowed on the rock formations

name: Woodstock Tower
desc: Steel observation tower built by the CCC in 1935 on Massanutten's ridge, a few minutes' walk from the road, looking straight down on the Seven Bends of the North Fork Shenandoah. Road closed in winter.

name: Wye Island - Ferry Point Trail
desc: Short flat walk through a tunnel of old Osage orange trees to a small sandy beach on the Wye River at the west tip of the island, with a picnic table and rope swing.

name: Independence National Historical Park
desc: Independence National Historical Park is a federally protected historic district in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, that preserves several sites associated with the American Revolution and the nation's founding history.

name: Crystal Cave
desc: Crystal Cave is a cave in Richmond Township, near Kutztown, in Berks County, Pennsylvania, United States, the heart of Pennsylvania Dutch Country. It was discovered by William Merkel and John Gehret on November 12, 1871, and quickly became a popular tourist attraction.

name: Laurel Fork North Wilderness
desc: Laurel Fork North Wilderness is a U.S. Wilderness Area located in the Greenbrier Ranger District of Monongahela National Forest in West Virginia. The Wilderness protects high-elevation lands along Laurel Fork (Cheat River) and is bordered by Middle Mountain to the west.

name: Laurel Summit State Park
desc: Laurel Summit State Park is a 6-acre (2.4 ha) Pennsylvania state park in Cook Township, Westmoreland County, Pennsylvania in the United States. It is also a picnic area with a scenic view of Linn Run on the summit of Laurel Mountain.

name: Penn-Roosevelt State Park
desc: Penn-Roosevelt State Park is a 41 acres (17 ha) Pennsylvania state park in Harris Township, Centre County, Pennsylvania in the United States. The park is surrounded by Rothrock State Forest. Penn-Roosevelt State Park is 6 miles (9.7 km) from U.S.

name: Priest Wilderness
desc: The Priest Wilderness is a U.S. Wilderness Area in the Glenwood/Pedlar Ranger District of the George Washington and Jefferson National Forests. The wilderness area is located just south of the Tye River, the Three Ridges Wilderness, and Virginia State Route 56.

name: Westmoreland State Park
desc: Westmoreland State Park lies within Westmoreland County, Virginia. The park extends about one and a half miles along the Potomac River and covers 1,321 acres. The Horsehead Cliffs provide visitors with a panoramic view of the Potomac River, and lower levels feature fossils and beach access.

name: Fort Tonoloway State Park
desc: Fort Tonoloway State Park is an undeveloped Maryland state park located near present-day Hancock. Fort Tonoloway was a frontier fort built in 1755 by Lt. Thomas Stoddert and men from the Maryland State Militia.

name: Patapsco Valley State Park Alberton Area
desc: Sub-unit of the larger Patapsco Valley State Park.

name: Patapsco Valley State Park Davis Area
desc: Sub-unit of the larger Patapsco Valley State Park.

name: Patapsco Valley State Park Freedom Area
desc: Sub-unit of the larger Patapsco Valley State Park.

name: Patapsco Valley State Park Glen Artney Area
desc: Sub-unit of the larger Patapsco Valley State Park.

name: Patapsco Valley State Park Marriottsville Area
desc: Sub-unit of the larger Patapsco Valley State Park.

name: Patapsco Valley State Park Orange Grove Area
desc: Sub-unit of the larger Patapsco Valley State Park.

name: Patapsco Valley State Park Pickall Area
desc: Sub-unit of the larger Patapsco Valley State Park.

name: Patapsco Valley State Park Sykesville/Henryton Area
desc: Sub-unit of the larger Patapsco Valley State Park.

name: Blackwater Falls
desc: Blackwater Falls State Park is located in the Allegheny Mountains of Tucker County, West Virginia, US. The centerpiece of the park is Blackwater Falls, a 62-foot (19 m) cascade where the Blackwater River leaves its leisurely course in Canaan Valley and enters rugged Blackwater Canyon.

name: Suquehanna National Wildlife Refuge
desc: Susquehanna River National Wildlife Refuge is located on a small island 3.79 acres (15,300 m2) in size located at the mouth of the Susquehanna River in Harford County, Maryland. It is a satellite refuge managed by Blackwater National Wildlife Refuge.

name: Delaware Seashore State Park Fresh Pond
Gunpowder Falls State Park Central Area
Gunpowder Falls State Park Franklintown Area
Gunpowder Falls State Park Jerusalem Mill Area
Gunpowder Falls State Park Lost Lake Area
Gunpowder Falls State Park Pleasantville Area
Gunpowder Falls State Park Springdale Area
Gunpowder Falls State Park Sweathouse Area
Patapsco Valley State Park Deep Run Area
desc: Sub-unit of the larger Patapsco Valley State Park.

name: Patapsco Valley State Park Halethorpe Ponds Area
desc: Sub-unit of the larger Patapsco Valley State Park.

name: Patapsco Valley State Park Woodstock Area
desc: Sub-unit of the larger Patapsco Valley State Park.

name: Joseph E. Ibberson Conservation Area
desc: Joseph E. Ibberson Conservation Area is an 803-acre (325 ha) Pennsylvania state park in Middle Paxton and Wayne Townships, Dauphin County, Pennsylvania in the United States. It is dominated by large hardwood trees and offers opportunities for hiking, cross-country skiing and hunting.

name: Serpentine Barrens Conservation Park
desc: Serpentine Barrens Conservation Park is the name of two protected areas in Montgomery County, Maryland. They cover a total of 288 acres, and protect rare serpentine ecosystems.

name: Soldiers Delight Natural Environment Area
desc: Soldiers Delight Natural Environmental Area is a nature reserve near Owings Mills in western Baltimore County, Maryland, U.S. The site is designated both as a Maryland Wildland (1,526 acres) and as a Natural Environment Area (1,900 acres) and is part of the Maryland Wildlands Preservation System.

name: Trexler Nature Preserve
desc: The Trexler Nature Preserve is an 1,108-acre county park (448 ha) owned and maintained by Lehigh County in the Lehigh Valley region of Pennsylvania. The preserve is situated in Lowhill Township and North Whitehall Township near the community of Schnecksville.

name: Tyler Arboretum
desc: Tyler Arboretum is a nonprofit arboretum located at 515 Painter Road, Middletown Township, Delaware County, Pennsylvania. The arboretum is open daily except for major holidays and an admission fee is charged to non-members.

name: White Clay Creek Preserve
desc: White Clay Creek Preserve is a 3,050-acre (1,230 ha) Pennsylvania state park along the valley of White Clay Creek in London Britain Township in Chester County, Pennsylvania in the United States.

name: Catoctin National Recreation Trail
desc: The Catoctin National Recreation Trail is a 26.6 mi (42.4 km) hiking trail that traverses federal, state, and municipal woodlands along the northern half of Catoctin Mountain in Frederick County in central Maryland, USA.

name: Gerry Connolly Cross County Trail
desc: The Gerry Connolly Cross County Trail is a 40.5-mile hiking, biking and bridle trail in Fairfax County, Virginia that traverses the entire length of the county in an arc that begins and ends at different points near the Potomac River.

name: Patapsco Valley State Park Avalon Area
desc: Sub-unit of the larger Patapsco Valley State Park.

name: Patapsco Valley State Park Gray's Mill Area
desc: Sub-unit of the larger Patapsco Valley State Park.

name: Patapsco Valley State Park Ilchester Area
desc: Sub-unit of the larger Patapsco Valley State Park.

name: Patapsco Valley State Park Norbeck Area
desc: Sub-unit of the larger Patapsco Valley State Park.

name: Patapsco Valley State Park Rockhaven Area
desc: Sub-unit of the larger Patapsco Valley State Park.

name: Blackbird State Forest
desc: Blackbird State Forest is a 6,000-acre (24 km2) state forest of Delaware located in New Castle County and Kent County, north of Smyrna.

name: Buchanan State Forest
desc: Buchanan State Forest is a Pennsylvania State Forest in Pennsylvania Bureau of Forestry District #2. The main office is located in McConnellsburg in Fulton County, Pennsylvania, in the United States. The forest also includes tracts in Franklin and Bedford Counties.

name: Delaware Breakwater East End Lighthouse
desc: The Delaware Breakwater East End Light is a lighthouse located on the inner Delaware Breakwater in the Delaware Bay, just off the coast of Cape Henlopen and the town of Lewes, Delaware.

name: Forbes State Forest
desc: Forbes State Forest is a Pennsylvania state forest in Pennsylvania Bureau of Forestry District #4. The main offices are located in Laughlintown in Westmoreland County, Pennsylvania in the United States. Mount Davis, the highest peak in Pennsylvania, is located in the forest.

name: Fort Loudoun
desc: Fort Loudoun (or Fort Loudon, after the modern spelling of the town) was a fort in colonial Pennsylvania, one of several forts in colonial America named after John Campbell, 4th Earl of Loudoun.

name: Fort Roberdeau
desc: Fort Roberdeau, also known as The Lead Mine Fort, is an historic fort, which is located in Tyrone Township, outside Altoona, Pennsylvania. It was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1974.

name: Fort Stevens Park
desc: Fort Stevens, formerly named Fort Massachusetts, was part of the extensive fortifications built around Washington, D.C., during the American Civil War.

name: Gallitzin State Forest
desc: Gallitzin State Forest is a Pennsylvania State Forest in Pennsylvania Bureau of Forestry District #6. The main offices are located in Ebensburg in Cambria County, Pennsylvania in the United States. The forest is located on 24,370 acres (9,860 ha) in two non-contiguous tracts.

name: Harbor of Refuge Light
desc: The Harbor of Refuge Light (originally Harbor of Refuge West End Light, though its east end counterpart has been long since discontinued) is a lighthouse built on the ocean end of the outer Delaware Breakwater at the mouth of the Delaware Bay, just off Cape Henlopen.

name: Michaux State Forest
desc: Michaux State Forest is a Pennsylvania State Forest in Pennsylvania Bureau of Forestry District #1. The main offices are located in Fayetteville in Franklin County, Pennsylvania, USA.

name: Poole's Island Lighthouse
desc: Pooles Island Light is the oldest lighthouse still standing in Maryland and the fourth oldest in the Chesapeake Bay area. The light is located on Pooles Island in the central Chesapeake Bay.

name: Rothrock State Forest
desc: Rothrock State Forest is a Pennsylvania state forest in Pennsylvania Bureau of Forestry District #5. The main offices are located in Huntingdon in Huntingdon County, Pennsylvania in the United States. Rothrock State Forest is located in Centre, Huntingdon, and Mifflin Counties.

name: Savage River State Forest
desc: Savage River State Forest is located in the north and northeastern part of Garrett County, in the U.S. state of Maryland. The state forest has many waterways, including Savage River Reservoir, which was built in 1952 by the U.S. Army.

name: Thomas Point Shoal Light
desc: The Thomas Point Shoal Light, also known as Thomas Point Shoal Light Station, is a historic lighthouse in the Chesapeake Bay on the east coast of the United States, and the most recognized lighthouse in Maryland. It is the only screw-pile lighthouse in the bay which stands at its original site.

name: Weiser State Forest
desc: Weiser State Forest is a Pennsylvania State Forest in Pennsylvania Bureau of Forestry District #18. The main offices are located in Cressona in Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania in the United States.

name: Auburn Valley State Park Oversee Property
Goshen Pass Natural Area Preserve
desc: Goshen Pass Natural Area Preserve is a 936-acre (3.79 km2) Natural Area Preserve located in Rockbridge County, Virginia. The oldest state-managed natural area in Virginia, it was first acquired in 1954 to help protect views of the gorge along the Maury River.

name: Gunpowder Falls State Park Graham Memorial Park Area
Patapsco Valley State Park Belle Grove Area
desc: Sub-unit of the larger Patapsco Valley State Park.

name: U-1105
desc: German submarine U-1105, a Type VII-C/41 U-boat of Nazi Germany's Kriegsmarine, was built at the Nordseewerke Shipyard, Emden, Germany, and commissioned on 3 June 1944. Oberleutnant zur See Hans-Joachim Schwarz was given command. He would command U-1105 for the remainder of the war.

name: Youghiogheny Wild River Natural Environmental Area
desc: The Youghiogheny Scenic & Wild River is a river given special protected status by the state of Maryland. This wild and scenic portion of the Youghiogheny River is located in Western Garrett County, in Western Maryland.

name: Zekiah Swamp Natural Environment Area
desc: Zekiah Swamp ( or ) is a swamp in Charles County, Maryland, in the United States, formed by the Zekiah Swamp Run, a braided stream which becomes Allens Fresh Run as it debouches into the Wicomico River, a left tributary of the Tidal Potomac River.

name: 1879 Hooper Straight Lighthouse
desc: Hooper Strait Light is one of four surviving Chesapeake Bay screw-pile lighthouses in the U.S. state of Maryland. Originally located in Hooper Strait, between Hooper and Bloodsworth Islands in Dorchester County and at the entrance to Tangier Sound, it is now an exhibit at the Chesapeake Bay…

name: Assateague Light
desc: Assateague Light is the 142-foot-tall (43 m) lighthouse located on the southern end of Assateague Island off the coast of the Virginia Eastern Shore, United States.

name: Baker Shoal Range Rear Light
desc: Baker Shoal Range Rear Lighthouse is a lighthouse in Delaware, United States, on the Delaware River, near Port Penn.

name: Baltimore Lighthouse
desc: The Baltimore Harbor Light, officially Baltimore Light and historically Baltimore Harbor Lighthouse is a privately owned caisson lighthouse in the Chesapeake Bay in Maryland.

name: Bellevue Range Rear Light
desc: Bellevue Range Rear Lighthouse is a lighthouse in Delaware, United States, at the mouth of the Christina River on the Delaware River, Wilmington, Delaware

name: Belt Woods Natural Environment Area
desc: Belt Woods is a nature reserve in Prince George's County, Maryland, U.S., containing the "South Woods", a 43-acre (170,000 m2) woodland which constitutes one of the last stands of old growth hardwood forest on the Atlantic coastal plain. It is a mere 8 miles (13 km) east of Washington, D.C.

name: Betsy Bell and Mary Gray Wilderness Parks
Blackistone Lighthouse
desc: The Blackistone Island Light was a lighthouse located on what is now St. Clement's Island on the Potomac River in Maryland. It is best known as the target of a Confederate raid in the Civil War.

name: Bloody Point Light
desc: Bloody Point Bar Light is an early sparkplug lighthouse in the Chesapeake Bay near Kent Island, Maryland.

name: Cannon Branch Redoubt
desc: The Cannon Branch Fort is a historic American Civil War fortification at 10611 Gateway Boulevard in Manassas, Virginia. Details of the exact time and circumstances of its construction are not known; it is believed to have been built by Union Army forces in 1863 or 1864 to defend the nearby railroad…

name: Concord Point Lighthouse
desc: Concord Point Light is a 36-foot (11 m) lighthouse in Havre de Grace, Maryland. It overlooks the point where Susquehanna River flows into the Chesapeake Bay, an area of increasing navigational traffic when it was constructed in 1827.

name: Conestoga Trail System
desc: The Conestoga Trail is a 65.8-mile (105.9 km) linear hiking trail in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania. The trail connects several relatively short and discontinuous footpaths with walks on paved roads.

name: Craighill Channel Lower Range Front Light
desc: The Craighill Channel Lower Range Front Light, named for William Price Craighill, was the first caisson lighthouse built in the Chesapeake Bay in Maryland, USA.

name: Craighill Channel Lower Range Rear Light
desc: The Craighill Channel Lower Range Rear Light is one of a pair of range lights that marks the first section of the shipping channel into Baltimore harbor. It is the tallest lighthouse in Maryland.

name: Craighill Channel Upper Range Front Light
desc: The Craighill Channel Upper Range Front Light is one of a pair of range lights that marks the second section of the shipping channel into Baltimore harbor.

name: Craighill Channel Upper Range Rear Light
desc: The Craighill Channel Upper Range Rear Light is one of a pair of range lights that marks the second section of the shipping channel into Baltimore harbor.

name: Fishing Battery Light
desc: Fishing Battery Light was the last lighthouse constructed in Maryland by John Donahoo. While still standing, it has been supplanted by a steel tower which stands adjacent to it.

name: Fort Armistead
desc: Fort Armistead was a United States Army coastal defense fort, active from 1901 to 1920, that defended Baltimore, Maryland.

name: Fort Carroll Lighthouse
desc: Fort Carroll Light is a derelict lighthouse consisting of a short wooden tower on the walls of its namesake fortifications in the Patapsco River.

name: Fort Delaware
desc: Fort Delaware is a former harbor defense facility, designed by chief engineer Joseph Gilbert Totten and located on Pea Patch Island in the Delaware River.

name: Fort Foote
desc: Fort Foote was an American Civil War-era wood and earthwork fort that was part of the wartime defenses of Washington, D.C., which helped defend the Potomac River approach to the city.

name: Fort Ligonier
desc: Fort Ligonier is a British fortification from the French and Indian War located in Ligonier, Pennsylvania, United States. The fort served as a staging area for the Forbes Expedition of 1758. During the eight years of its existence as a garrison, Fort Ligonier was never taken by an enemy.

name: Fort Washington Light
desc: Fort Washington Light is a lighthouse located on the banks of the Potomac River on the grounds of its namesake fort. There has been a lighthouse on the location since 1857; the current light was converted from a fog bell tower in 1901.

name: Harrisburg Military Post
desc: The Harrisburg Military Post is an historic National Guard armory complex and national historic district which is located in Harrisburg, Dauphin County, Pennsylvania. It serves as the headquarters for the 28th Infantry Division. It was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1991.

name: Holland Island Bar Light
desc: The Holland Island Bar Light was a screw-pile lighthouse in the Chesapeake Bay which existed from 1889 to 1960. It is remembered for the unexplained death of one of its keepers, and for being "attacked" by United States Navy pilots during a training exercise.

name: Hooper Island Light
desc: The Hooper Island Light is a lighthouse in the Chesapeake Bay, west of Middle Hooper Island in Maryland.

name: Hooper Strait Light
desc: Hooper Strait Light is one of four surviving Chesapeake Bay screw-pile lighthouses in the U.S. state of Maryland. Originally located in Hooper Strait, between Hooper and Bloodsworth Islands in Dorchester County and at the entrance to Tangier Sound, it is now an exhibit at the Chesapeake Bay…

name: Jones Point Lighthouse
desc: The Jones Point Light is a small river lighthouse located on the Potomac River in Alexandria, Virginia. It was built in 1855.

name: Laurel Highlands Hiking Trail
desc: Laurel Ridge State Park is a 13,625-acre (5,514 ha) Pennsylvania state park that with parcels in Cambria, Fayette, Somerset, and Westmoreland counties, Pennsylvania in the United States.

name: Lazaretto Point Light
desc: The Lazaretto Point Light was a historic lighthouse in Baltimore harbor. Though long demolished, a replica stands near its original site.

name: Liston Range Front Light
desc: Liston Range Front Lighthouse is a lighthouse in Delaware, United States, on the Delaware River. It is a range light, paired with the Liston Range Rear Light, to create the Liston Range.

name: Love Point Light
desc: Love Point Light was a screw-pile lighthouse in the Chesapeake Bay, off the northern end of Kent Island, Maryland.

name: Marcus Hook Range Rear Light
desc: Marcus Hook Range Rear Light is a lighthouse near Bellefonte, Delaware marking a range on the Delaware River. It is the highest light on the Atlantic coast of the United States. The lighthouse is visible on the horizon from the windows of high-rise buildings in downtown Wilmington, Delaware.

name: Point Lookout Light
desc: Point Lookout Light is a lighthouse that marks the entrance to the Potomac River at the southernmost tip of Maryland's western shore of the Chesapeake Bay, south of the town of Scotland in Saint Mary's County, Maryland, USA. The lighthouse is located in Point Lookout State Park.

name: Point No Point Light
desc: Point No Point Light, located in the Chesapeake Bay off the eponymous point several miles north of the mouth of the Potomac River, was constructed as part of a program to add lighted navigational aids in a thirty-mile stretch of the bay between Cove and Smith Points.

name: Ragged Point Light
desc: The Ragged Point Light was a screw-pile lighthouse located in the Potomac River. It was the last lighthouse built in Maryland waters and the last built at a location in the Chesapeake Bay.

name: Reedy Island Range Rear Light Station
desc: Reedy Island Range Rear Lighthouse is a skeletal tower lighthouse near Taylor's Bridge, Delaware. The tower is an active aid to navigation.

name: Sandy Point Shoal Light
desc: Sandy Point Shoal Light is a brick three story lighthouse on a caisson foundation that was erected in 1883. It lies about 0.6 mi (0.97 km) off Sandy Point, north of the Chesapeake Bay Bridge, from whose westbound span it is readily visible.

name: Solomons Lump Light
desc: Solomons Lump Light is a lighthouse in the Chesapeake Bay, the abbreviated remains of a caisson light built in 1895. That structure replaced a screw-pile light built on the same spot in 1875, which in turn superseded the Fog Point Light.

name: Standing Stone Trail
desc: The Standing Stone Trail is an 84.2-mile (135.5 km) linear hiking trail in south-central Pennsylvania, leading from Cowans Gap State Park in Fulton County, north to Detweiler Run Natural Area in Huntingdon County.

name: Turkey Point Light
desc: The Turkey Point Light is a historic lighthouse at the head of the Chesapeake Bay. Although only a 35-foot (11 m) tower, the 100-foot (30 m) height of the bluffs on which it stands makes it the third highest light off the water in the bay.

name: Turtle Rock Light
desc: The Lighthouse on Turtle Rock is a lighthouse built in 1887 to aid traffic on the Schuylkill River near Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The lighthouse was constructed by Frank Thurwanger at a cost of $2,663 on an area of land just west of Boathouse Row.

name: Wheaton Regional Park
desc: Wheaton Regional Park is a public park and county-designated protected area, located in Wheaton, Maryland. It is operated and managed by Montgomery County Parks (Montgomery Parks), a division of a bi-county agency, Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission (M–NCPPC), which serves both…

name: York County Heritage Rail Trail
desc: Heritage Rail Trail County Park is a National Recreation Trail rail-with-trail in Pennsylvania built in 1999 by the York County Rail Trail Authority (YCRTA). It connects with the Torrey C. Brown Rail Trail in Maryland.

name: Abbott's Mill Nature Center
desc: Working water-powered grist mill on a pond outside Milford, with more than three miles of trails and boardwalks through pine woods, stream bottom and Atlantic white cedar swamp.

name: Abingdon Plantation ruins (Reagan National Airport)
desc: Excavated brick foundations of an 18th-century plantation house preserved on a grassy knoll between parking garages A and B/C at Reagan National Airport. Free; walk over from the Metro station.

name: Acton Cove Park
desc: Small city waterfront park at Acton Cove on Spa Creek with benches overlooking the moored boats. A quiet sit-down spot a few blocks from downtown Annapolis.

name: Adams Memorial (Rock Creek Cemetery)
desc: Augustus Saint-Gaudens' shrouded bronze figure of 1891, seated in a small hedged room designed by Stanford White inside Rock Creek Cemetery. Quiet, free, open during cemetery hours.

name: Air Force Memorial
desc: Three stainless-steel spires up to 270 ft tall on a hill above the Pentagon. The plaza looks across the Potomac to the Washington Monument and the Capitol.

name: Aldie Mill
desc: Early-1800s brick merchant mill with twin overshot water wheels, restored and run as a small NOVA Parks historic park. Walk around the outside on US-50 any time; the interior opens for grinding demonstrations on set days.

name: Algonkian Regional Park
desc: 838-acre park on the Potomac in eastern Loudoun with a boat ramp, picnic shelters, rental cottages and paved and natural trails through riverside woods. Open sunrise to sunset.

name: Allens Fresh / Zekiah Swamp Natural Environment Area
desc: Where the 20-mile Zekiah Swamp, one of the largest hardwood swamps in Maryland, drains into the Wicomico River. Roadside access on MD 234 for birding, fishing and launching a kayak; no trails.

name: Allstadt Farm Ruins (Schoolhouse Ridge South)
desc: Stone ruin of the Greek Revival Allstadt house, its interior burned out in 1986, on the Schoolhouse Ridge South battlefield trail (up to 3.7 mi round trip) west of town. Look from outside; the park is still documenting the site.

name: Anita C. Leight Estuary Center
desc: Nature center on Otter Point Creek, part of the Chesapeake Bay research reserve: wooded trails to tidal freshwater marsh, an observation deck and guided canoe trips.

name: Annapolis City Dock
desc: The colonial harbor basin at the foot of Main Street, with the Kunta Kinte-Alex Haley Memorial and Susan Campbell Park at the water's end. Parts have been under reconstruction as a raised waterfront park.

name: Annapolis Waterworks Park
desc: About 11 miles of unpaved hiking and mountain-bike trails around the old Annapolis city reservoir, linking toward Bacon Ridge. Entry is by paid city permit only (monthly, quarterly or annual).

name: Antietam Creek Aqueduct (C&O Canal)
desc: Three-arch stone aqueduct carrying the towpath over the mouth of Antietam Creek, next to a walk-in riverside campground.

name: Antietam Iron Works
desc: Ironworks hamlet at the mouth of Antietam Creek: a four-arch stone bridge of 1832, the dam and race, and stone kilns and other ironworks remnants beside Harpers Ferry Rd. Roadside viewing only; the houses are private homes.

facts.access: You can only look at this one from outside (road, trail or water). The site itself is closed or fenced.

name: Apollo County Park
desc: Undeveloped county park of steep wooded ravines dropping to the Susquehanna, crossed by the Mason-Dixon Trail. Rugged and little used.

name: Appalachian Trail Museum and halfway point
desc: Old stone mill turned museum of the Appalachian Trail, at the trail's traditional halfway stop, where thru-hikers attempt to eat a half gallon of ice cream at the general store.

name: Aquatic Resources Education Center Boardwalk
desc: State fish-and-wildlife education site on the road to Woodland Beach with a three-quarter-mile boardwalk loop over the salt marsh and small fishing piers on the ponds.

name: Aqueduct Bridge Abutment
