desc: Stone abutment and a river pier of the Aqueduct Bridge that once carried canal boats, then traffic, across the Potomac from Georgetown. At the foot of the Capital Crescent Trail by the boathouse; free.

name: Auburn Valley State Park
desc: Delaware's newest state park, built around the Marshall family's 1897 mansion and steam-car collection, with trails along Red Clay Creek on a reclaimed mill site.

name: Augustine Beach and Port Penn Wetlands
desc: Sandy strip on the Delaware River with a boat ramp and big parking lot, a mile south of Port Penn's short boardwalk trail into the marsh. Wide river views across to New Jersey.

name: Baker Park and Carroll Creek Park
desc: Downtown Frederick's main park with a carillon tower and Culler Lake, linked to the Carroll Creek promenade of brick walks, footbridges and water-lily plantings.

name: Baltimore Boulevard Remnants (Life of the Dunes Trail)
desc: Broken asphalt of the main road of a 1950s resort subdivision on Assateague, destroyed by the March 1962 storm, half-buried in dunes along a short sandy loop trail in the national seashore. Park entry fee.

name: Banner's Overlook (Green Ridge State Forest)
desc: Overlook at 1,650 ft on Mertens Avenue near the center of the forest, looking east toward the Potomac and the West Virginia ridges. Named for an early forest warden.

name: Battery Hartshorne (Fort Smallwood Park)
desc: Concrete gun battery of the 1890s Patapsco coast-defense fort that gave Fort Smallwood Park its name, on Rock Point a few miles from Pasadena, near the fishing pier and beach. County park with a vehicle entry fee.

name: Battery Kemble Park
desc: Grassy bowl and wooded ravine in the Palisades around the earthworks of an 1861 gun battery. A dirt trail follows the stream downhill toward the C&O Canal; popular for sledding in winter.

name: Bay Shore Park Remnants
desc: What is left of a trolley amusement park that ran 1906-1947 and was torn down by Bethlehem Steel: the restored trolley station and fountain, a pier, and the roofless power house. Flat paths in North Point State Park; fee.

name: Bazil Newman Riverfront Park
desc: Loudoun County park (formerly Elizabeth Mills Riverfront Park) on the Potomac just below the mouth of Goose Creek. Riverside stretch of the Potomac Heritage Trail; canoe launch at adjoining Kephart Bridge Landing.

name: Bazzel Church
desc: Weathered 1911 frame church alone in a field on Bestpitch Ferry Rd, on the site of an earlier chapel where Harriet Tubman's family is said to have worshipped. Fragile and on private ground; look from the roadside.

facts.access: You can only look at this one from outside (road, trail or water). The site itself is closed or fenced.

name: Bealers Ferry (South Fork Shenandoah)
desc: Secluded Forest Service boat launch on the South Fork below Massanutten's east wall, with an accessible fishing pond beside it. A put-in or take-out for float trips.

name: Bellevue Landing
desc: Public dock, boat ramp, picnic area and a tiny beach at the Bellevue end of the Oxford ferry crossing. Faces east over the Tred Avon, so it is a sunrise spot.

name: Benjamin Banneker Historical Park
desc: 142-acre county park on the homestead of the self-taught astronomer and almanac author Benjamin Banneker, with a museum, a replica cabin and wooded trails that link to the No. 9 Trolley Trail.

name: Bentonville Low-Water Bridge and Landing
desc: One-lane concrete bridge that sits just above the South Fork Shenandoah on Indian Hollow Road, with a state boat landing and parking beside it. A common spot to wade, tube or launch a canoe.

name: Bethany Beach Boardwalk
desc: Short, low-key boardwalk on a guarded ocean beach in the quietest of the Delaware resort towns.

facts.fee: beach free; paid parking in season

name: Betsy Bell Wilderness Park
desc: Wooded hill in Staunton with an observation platform at 1,959 ft looking east toward Waynesboro and the Blue Ridge. Reached by a steep access road or on foot. About 154 miles from home.

name: Bickle Knob Observation Tower
desc: One of the last climbable observation towers in Monongahela National Forest, on a summit east of Elkins near the south end of Otter Creek Wilderness. Road access in the warm months.

name: Big Meadows Campground
desc: The park's central campground (221 sites, mile 51.2), walking distance to Big Meadows, Dark Hollow Falls and Lewis Falls. Open spring to late November.

name: Big Round Top (Gettysburg)
desc: Wooded, boulder-strewn hill that is the highest point on the battlefield. A short steep path climbs to the summit; quiet compared with its neighbor.

name: Big Run Loop
desc: Quiet South District loop from Big Run Overlook down into the park's largest watershed and back on the AT past Doyles River Overlook. Chosen for solitude more than views.

name: Big Run State Park and Savage River Reservoir
desc: Primitive campsites where Big Run and Monroe Run meet at the head of the 360-acre Savage River Reservoir, deep in state forest. Quiet paddling and trout fishing.

name: Big Spring Railroad Tunnel
desc: Never-finished narrow-gauge railroad tunnel bored into Conococheague Mountain during the lumber era. A one-mile trail leads to it from Big Spring State Forest Picnic Area on PA-274. Look at the portal; do not go inside.

name: Big Spring State Forest Picnic Area
desc: Picnic stop on PA 274 with a trail to a railroad tunnel that was started into Conococheague Mountain and never finished.

name: Big Stone Beach
desc: Remote bay beach at the end of a long road through the Milford Neck marshes, with room for two or three cars and a lone WWII fire-control tower standing back from the sand.

name: Bill Burton Fishing Pier State Park
desc: The old Choptank River bridge, kept as fishing piers beside the new one, with a short trail and a strip of river beach on the Talbot side. Pier sections have been closed for repairs; check first.

name: Billy Goat Trail Section B
desc: 1.4-mile riverside section reached from the Angler's parking area, quieter than Section A with a few easy scrambles. Closed for years by erosion; NPS listed it open in late September 2026.

name: Biscoe Gray Heritage Farm
desc: County heritage farm beside Battle Creek with mown and wooded trails past old tobacco barns and farm buildings down to the creek marsh. Pairs well with the cypress swamp nearby.

name: Bishop's Garden (Washington National Cathedral)
desc: Walled garden below the cathedral's south side with a stone gazebo, herb beds, old boxwood and roses, plus views up to the towers. The Olmsted Woods path starts next door. Open daily, free.

name: Black Rock Mill
desc: Stone shell of an 1815 grist and sawmill beside Great Seneca Creek, stabilized with interpretive panels inside. Roadside stop on Black Rock Road and a landmark on the Seneca Creek Greenway Trail.

name: Blackbird Creek Reserve
desc: State estuarine research reserve with more than seven miles of mown and wooded trails along a winding tidal creek, plus a canoe launch. Little used.

name: Blackbird State Forest - Cypress Complex
desc: Delaware has three state forests, one in each county, totaling more than 19,000 acres (77 km2). These natural resource areas are managed by the Delaware Department of Agriculture Forest Service.

name: Bladensburg Waterfront Park
desc: County park on the tidal Anacostia with a boat ramp, fishing pier, kayak and canoe rentals and pontoon tours in season. The Anacostia River Trail heads south from here to Kenilworth and DC.

name: Bloede Dam Site
in: Patapsco Valley State Park Orange Grove Area
desc: Where Bloede Dam, built in 1906 with the first hydroelectric plant housed inside its own spillway, stood until it was breached in 2018 and gone by 2019. The freed river is seen from the Grist Mill Trail.

name: Bloody Lane Observation Tower (Antietam)
desc: Stone War Department tower at the end of the Sunken Road. Climb it for a full view of the battlefield with South Mountain on the horizon.

name: Bloomery Iron Furnace
desc: Stone iron furnace from the 1830s standing a few feet off WV-127 (Bloomery Pike) near the Cacapon River. On private ground; look from the roadside and historical marker.

facts.access: You can only look at this one from outside (road, trail or water). The site itself is closed or fenced.

name: Blue Blazes Whiskey Still (Catoctin Mountain Park)
desc: Short creekside trail from the visitor center to a moonshine still exhibit at the site of a large Prohibition-era operation raided in 1929.

name: Blue Hole Day Use Area (Bergton)
desc: Forest Service picnic spot at a deep bend of the North Fork Shenandoah off Route 259, used as a swimming hole by locals. Open sunrise to sunset; no cliff jumping or rope swings.

name: Blue Ridge Summit Vista (Catoctin Mountain Park)
desc: North-facing overlook toward Blue Ridge Summit and the Pennsylvania line, on the ridge trail between Hog Rock and Thurmont Vista. The quietest of the park vistas.

name: Bob's Hill Overlooks (Cunningham Falls State Park)
desc: Climb the Catoctin Trail from the Manor Area to two short spur trails, one ledge facing north and one facing south over the Frederick Valley.

facts.fee: Manor Area: $3 per vehicle MD residents, $5 out of state

name: Bogles Wharf Landing
desc: County landing on the Chester River side of Eastern Neck Island with a pier, ramp and a small sandy shoreline. A quiet place to sit or launch a kayak inside the refuge.

name: Bohemia River State Park
desc: State park opened in 2022 on former farmland along Great Bohemia Creek: about five miles of flat natural-surface trails through fields and woods to creek overlooks. Open 7 am to sunset.

name: Bolen Cemetery (Little Devils Stairs)
desc: Stone-walled family cemetery left from a mountain community removed for Shenandoah National Park, beside Keyser Run Fire Road. Passed on the Little Devils Stairs loop (about 5.5 mi) from the end of VA-614.

name: Bolivar Heights
desc: Open ridge with Civil War earthworks and cannon and a clear view east through the Harpers Ferry water gap. Easy mowed loops from the lot.

name: Bondsville Mill Park
desc: Township park built around the surviving stone buildings and ruins of the Bondsville textile mill on Beaver Creek, with a short loop trail. On Bondsville Rd north of Downingtown; free.

name: Borden Tunnel
desc: 957 ft formerly abandoned Western Maryland Railway tunnel on the Great Allegheny Passage, about 2.5 mi up the trail from the Frostburg trailhead. Open to walkers and bikes.

name: Box Huckleberry Natural Area
desc: Ten-acre woodlot protecting a single colony of box huckleberry more than 1,000 years old, on a short interpretive loop. The smallest state forest natural area in Pennsylvania.

name: Boyd Big Tree Preserve Conservation Area
desc: 1,025 acres of mature forest on the slope of Blue Mountain north of Harrisburg, set aside for its large trees, with a network of loop trails.

name: Brighton Dam Azalea Garden
desc: Five acres of woodland with more than 22,000 azaleas beside Triadelphia Reservoir, peaking in late April and early May. Open daily in season from 7 am to sunset; no pets.

name: Bristoe Station Battlefield Heritage Park
desc: Open fields and woods preserved from the 1863 battle, with mown walking trails, interpretive signs and big skies. A quieter alternative to the Manassas battlefield.

name: Broadford Lake Park
desc: Town-run lake park just outside Oakland with a beach and swimming area and cheap canoe, kayak and paddle-boat rentals. Open Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day weekend.

name: Brown Mountain Overlook
desc: Long South District overlook at 2,844 ft over Big Run, with Rocky Mountain close in and Rockytop and Trayfoot Mountain beyond.

name: Buchanan's Birthplace State Park
desc: Pyramid of native stone in a wooded hollow below Tuscarora Mountain, marking the cabin site where President James Buchanan was born. An 18.5-acre park with a trout stream and picnic tables.

name: Buddy Attick Lake Park (Greenbelt Lake)
desc: Crushed-stone path of about 1.25 miles around Greenbelt Lake, built with the New Deal town in the 1930s. Shaded, flat and a short walk from the historic Roosevelt Center.

name: Bull Run Hydroelectric Dam Ruins
desc: Broken concrete dam and powerhouse remains on Bull Run, with the Union Mills site just upstream, below Hemlock Overlook Regional Park. Downhill walk on the park trails to the Bull Run-Occoquan Trail; free.

name: Bunny Man Bridge (Colchester Overpass)
desc: One-lane concrete tunnel under the railroad on Colchester Road, the setting of Fairfax County's 1970s 'Bunny Man' legend. No parking at the bridge; police restrict access around Halloween.

name: Bushwood Wharf
desc: County landing on the wide Wicomico River with a pier, floating dock and picnic tables. Faces west over open water, so it is a quiet local sunset spot.

name: Buzzard Hill
desc: Quiet stretch of the AT 'Roller Coaster' from a small lot on gravel Morgans Mill Road: a creek crossing, a small waterfall and west-facing ledges at 1,266 ft.

name: Buzzards Rock (Patapsco Valley State Park)
in: Patapsco Valley State Park Gray's Mill Area
desc: Rock outcrop high on the wooded gorge wall in the Hilton Area with a framed view down the Patapsco valley, reached by a moderate hike on the park's ridge and Sawmill Branch trails.

name: C.M. Crockett Park
desc: Fauquier County park on 109-acre Germantown Lake with a boat ramp, boat rentals, shoreline fishing and picnic grounds on 100 acres of rolling woods.

name: Cabin Branch Pyrite Mine
desc: Capped shafts and foundations of a commissary, crusher house and mill from a pyrite mine on Quantico Creek, in Prince William Forest Park. Reached by park trails with interpretive signs; park entry fee.

name: Cabin John Stream Valley Trail
desc: Natural-surface trail of 8.8 miles following Cabin John Creek from MacArthur Boulevard near the Potomac up to Cabin John Regional Park, in a wooded corridor between neighborhoods.

name: Cacapon Mountain Overlook
desc: Overlook at 2,320 ft on the crest of Cacapon Mountain, the highest point in the park and in Morgan County, reached by the park's mountain road or by trail.

name: Caledonia Furnace
desc: Rebuilt stone stack and blacksmith shop marking Thaddeus Stevens's ironworks, burned by Confederate cavalry in June 1863 on the way to Gettysburg. Beside US-30 at the entrance of Caledonia State Park. Free.

name: Camp Roosevelt Recreation Area
desc: Small Forest Service campground on the site of the first Civilian Conservation Corps camp in the nation; a path passes the old building foundations. Trailhead for Kennedy Peak. Seasonal.

name: Canal Place (C&O Canal terminus)
desc: Western end of the 184.5-mile C&O Canal towpath and starting point of the Great Allegheny Passage, beside the scenic railroad station in downtown Cumberland.

name: Canton Waterfront Park
desc: Open lawn and promenade on the harbor in Canton with a public boat ramp, fishing pier, the Korean War Memorial and views across to Fort McHenry and the working port.

name: Carlisle Iron Works Furnace
desc: 18th-century stone iron furnace stack standing beside the Appalachian Trail and Children's Lake in the village of Boiling Springs. A two-minute walk from the trail parking; free.

name: Carrollton Viaduct
desc: Stone arch over the Gwynns Falls finished in 1829 for the B&O, still carrying freight trains. Seen from the Gwynns Falls Trail near Carroll Park; the bridge itself is railroad property.

facts.access: You can only look at this one from outside (road, trail or water). The site itself is closed or fenced.

name: Carrs Wharf
desc: County pier at the end of Carrs Wharf Road on the Rhode River in Mayo. A small quiet site for fishing, crabbing and launching a kayak, with only a few parking spaces.

name: Casselman River Bridge State Park
desc: Stone bridge built in 1813-14 for the National Road; its 80-ft span was the largest stone arch in America at the time. Walk over it, then visit the artisan village next door.

name: Catharine Furnace Ruins
desc: Stone stack of an iron furnace built in 1837, shut ten years later, revived for the Confederacy and partly wrecked by Union troops in 1864. Roadside stop on Furnace Rd, on Jackson's flank march route at Chancellorsville battlefield. Free.

name: Catherine Furnace
desc: A 32-foot pyramidal stone iron furnace built in 1836 and abandoned in 1885, standing beside a forest road in the southern Massanutten. Trailhead for Roaring Run and Morgan Run loops.

name: Cedar Creek and Belle Grove National Historical Park
desc: Belle Grove's 1797 limestone manor and the surrounding Cedar Creek battlefield of October 1864. The Morning Attack Trails, three linked loops, walk the ground of the dawn assault.

name: Cedar Haven Fishing Area
desc: Tiny county waterfront site on the wide lower Patuxent at Eagle Harbor: 10 parking spaces, picnic tables, shoreline fishing and a soft launch for kayaks. Open 8 to sunset, free.

name: Champe Rocks
desc: Twin quartzite crags like a smaller Seneca Rocks, standing over the North Fork a few miles north on WV 28. Viewed from the road.

name: Chapel Point State Park
desc: Undeveloped state land on the Port Tobacco River with a sandy soft launch for canoes and kayaks and a small shoreline for fishing. No facilities.

name: Chatham Manor
desc: 1771 Georgian mansion on Stafford Heights with a walled garden and a river terrace looking across the Rappahannock to Fredericksburg's steeples. National Park Service site; grounds free.

name: Cherry Beach Park
desc: Town park on the upper Nanticoke River at Sharptown with a small sandy beach, boat ramp and picnic area on a quiet, tree-lined bend.

name: Chesapeake Beach Railway Trail
desc: Flat boardwalk-and-gravel path on the old railway bed along Fishing Creek, crossing tidal marsh on long wooden bridges. Good for herons, ospreys and an easy out-and-back run.

name: Children's Lake (Boiling Springs)
desc: Spring-fed village lake with a level path around it, an old iron furnace stack, and the Appalachian Trail running along the shore.

name: Chimney Rock and Calvary Rocks
desc: Out-and-back from Riprap parking (mile 90) to white quartzite outcrops with views west and north; Chimney Rock stands alone across a gap. The short version of the Riprap loop.

name: Chincoteague Island Nature Trail
desc: Paved 1.4-mile loop through pine woods on the town side of the island, off Hallie Whealton Smith Drive. A shaded walk or jog outside the refuge.

name: Chincoteague Veterans Memorial Park
desc: Bayside park on the south part of the island with a fishing and crabbing pier, boat ramp and an open view west across the channel. A local sunset spot.

name: Chris Greene Lake Park
desc: Sand beach on a lake north of Charlottesville, open for swimming 10-6 from Memorial Day weekend, with 3 miles of trails and a dog park.

facts.fee: Beach fee in summer for non-residents

name: Claiborne Landing
desc: Old steamboat and ferry landing on Eastern Bay: a stone jetty, boat ramp and a short path to a small beach and wading area. Open water to the west for sunsets.

name: Claude Moore Park
desc: County park in Sterling with ponds, woods and a preserved stretch of colonial Vestal's Gap Road, plus the Lanesville house and a farm museum. Miles of easy loop trails.

name: Clifton Park Valve House
desc: Derelict octagonal stone gatehouse built for the Lake Clifton reservoir, on Preservation Maryland's threatened list since 2014. Fenced; look from the park edge along St. Lo Dr. Exterior only.

facts.access: You can only look at this one from outside (road, trail or water). The site itself is closed or fenced.

name: Climbers Run Nature Center
desc: Lancaster Conservancy preserve and nature center on a restored trout stream, with easy loops through woods and meadow.

name: Clopper Mill Ruins
desc: Stone-and-brick walls of a grist mill on Great Seneca Creek in Seneca Creek State Park, near Clopper Rd and Waring Station Rd. A short path from the roadside; walls are unstable, look from outside.

name: Codorus Furnace
desc: Stone iron furnace from about 1836 standing beside the road near the mouth of Codorus Creek. A two-minute stop.

name: Columbia Crossing River Trails Center
desc: Riverfront trailhead under the mile-long concrete-arch Veterans Memorial Bridge, start of the Northwest Lancaster County River Trail.

name: Columbia-Wrightsville Bridge Piers
desc: Line of old stone piers marching across the mile-wide Susquehanna beside the 1930 concrete arch bridge: relics of earlier crossings, one of them burned in June 1863 to stop the Confederate advance. Seen from either riverfront.

facts.access: You can only look at this one from outside (road, trail or water). The site itself is closed or fenced.

name: Colvin Run Mill
desc: Working water-powered gristmill from about 1811 with a wooden water wheel, a miller's house and a general store. Grounds are free; mill tours and grinding demonstrations on set days.

name: Confederate Breastworks (Fort Edward Johnson)
desc: Trenches dug in 1862 along the crest of Shenandoah Mountain where US-250 crosses it, with a short signed loop and long views west. National forest roadside lot; free.

name: Congressional Cemetery
desc: Active cemetery founded in 1807 above the Anacostia: rows of sandstone cenotaphs for early members of Congress and the graves of John Philip Sousa and J. Edgar Hoover. Open daily for walking.

name: Conway Robinson State Forest
desc: 444-acre state forest beside the Manassas battlefield with stands of old pine and hardwood and flat loop trails for hikers, riders and mountain bikers. Small lot on US 29.

name: Cosca Regional Park
desc: More than 690 acres near Clinton with a small lake, the Clearwater Nature Center, natural-surface trails through forest and reservable campsites. Lake fishing is suspended after dredging.

name: Cove Point Lighthouse
desc: Working 1828 brick lighthouse on a sand spit jutting into the Bay, with the LNG terminal offshore. The grounds only open on limited afternoons May-September (1-4 pm); check before driving.

name: Coventry Parish Ruins
desc: Tall roofless brick walls of an 18th-century Episcopal church used until the late 1800s, standing in its churchyard at Rehobeth near the Pocomoke River; stabilized in 1928 and 2005. Roadside, free.

name: Cox's Point Park
desc: County park on a point in Back River with a two-lane boat ramp, piers, shoreline fishing, picnic pavilions and a playground. No ramp fee.

name: Cromwell Valley Lime Kilns
desc: Restored stone lime kilns from the valley's 19th-century lime-burning industry, beside Minebank Run on the easy trails of Cromwell Valley Park off Cromwell Bridge Rd. Free.

name: Crownsville Hospital Memorial Park
desc: Campus of the state psychiatric hospital founded for Black patients, open 1911-2004 and county-owned since 2022. Buildings are closed while a master plan is made; the patient cemetery is reached through Bacon Ridge Natural Area.

facts.access: You can only look at this one from outside (road, trail or water). The site itself is closed or fenced.

name: Culp's Hill Observation Tower (Gettysburg)
desc: Steel War Department tower on the wooded hill that anchored the Union right. Climb it for a view over the town and the fields to the east.

name: Curtis Merritt Harbor
desc: Working harbor at the far south tip of Chincoteague Island. From the lot you look across the inlet to Assateague's hook and out over open marsh; seafood boats come and go.

name: Cypress Branch State Park
desc: Small state park opened in 2022 two miles north of Millington: a three-acre fishing pond with picnic tables and 314 acres of undeveloped meadow and woods to wander. Open 8 am to sunset.

name: Cypress Park and Nature Trail, Pocomoke City
desc: Riverside town park with a boardwalk nature trail that leaves the lawn and winds through bald cypress swamp along the Pocomoke River.

name: Daingerfield Island
desc: National Park Service peninsula south of the airport with the Washington Sailing Marina, a shoreline path and picnic lawns. Wide view of the river, planes and the DC skyline; on the Mount Vernon Trail.

name: Dam 4 (C&O Canal)
desc: Stone canal dam with the whole Potomac pouring over it, a winch house and an old hydro plant on the far bank. Flatwater paddling above, fishing below.

name: Dam 5 (C&O Canal)
desc: Canal feeder dam across the Potomac with a lockhouse and inlet lock at the end of a quiet road. Loud water and little company.

name: Dans Mountain State Park
desc: 482-acre park high on Dans Mountain above the Georges Creek valley, with a summer swimming pool, picnic areas and a fishing pond.

name: David Force Natural Resource Area
desc: Undeveloped county woodland with a few miles of quiet natural-surface trails across streams and through mature forest. Small roadside trailhead.

name: Davidsonville Park (Patuxent River launch)
desc: County park on Patuxent River Road listed for both fishing and a cartop launch, giving access to the upper tidal Patuxent. The rest of the park is athletic fields.

name: Deale Wharf
desc: County fishing pier on Rockhold Creek in the working-waterfront village of Deale, listed by the county as a public fishing site.

name: Devil's Backbone County Park
desc: Small county park where Antietam Creek bends around a narrow rock ridge: a dam, a footbridge, canoe access, fishing and picnic tables under big sycamores.

name: Dinosaur Land
desc: Roadside park of more than fifty painted dinosaur statues (plus a giant shark and King Kong) set among trees, running since 1963. Seasonal hours; small admission fee.

name: Dinosaur Park
desc: Fenced clay exposure, 115 million years old, where Astrodon and other dinosaur fossils turn up. Open houses on the 1st and 3rd Saturdays let visitors search with staff; finds stay with the park.

name: Discovery Village
desc: County-owned waterfront site on Atwell Road in Shady Side, listed as a cartop launch for canoes and kayaks. Sunrise to sunset.

name: Dogwood Harbor, Tilghman Island
desc: Working harbor just past the Knapps Narrows drawbridge, home port to some of the last skipjacks that dredge oysters under sail. Watermen unload crabs and oysters at the docks.

name: Double Rock Park
desc: 102-acre county park in Parkville with wooded hiking loops; the blue trail follows Stemmers Run to the small Double Rock waterfall that gives the park its name. Take care at stream crossings.

name: Douglas Point Special Recreation Management Area
desc: Federal and state forest on the Potomac with two easy woodland trails, one ending at a secluded river beach and one passing the ruins of the 18th-century Chiles homesite.

name: Doves Landing Park
desc: Wooded county park inside a bend of the Occoquan River south of Manassas. Natural-surface trails lead to quiet riverbank spots for fishing and sitting by the water.

name: Dundee Creek Marina (Gunpowder Falls State Park)
desc: State-run marina and boat ramp on Dundee Creek next to the Hammerman Area, the put-in for paddling the tidal marshes of Dundee and Saltpeter creeks toward Marshy Point.

name: DuPont Environmental Education Center
desc: Four-story glass building and a quarter-mile boardwalk loop over a 212-acre tidal marsh at the edge of downtown Wilmington. Beavers, herons and eagles within sight of I-95.

name: Dupont Underground
desc: Curved streetcar station and tunnels under Dupont Circle, shut when the trolleys stopped in 1962 and reused as an art space. Entry only with a ticket for an exhibit, event or tour; entrance on 19th St NW.

facts.access: Open by guided tour or by arrangement only. Check before you go.

name: Eagle Rock (Smoke Hole)
desc: Tall fin of rock rising straight from the South Branch beside Smoke Hole Road, with a deep pool at its base. An easy pull-off inside the canyon.

name: Eagle Rock (Tuscarora Trail)
desc: Ridge walk north from VA/WV Route 55 past radio towers to a cliff-top view of Massanutten and the Blue Ridge. Part of the trail crosses hunt-club land on an easement; stay on it.

name: Eastham Park and Front Royal Boat Landing
desc: Town park on the South Fork Shenandoah with about a mile of paved riverside path, a public boat launch and a dog park.

name: Eden Mill Nature Center
desc: Historic grist mill and dam on Deer Creek with a nature center, a canoe and kayak launch and wooded creekside trails.

name: Edith J. Carrier Arboretum
desc: 125-acre wooded preserve and gardens on the James Madison University campus, with a pond and forest paths. Open dawn to dusk every day.

name: Edward H. McCabe Preserve
desc: Nature Conservancy preserve on the Broadkill River with two-plus miles of easy trails through upland forest to the river's edge and a stand of Atlantic white cedar.

name: Edwards Ferry (Lock 25)
desc: Remote canal access west of Poolesville with a boat ramp on the Potomac, the restored Lock 25 lockhouse and the brick shell of an old store. Long, empty towpath stretches in both directions.

name: Edwards Ferry: Jarboe's Store Ruins and Lock 25
desc: Roofless brick shell of a canal-side store next to Lock 25 and its lockhouse on the C&O Canal, at a former Potomac ferry crossing. At the end of Edwards Ferry Rd by the boat ramp; free. The lockhouse is a rental, not open.

name: Elk Neck State Forest
desc: About 3,500 acres of quiet oak and pine forest between North East and Elkton with miles of sandy forest roads and trails, including a stretch of the Mason-Dixon Trail.

name: Elkhorn Lake
desc: Quiet reservoir (Staunton's water supply) with a day-use area for non-motorized boating and fishing, including a wheelchair-accessible pier. Near Todd Lake and the North River Gorge.

name: Elktonia-Carr's Beach Heritage Park
desc: Five bay-front acres bought by Annapolis in 2022, the last piece of the Black beach resorts that hosted major music acts under segregation. A quarter-mile path from the Maritime Museum park reaches the sand.

name: Ellanor C. Lawrence Park
desc: 650 acres of stream-valley woods and meadows in Chantilly, with Walney Pond, an 18th-century farmhouse visitor center, dairy and ice-house remains and several miles of loop trails.

name: Ellen O. Moyer Nature Park at Back Creek
desc: Twelve-acre waterfront park on Back Creek run with the Annapolis Maritime Museum: short paths, a living shoreline, piers and a kayak launch. Start of the walking path to Elktonia-Carr's Beach.

name: Ellwood Manor and Stonewall Jackson's Arm
desc: 1790s plantation house on the Wilderness battlefield whose family cemetery holds a stone marker for the amputated left arm of Stonewall Jackson, buried here in May 1863.

name: Emory Landing Campsite
desc: Paddle-in campsite in Emory Waters Nature Preserve at Jug Bay with a tent pad, table and fire ring. Mud flats block it except near high tide, so approach from the south. No pets.

name: Endless Caverns
desc: Show cave at the foot of Massanutten, three miles south of New Market, seen on 75-minute guided tours. On the grounds of an RV resort; check current hours before going.

name: Exorcist Steps
desc: Steep 75-step stone staircase between Prospect Street and M Street in Georgetown, used in the 1973 film The Exorcist. A plaque marks the spot; locals run repeats on it.

name: Fairfax Stone State Park
desc: Boundary stone at the spring where the North Branch of the Potomac begins, first set in 1746 to settle the limits of Lord Fairfax's land grant.

name: Falls Ridge Waterfall
desc: Circuit on North Mountain with an unmarked, hard-to-follow side path to a 30-foot waterfall against a 60-foot cliff. Forest Road 252 is open only Apr 1-May 21 and Aug 1-Dec 31.

name: Falmouth Beach (Historic Port of Falmouth Park)
desc: Sandy bank on the Rappahannock just below the fall line, across from Fredericksburg. Wading, fishing and kayak landing; currents and drop-offs here are dangerous, so life jackets are strongly advised.

name: Fenwick Island Lighthouse and Transpeninsular Marker
desc: An 1859 lighthouse stranded among beach houses on the Maryland line. At its foot sits the 1751 stone that starts the Transpeninsular Line, carved with the Calvert and Penn arms.

name: Ferncliff Wildlife and Wildflower Preserve
desc: Old woods road following Barnes Run down a steep ravine to the Susquehanna. A Lancaster Conservancy preserve known for spring wildflowers and ferns.

name: Finzel Swamp Preserve
desc: Nature Conservancy wetland at the head of the Savage River with tamarack and other northern holdovers. A trail crosses the swamp on short wooden bridges to a shallow pond.

name: Fire Control Tower 3
desc: One of the cylindrical concrete WWII spotting towers built for Fort Miles' guns, standing in the dunes at Tower Road beach in Delaware Seashore State Park between Dewey and Indian River Inlet. Exterior only; park fee.

facts.access: You can only look at this one from outside (road, trail or water). The site itself is closed or fenced.

name: Fleming Park
desc: 16-acre waterfront park on Bear Creek in historic Turner Station with a new lighted fishing pier and an accessible walking path.

name: Flying Point Park
desc: County waterfront park on the Bush River in Edgewood with a boat launch, a playground, pavilions and a short trail.

name: Foamhenge
desc: Full-size styrofoam replica of Stonehenge, moved from Natural Bridge to Cox Farms in 2017. Access is limited: included with Fall Festival admission, or by free shuttle 1-2 pm on summer Saturdays.

facts.fee: Fall Festival admission, or free on Smokin' Saturdays (Apr-Aug)

name: Font Hill Wetland Park
desc: Small suburban wetland park with ponds, boardwalks and paved paths. An easy spot for herons, turtles and dragonflies.

name: Ford Campsite at Stocketts Run
desc: County paddle-in campsite on the Patuxent River near Harwood: one tent pad, picnic table and fire ring, reached only by canoe or kayak. Reserve ahead; two-night maximum, up to six people.

name: Fort Bedford Museum
desc: Fort Bedford was a French and Indian War-era British military fortification located at the present site of Bedford, Pennsylvania. The fort was a star-shaped log fortress erected in the summer of 1758.

name: Fort C.F. Smith Park
desc: Quiet Arlington park preserving the earthworks of an 1863 fort, with a meadow, old trees and an early-1900s house. Good for a short walk and birding close to Rosslyn.

name: Fort DeRussy
desc: Overgrown parapet and ditch of a Civil War fort built in 1861 on a hilltop in Rock Creek Park. Reached by a short dirt path through the woods off the trail near Oregon Ave and Military Rd NW. Free.

name: Fort Dupont Park
desc: 376 wooded acres east of the Anacostia with the earthworks of a Civil War fort, picnic groves and the Fort Circle hiker-biker trail, a 7-mile path linking the ridge-top fort sites.

name: Fort DuPont State Park
desc: Former Army post beside the Delaware River and the canal mouth, with overgrown concrete gun batteries and a riverside trail that looks across to Fort Delaware.

name: Fort Foote Park
desc: Wooded earthworks of an 1863 river fort with two 15-inch Rodman cannons still on the parapet. A path drops down the bluff to a small, usually empty beach on the Potomac.

name: Fort Hunt Park
desc: Loop road and picnic groves around concrete gun batteries from the Spanish-American War era. During WWII it was the secret interrogation camp known as P.O. Box 1142.

name: Fort Hunt Park Batteries
desc: Concrete coast-defense batteries of a Spanish-American War era fort scattered around a picnic park off the George Washington Parkway; also the site of a secret WWII interrogation center. Free, open dawn to dusk year-round.

name: Fort Hunter Mansion and Park
desc: Riverside county park around a stone mansion, with big old trees and a view upstream to the Rockville Bridge, the longest stone-arch railroad viaduct ever built.

name: Fort Marcy
desc: Earthworks and cannon of an 1861 fort that guarded Chain Bridge, in quiet woods reached only from the northbound GW Parkway. A short path connects to the Potomac Heritage Trail.

name: Fort Mill Ridge Civil War Trenches
desc: Well-preserved Civil War trenches on a wooded ridge above the South Branch, dug to guard the approaches to Romney. Short interpretive loop.

name: Fort Reno Park
desc: Grassy hilltop in Tenleytown holding the highest natural point in DC, 409 ft, marked by a small survey disc near the water towers. Site of a Civil War fort; free summer concerts.

name: Fort Ritchie
desc: Army post closed in 1998, known for its castle-style stone buildings and the WWII 'Ritchie Boys' intelligence school. Being reopened as a village with a museum and shops around the lakes; streets are open, interiors vary.

name: Fort Ward Park
desc: Best-preserved of the Civil War forts that ringed Washington, with a rebuilt Northwest Bastion mounting cannon, original earthwork walls, a small museum and a shaded loop road for walking.

name: Fort Windham Rocks
desc: Short AT walk north from Compton Gap to a cluster of split greenstone outcrops, remnants of ancient lava flows, sitting in the woods beside the Dickey Ridge Trail.

name: Founders Park (Old Town waterfront)
desc: Grassy riverfront park at the north end of Old Town's waterfront walk. Benches face east over the Potomac for sunrise; paths continue to Oronoco Bay Park and the Mount Vernon Trail.

name: Fountain Rock Lime Kilns
desc: Row of stone lime kilns and a spring-fed quarry pond left from a lime works, now a small county park and nature center. Level paths around the kilns; free.

name: Fountain Rock Park
desc: Row of old stone lime kilns beside a spring-fed quarry pond, with a small nature center. A short, flat walk.

name: Four Locks (C&O Canal)
desc: Four lift locks in a row where the canal cut across a river bend, with a lockhouse, mule barn and boat ramp left from the canal community that stood here.

name: Fowler Beach
desc: Undeveloped bay beach at the end of a road across the Prime Hook marsh, rebuilt after storms breached it. No houses or facilities; parts close in spring and summer for nesting shorebirds.

name: Fox Hollow Trail
desc: 1.2 mi loop from Dickey Ridge Visitor Center (Skyline Drive mile 4.6) through the Fox family's farm: long stone piles cleared from fields, a walled family cemetery and a spring box in regrown woods. Park entry fee.

name: Fox Point State Park
desc: Narrow strip of reclaimed industrial shoreline on the Delaware River with a paved path, lawns and benches for watching ships head to and from Philadelphia.

name: Foxcatcher Farms Covered Bridge (Fair Hill)
desc: Red 1860 covered bridge over Big Elk Creek inside Fair Hill, one of only two historic covered bridges left in Cecil County. Trails lead out from the parking area by the bridge.

name: Foxstone Park
desc: Small wooded neighborhood park in Vienna whose footbridge was a dead-drop site used by FBI agent Robert Hanssen, arrested here in February 2001 after spying for Moscow for two decades.

name: Franklin Point State Park
desc: Undeveloped 477-acre peninsula between the Bay, Deep Creek and Flag Pond with volunteer-built trails and a shallow soft launch. Gated with a combination lock: request the code from DNR first.

name: Frazier Discovery Trail (Loft Mountain)
desc: Short loop from Loft Mountain Wayside up to rock ledges with wide views west over the South District, passing under an overhanging cliff.

name: Frederick Douglass National Historic Site (Cedar Hill)
desc: Douglass's hilltop house in Anacostia. The front lawn looks across the river to the Capitol dome and Washington Monument; grounds are free to walk and the house is seen by ranger tour.

name: Frederick Douglass Park on the Tuckahoe
desc: County park on Tuckahoe Creek near the farm where Frederick Douglass was born, with overlooks across the creek marsh and signs on his early life.

name: Fredericksburg Battlefield: Sunken Road and Marye's Heights
desc: Walk the restored Sunken Road and its original stone wall section, then climb Marye's Heights through the national cemetery for a view over town. Free; visitor center at the foot of the hill.

name: Fredericksburg Quarry Trails
desc: Network of natural-surface trails along the Rappahannock upstream of town, used by hikers and mountain bikers. Rock ledges and river access points; small lot at Normandy Ave and Fall Hill Ave.

name: Freeland Boardwalk (Canaan Valley National Wildlife Refuge)
desc: Half-mile boardwalk loop over beaver ponds and wet meadows on the valley floor. Good for birds and for a flat walk after a hard hike.

name: Fresh Pond (Delaware Seashore State Park)
desc: Wooded tract north of Bethany with more than five miles of flat trails on crushed stone, boardwalk and packed earth around a freshwater pond.

name: Friendship Farm Park
desc: County park on a bluff over Nanjemoy Creek: two loops totalling nearly 4 miles of field and forest trail with observation decks, plus a boat ramp for paddling the creek.

name: Gaithersburg Latitude Observatory
desc: Small white hut with a roll-off roof, one of six observatories built on the same latitude around the world in 1899 to measure the wobble of Earth's axis. Stands in a neighborhood park; exterior only.

name: Galesville Wharf
desc: County pier at the end of Galesville's main street on the West River, with a cartop launch and room to fish or sit and watch the boats. Sunrise to sunset.

name: George Island Landing
desc: Remote landing at the end of a marsh road on lower Chincoteague Bay, next to a seafood dock. Launch a kayak or just watch the light on miles of open salt marsh.

name: Georgetown Waterfront Park
desc: Riverside lawn, steps and promenade on the Potomac below Georgetown. West-facing views to Key Bridge and Roosevelt Island at sunset; rowers and kayaks pass close by. Joins the Capital Crescent Trail.

name: Germany Valley Overlook
desc: Pull-off on US 33 climbing North Fork Mountain, looking across the farms and limestone ridges of Germany Valley toward Spruce Mountain.

name: Gilbert Run Park
desc: Wooded county park around the 60-acre Wheatley Lake with a two-mile lakeside trail, fishing piers and seasonal canoe and pedal-boat rentals.

name: Gilpin's Falls Covered Bridge
desc: Maryland's longest surviving covered bridge, a 119-foot Burr arch span from 1860 beside MD 272. North East Creek tumbles over a rocky cascade just below; roadside parking, no formal trail to the falls.

name: Glen Echo Park
desc: Former amusement park (closed 1968) kept as an arts park: Art Deco entrance and arcade, a 1921 Dentzel carousel that runs in summer, the Spanish Ballroom and artist studios. Free to walk.

name: Glenn Dale Hospital
desc: Tuberculosis sanatorium of 23 buildings on 216 acres, built 1934 and closed 1981 for asbestos. Posted and regularly patrolled by Park Police, so going in is trespassing; the brick blocks are seen from Glenn Dale Rd.

facts.access: You can only look at this one from outside (road, trail or water). The site itself is closed or fenced.

name: Glover-Archbold Park
desc: Narrow wooded stream valley running north from near Georgetown toward Tenleytown, with a dirt trail under big tulip trees. NPS has the trail's southern end under emergency closure (detour via Foxhall Rd).

name: Godey Lime Kilns
desc: Two stone lime kiln stacks left from a lime works built in 1864 and run until 1907, marooned beside the Rock Creek Parkway ramps at 27th and L St NW. Partly restored in the 1960s; seen from the sidewalk and trail.

name: Gold Mine Loop and Maryland Mine ruins
desc: Wooded loop on the bluff above Great Falls Tavern passing trenches, shafts and building remains of the Maryland Mine, which worked gold-bearing quartz here off and on from 1867 to 1939.

name: Goose Creek Stone Bridge
desc: Four-arch, 200-foot stone turnpike bridge built about 1810, bypassed by US 50 and now closed to cars. Cavalry fought across it on June 21, 1863. Short walk from a small lot.

name: Governor Bridge Natural Area
desc: Former sand and gravel pits on the Patuxent east of Bowie, now ponds, meadows and woods with informal trails and a canoe launch on the river. Quiet birding spot.

name: Great Marsh Park
desc: City park on a point in the Choptank River with a boat launch, fishing piers, picnic tables and an open western horizon over the water.

name: Green Haven Wharf
desc: Small county wharf at the end of Outing Avenue in Green Haven, listed by the county as a cartop launch for canoes and kayaks. Sunrise to sunset.

name: Green Ridge State Forest Headquarters Overlook
desc: Wooden platform behind the forest headquarters just off I-68 with a first look across the ridges. Pick up the overlook driving map and campsite permits here.

name: Green Spring Gardens
desc: Fairfax County's public garden: demonstration beds, a glasshouse, a 1784 house, native woodland and two small ponds in a stream valley. Free.

name: Greenbelt Park
desc: National Park Service forest 12 miles from the Mall. The 5.3-mile Perimeter Trail circles the park through pine and oak woods, with three shorter loops and a large campground.

name: Greenbury Point Radio Towers
desc: Three 600 ft lattice towers of 1938, all that stands of the Navy's NSS Annapolis transmitter station, on a peninsula across the Severn from Annapolis. Flat trails on Navy land; closed whenever the firing range is in use, so check first.

name: Greenland Gap Preserve
desc: Deep gap through New Creek Mountain ringed by sandstone cliffs about 800 ft above the creek. A Nature Conservancy preserve with no maintained trails; two rough paths climb to the cliff tops.

name: Greenwood Furnace
desc: Stone furnace stack of an ironworks that went into blast in 1834, with a church, blacksmith shop and cemetery left from its vanished company town. State park with a self-guided historic walk; free.

name: Guard Shore
desc: Narrow, undeveloped public beach on the Chesapeake at the end of Guard Shore Road, with shallow water, marsh behind it and no facilities. Often empty.

name: Guilford Quarry Pratt Truss Bridge
desc: Small iron railroad truss built in 1902 to reach the Guilford granite quarries, now a footbridge on the Patuxent Branch Trail between Savage and Lake Elkhorn.

name: Gunston Hall
desc: George Mason's 1755 brick house with a restored boxwood garden on a terrace above the Potomac. Trails lead through woods to the river shore. Admission covers house and grounds.

name: Gwynns Falls Trail
desc: 15-mile greenway trail following the Gwynns Falls stream valley from the I-70 park-and-ride through Leakin Park to the Middle Branch and Inner Harbor.

name: Hagerstown City Park
desc: City park around a spring-fed lake with swans, a walking loop, an art museum and a steam locomotive on display.

name: Hallowing Point Waterfront Park
desc: Small state waterfront site on the Patuxent beside the Benedict bridge: two boat ramps, a kayak launch and a sandy strip of shoreline for fishing and picnicking. Open sunrise to sunset.

name: Hammonds Rocks
desc: Cluster of quartzite outcrops on the crest of South Mountain right beside Ridge Road. Scramble up for views north over the Cumberland Valley.

name: Hampton National Historic Site
desc: 1790 Georgian mansion that was once among the largest houses in America, with terraced formal gardens falling away below it and a farm side with stone slave quarters. Grounds are free.

name: Hancock's Resolution
desc: 1785 stone farmhouse and farm on the Bodkin peninsula, described as the oldest structure in Maryland north of the Severn River. Open Sundays 1-4 p.m., late March to late October.

name: Hanging Rocks
desc: Vertical cliffs rising nearly 300 ft from the South Branch Potomac where WV 28 and the railroad squeeze past, four miles north of Romney.

name: Harbor Wetland at the National Aquarium
desc: Floating salt-marsh habitat of about 10,000 square feet moored between Piers 3 and 4 at the Inner Harbor, opened in 2024. Free walkways pass over tidal marsh grasses planted to draw crabs, fish and birds.

name: Harpers Ferry Armory Site and Bridge Piers at The Point
desc: Most of the US Musket Factory lies under the 1890s rail embankment; what shows is the excavated Smith and Forging Shop (1848), John Brown's Fort and, from The Point, the stone piers of washed-out bridges standing in both rivers.

name: Harry and Jeanette Weinberg Park
desc: Wooded county park off Fairview Beach Road with walking trails and shoreline fishing, open dawn to dusk. A kayak launch and swimming beach were still under county review; closes some fall mornings for deer management.

name: Hazel Mountain Overlook
desc: Southeast view at 2,770 ft from a rounded granodiorite outcrop you can walk out on, toward Hazel Mountain. Popular for sunrise.

name: Helen Avalynne Tawes Garden
desc: Free five-acre garden at the Department of Natural Resources headquarters that recreates Maryland landscapes in miniature, from a western mountain forest to an Eastern Shore peninsula, around ponds.

name: Hemlock Overlook Regional Park
desc: Hemlock-shaded bluffs above Bull Run near Clifton. A short descent reaches the Bull Run-Occoquan Trail for out-and-back walks along the water in either direction.

name: Hemlocks Natural Area
desc: 120 acres of old-growth hemlock in a narrow ravine of Tuscarora State Forest, a National Natural Landmark. Trails follow Patterson Run under the big trees.

name: Henry Clay Furnace (Coopers Rock)
desc: Lone stone iron furnace in the woods of Coopers Rock State Forest; nothing else of the furnace village survives. Reached by the Clay Furnace Trail, roughly 1 mi each way downhill from the main forest road. Free.

name: Henry Clay Iron Furnace
desc: Stone furnace 30 ft square and 30 ft high, built in 1834-36, standing alone in the woods of Coopers Rock State Forest at the end of a downhill trail.

name: Herring Creek Nature Park
desc: County nature park with an easy loop path through meadow and woods to an overlook on Herring Creek, minutes from the Route 50 strip.

name: Herring Run Park
desc: 375 acres of wooded stream valley in northeast Baltimore, with paved and dirt paths following Herring Run for 2.3 miles and a connector to the Lake Montebello loop.

name: Hidden Rocks (Hone Quarry)
desc: Short trail across Rocky Run to a small waterfall and tall rock walls used by climbers, with a scramble route to a valley view from the top.

name: Hidden Valley Natural Area (Rocks State Park)
desc: Undeveloped piece of Rocks State Park nine miles north of the main park, where Carea and Telegraph roads meet Deer Creek: a creekside trail, fishing, wading and tubing. Lot for 8-10 cars, no facilities.

name: Hightop Mountain
desc: Appalachian Trail climb from mile 66.7 up a ridge to a rocky viewpoint at about 3,300 ft, looking south and west over the South District ridges.

name: Hillwood Estate gardens
desc: Marjorie Merriweather Post's estate above Rock Creek, with 13 acres of formal gardens: Japanese-style garden, French parterre, rose garden and an orchid greenhouse. Closed Mondays.

name: Historic Sotterley
desc: Early-1700s Tidewater plantation above the Patuxent with an original slave cabin, colonial garden and several miles of trails through fields and woods down to the river.

name: Hog Rock (Catoctin Mountain Park)
desc: Rock ledge overlook a short walk from the Hog Rock lot on Park Central Road, on a loop trail through big hardwoods. An easy fall-color stop.

facts.dogs: leashed; not allowed on the rock formations

name: Hogback Mountain Loop
desc: North District loop over Hogback and Little Hogback on the Appalachian Trail, with views west to Massanutten, returning through laurel on side trails.

name: Holtwood Dam and Face Rock Overlook
desc: Overlook down onto Holtwood Dam, built 1905-10 and the oldest of the three big dams on the lower Susquehanna, and the scoured bedrock below it.

name: Homeport Farm Park
desc: Small gated county park with a cartop launch onto Church Creek off the South River. Request the free gate code from the county portal before visiting.

name: Homer Gudelsky Park
desc: Small sandy beach on the West Ocean City side of the inlet, known locally as Stinky Beach, looking straight across at the boardwalk and the boats heading out to sea.

name: Hone Quarry Falls
desc: Walk up a rutted forest road and trail past Hone Quarry Reservoir to a secluded waterfall (15 to 25 ft, depending on the source) with smaller ledge falls. High clearance helps on the access road.

name: Hone Quarry Recreation Area
desc: Streamside Forest Service campground and free picnic shelter in a narrow hollow west of Harrisonburg, a mile below Hone Quarry Reservoir. Trails lead to climbing rocks, ridges and a waterfall.

name: Hoopersville (end of Hoopers Island Road)
desc: Watermen's village on Middle Hooper Island where the public road gives out, most of an hour from Cambridge. The last stretch crosses a causeway with the Bay lapping at both shoulders.

name: Horn Point Park
desc: Small city park at Horn Point, the northeast tip of Eastport, facing the mouth of Annapolis harbor and the Naval Academy seawall across Spa Creek. A place to sit and watch boats come in.

name: House Rock and Wind Cave (Clark Nature Preserve)
desc: Conestoga Trail climb from Pequea to House Rock's view over the Susquehanna, passing Wind Cave, a fracture cave in the hillside. The return trip involves a lot of up and down.

name: Howard County Conservancy at Mt. Pleasant
desc: 232-acre 18th-century farm kept as a nature preserve, with mowed and wooded trails through meadows and along streams, native-plant gardens and a nature center. Grounds open daily, free.

name: Howard P. Rawlings Conservatory
desc: 1888 glass palm house in Druid Hill Park with orchid, tropical, Mediterranean and desert rooms and outdoor flower beds. A warm green stop in winter.

name: Howard Tunnel (Heritage Rail Trail)
desc: 275-ft brick-lined railroad tunnel in use since 1838, the second-oldest active rail tunnel in the country. The rail trail runs through it beside the track.

name: Ice Mountain Preserve
desc: Talus slope whose vents breathe cold air all summer, keeping ice into the warm months and sheltering northern plants. Visits are guided only: book a Nature Conservancy docent hike weeks ahead.

name: Idylwild Wildlife Management Area
desc: More than 3,000 acres of sandy pine-oak forest and swamp along Marshyhope Creek, with unpaved lanes for walking. Managed for hunting, so wear orange in season.

name: Indian River Life-Saving Station
desc: Restored 1876 station of the U.S. Life-Saving Service, standing alone in the dunes beside Route 1 with its surfboat and breeches-buoy gear. Small museum; beach across the dune.

name: Indian Steps Museum
desc: Riverside cabin from the early 1900s with thousands of Native American artifacts set into its walls, on wooded grounds beside the Susquehanna. Limited seasonal hours.

name: Indigo Tunnel
desc: Longest tunnel of the Western Maryland Railway, built 1904 and abandoned 1975. Closed to the public to protect bats; the Western Maryland Rail Trail leaves the grade at each portal for a 2 mi bypass on the C&O towpath.

facts.access: You can only look at this one from outside (road, trail or water). The site itself is closed or fenced.

name: Iron Hill Ore Pits
desc: Wooded hill pocked with old open iron-ore pits, crossed by the trails of Iron Hill Park and the Mason-Dixon Trail; a small museum sits nearby. County park off Old Baltimore Pike; free.

name: Irvine Nature Center
desc: Nonprofit nature center on more than 200 acres of meadow, woods and wetland in the Caves Valley, with easy walking trails and a nature museum.

name: Isle of Wight Nature Park
desc: Quiet county park on a marsh island where Route 90 crosses to Ocean City, with two piers, a canoe and kayak launch and picnic tables on the St. Martin River.

name: Ivy Creek Natural Area
desc: 219 acres of woods and fields on the South Fork Rivanna Reservoir with seven miles of quiet trails and the historic River View Farm. No pets, jogging or bikes. Dawn to dusk.

name: Jack Creek Park
desc: 60-acre natural area with trails and 3,000 feet of shoreline on Jack Creek and the Chesapeake Bay, plus a cartop launch. Gated: get the free code from the county portal. No swimming.

name: Jarrett Falls and Meadow Grounds Lake
desc: Trail from the dam of a 204-acre mountain lake on State Game Lands 53 down Roaring Run to a set of waterfalls.

name: Jennings Randolph Lake: Waffle Rock and West Virginia Overlook
desc: Boulder with a raised waffle-grid pattern weathered into the sandstone, displayed at the Corps of Engineers overlook above the 952-acre lake on the North Branch Potomac.

name: Jeremys Run and Knob Mountain
desc: Circuit from Elkwallow Wayside into the Jeremys Run drainage, a trout stream with many crossings and small pools. A longer 14-mile loop reaches the waterfall near the lower end.

name: John Dickinson Plantation
desc: Boyhood home of John Dickinson, "Penman of the Revolution": a 1740 brick mansion and rebuilt farm buildings in open fields near the St. Jones River. Free state museum.

name: Jones Falls Trail
desc: Paved city trail up the Jones Falls valley, about 8 miles from the Inner Harbor through Druid Hill Park and Woodberry to Cylburn Arboretum, with a later extension toward Mount Washington.

name: Jones Run Falls
desc: Out-and-back from Jones Run parking (mile 84.1) through quiet South District forest to a 42-foot waterfall over a mossy cliff.

name: Kaylor's Knob (Massanutten Ridge Trail)
desc: Easy ridge-line walk on the Massanutten Resort trail system with occasional valley views. Free parking; trails are closed in daylight Nov 1-Jan 8 for hunting, except Sundays.

name: Kelly's Ford (C.F. Phelps WMA)
desc: Rappahannock River crossing with a canoe ramp and parking on the Culpeper side, in a 4,539-acre wildlife area. Site of the March 1863 cavalry battle. Access permit or VA license needed age 17+.

facts.fee: DWR access permit or VA hunting/fishing license required

name: Kendall Ghost Town
desc: Site of a 19th-century logging town on the Youghiogheny; today mostly stone foundations in the woods. Reached by the flat Kendall Trail on the old rail grade upstream from Friendsville, about 2 mi each way.

name: Kepler Overlook
desc: Climb from Cedar Creek near the Van Buren Furnace over Tea Mountain to a ledge on Little North Mountain. Van Buren Road is gated from late fall to early spring, which adds walking.

name: Key Bridge Boathouse
desc: Seasonal kayak, canoe and paddleboard rentals on the Georgetown shore under Key Bridge. Paddle upstream to the Three Sisters rocks or circle Theodore Roosevelt Island.

name: Killiansburg Cave (C&O Canal)
desc: Shallow cave in the bluff above the towpath where Sharpsburg civilians sheltered during the Battle of Antietam. Reached by walking the towpath from Snyders Landing.

name: Kingman and Heritage Islands
desc: Two wooded man-made islands in the Anacostia reached by wooden footbridges from the RFK lots. Flat trails and river overlooks with herons, ospreys and turtles; quiet on weekdays.

name: Kitts Hummock
desc: Tiny bayfront community with a public beach access at the end of the road: two parking spaces, no facilities, and horseshoe crabs along the tide line in late spring.

name: Lake Accotink Park
desc: Loop trail of about 4 miles around a small lake, passing the dam spillway and under a tall railroad trestle. Part of the Cross County Trail; marina rentals in season.

name: Lake Arrowhead (Luray)
desc: Town of Luray's reservoir park at the foot of the Blue Ridge: white-sand swimming beach with lifeguards in summer, boat rentals and a 1.4-mile trail around the lake.

facts.fee: Beach fee in summer; open Memorial Day to Labor Day

name: Lake Frank (Rock Creek Regional Park)
desc: Undeveloped lake ringed by a loop trail of mixed pavement and dirt. No boating or facilities on the water; herons along the shore and Meadowside Nature Center on the east side.

name: Lake Kittamaqundi
desc: Downtown Columbia's lakefront: a paved loop around the 27-acre lake past the People Tree plaza, fountains and a wooded far shore.

name: Lake Needwood (Rock Creek Regional Park)
desc: 75-acre lake with seasonal boat rentals and shoreline trails. It is the northern end of the paved Rock Creek Trail, which runs 14 miles downstream to the DC line.

name: Lake Ridge Marina (Occoquan Reservoir)
desc: County marina on the Occoquan Reservoir with seasonal boat rentals, a boat ramp and a fishing pier. Calm, wooded shoreline to paddle in either direction.

name: Lancaster County Central Park
desc: Large county park on the Conestoga River at the edge of Lancaster, with wooded trails, a garden of five senses and a covered bridge.

name: Lands Run Falls
desc: Fire-road walk from mile 9.2 to a string of cascades dropping about 80 feet into a small gorge. Only worth it after rain; it can be dry in summer.

name: Laurel Lake (Pine Grove Furnace State Park)
desc: The larger of the park's two lakes, with a sand beach, boat rentals and Pole Steeple's cliff visible above the far shore.

name: LaVale Toll Gate House
desc: Seven-sided brick toll house built in 1835-36 on the National Road. A quick roadside stop.

name: LBJ Memorial Grove (Lady Bird Johnson Park)
desc: White pine grove and a pink granite monolith on Columbia Island, with open views across the Potomac to the monuments. Flat paths, the Mount Vernon Trail alongside and daffodils in spring.

name: Leesylvania Ruins and Freestone Point Battery
desc: Lee's Woods Trail loops past the site of the Lee family's Leesylvania house, the chimney and walls of the Fairfax house and a Confederate gun battery on Freestone Point over the Potomac. State park fee.

name: Leonardtown Wharf Park
desc: Small town park on Breton Bay at the foot of Washington Street with a promenade, benches, docks and a kayak launch.

name: Leopold's Preserve
desc: Privately owned conservation land open to the public daily, with miles of flat trails through wetlands, meadows and woods beside a housing development near Haymarket.

name: Liberty Dam and Reservoir
desc: Baltimore's 1954 water-supply reservoir on the North Branch of the Patapsco. Fire roads through the forested watershed serve as hiking trails, and the concrete dam's spillway is worth seeing after rain.

name: Limberlost Trail
desc: Level, wheelchair-accessible crushed-greenstone loop through mountain laurel (blooms in June), with a boardwalk, a bridge and a small outcrop of columnar jointing.

name: Little Buffalo State Park
desc: 923-acre park around Holman Lake with a covered bridge, a restored working grist mill, a swimming pool and lakeside trails.

name: Little Creek Wildlife Area Observation Tower
desc: Short boardwalk to a two-level observation deck over a broad impoundment of the Little Creek Wildlife Area. One of the easiest places on the bayshore to scan for waterfowl and shorebirds.

facts.fee: Delaware Conservation Access Pass or fishing/hunting license needed to park

name: Loch Raven Dam
desc: Stepped concrete dam from 1914 holding back Loch Raven Reservoir, with a roadside viewing area on Loch Raven Drive where water sheets down the spillway into the Gunpowder.

name: Loch Raven Fishing Center
desc: County boat dock on Loch Raven Reservoir renting rowboats, kayaks and electric-motor boats, the only way onto the water without your own permitted boat. Daily April to Labor Day, then Fri-Mon through October.

name: Lock 33 and Lockhouse 33 Ruins
desc: Stone shell of C&O Canal Lockhouse 33 and the dry lock beside it, at the Maryland end of the footbridge from Harpers Ferry's Lower Town, under the Maryland Heights cliffs. Flat, a few minutes' walk; also the start of the heights trail.

name: Loft Mountain Campground
desc: 207 sites on top of Big Flat Mountain at mile 79.5, with views both east and west from the campground loop and trails into the Big Run wilderness. Open spring to early November.

name: Lonaconing Iron Furnace
desc: Sandstone furnace stack 50 ft high that first made iron in 1839, standing in a small park in the middle of town.

name: Lorton Prison Beehive Brick Kiln
desc: Domed brick kiln surviving from the Lorton prison brickyard, where inmates made bricks for the prison and DC buildings; preserved with signs in Occoquan Regional Park on the Occoquan River. Free.

name: Lorton Workhouse and Reformatory
desc: Brick dormitories and yards of the District of Columbia's former Lorton prison complex, where suffragists were held in 1917. Reused as the Workhouse Arts Center with a small prison museum; grounds are free to walk.

name: Loys Station Covered Bridge
desc: Covered bridge over Owens Creek, rebuilt with its surviving timbers after a 1991 arson fire, set in a small park with picnic tables and creek access.

name: Luray Hawksbill Greenway
desc: Paved path along Hawksbill Creek through the middle of Luray, with footbridges and benches. An easy leg-stretch or run between cavern and Skyline Drive stops.

name: Luray Singing Tower
desc: A stone carillon tower (the Belle Brown Northcott Memorial) in a small park across from Luray Caverns; free recitals are played on its bells on a seasonal schedule.

name: Manayunk Bridge
desc: Curving open-spandrel concrete arch viaduct of the Pennsylvania Railroad high over the Schuylkill, closed to trains in 1986 and reopened as a trail linking the Cynwyd Heritage Trail to Manayunk. Free.

name: Marietta Furnace Ruins
desc: Chimney, walls and foundations of the anthracite iron furnaces that lined the river below Chickies Rock, in a small furnace park with a signed path off Furnace Rd by the Northwest River Trail. Museum in the old office, limited hours.

name: Mariner Point Park
desc: County park on a peninsula in the tidal Gunpowder River at Joppatowne with a boat launch, a playground and a short waterside trail.

name: Marshall Hall
desc: Brick shell of an early-1700s plantation house on the Potomac, later an amusement park, now part of the National Park Service's Piscataway Park. Boat ramp and river view across to Mount Vernon.

name: Martic Forge Trestle (Enola Low Grade Trail)
desc: Long rail-trail bridge crossing high above Pequea Creek and the road at Martic Forge.

name: Martin's Mill Covered Bridge
desc: 205-ft Town lattice truss covered bridge built in 1849 over Conococheague Creek, in a small township park open dawn to dusk.

name: Martinak State Park
desc: Small wooded park where Watts Creek joins the Choptank River: a couple of miles of easy trails, fishing pier, boat ramp and campground under tall hardwoods.

name: Martinsburg B&O Roundhouse
desc: Post-Civil War B&O shops with the oldest covered roundhouse in the US, where the 1877 rail strike began; a second roundhouse survives only as outer walls. Seen from the station footbridge; inside by tours and events.

facts.access: Open by guided tour or by arrangement only. Check before you go.

name: Mason Neck National Wildlife Refuge: Woodmarsh and Great Marsh trails
desc: First national refuge created for bald eagles (1969). Woodmarsh Trail loops 3 miles through forest to marsh overlooks; the paved Great Marsh Trail runs 0.75 mile to a view over the Potomac marsh.

name: Mason-Dixon Line marker (Great Allegheny Passage)
desc: The Maryland-Pennsylvania border marked across the rail trail with stone blocks, between Frostburg and Big Savage Tunnel, with a long view down the valley.

name: Mason-Dixon Middle Point Marker
desc: Stones under a small brick pavilion beside Route 54 mark the midpoint of the 1751 Transpeninsular Line, the southwest corner of Delaware and the spot where Mason and Dixon began their line north.

name: Massanutten Storybook Trail
desc: Flat paved path with signs on the geology of Massanutten, ending at a deck with a view east over Page Valley to the Blue Ridge. Ten minutes each way off Crisman Hollow Road.

name: Massey's Landing
desc: Public boat ramp and fishing pier at the tip of Long Neck, where Rehoboth Bay and Indian River Bay meet in a narrow channel. Water on three sides.

name: Matapeake Fishing Pier
desc: Long lighted fishing pier and boat ramp at the former Bay ferry terminal, next to Matapeake Beach. Open water to the west makes it a simple sunset stop.

name: McCrillis Gardens
desc: Five-acre shade garden of azaleas and rhododendrons under tall trees in a Bethesda neighborhood, at its best from late April into May. Free; street parking.

name: McKee-Beshers Wildlife Management Area
desc: State wildlife area on the Potomac floodplain known for sunflower fields that bloom in mid-July and for birding along the dikes of the Hughes Hollow impoundments. Flat, often muddy paths.

name: Meadowood Recreation Area
desc: About 800 acres of Bureau of Land Management meadows, ponds and hardwood forest on Mason Neck, with separate hiking, horse and mountain-bike trail networks. Free.

name: Meems Bottom Covered Bridge
desc: Virginia's longest covered bridge: a 204-foot single-span Burr arch built in 1892 over the North Fork Shenandoah, still open to cars. Small pull-off and river access beside it.

name: Meridian Hill Park
desc: Formal 12-acre hillside park with a 13-basin cascading fountain, exposed-aggregate concrete walls and terraces in the Italian style. Sunday afternoon drum circle on the upper level.

name: Merrimac Farm Wildlife Management Area
desc: Floodplain trail along Cedar Run through one of the larger Virginia bluebell stands in the region, at peak in mid-April. Fields and wetlands managed for wildlife the rest of the year.

facts.fee: Virginia DWR access permit or hunting/fishing license required (age 17+)

name: Merritt Point Park
desc: Dundalk neighborhood park on Bull Neck Creek with paved walking paths, piers, shoreline access, a two-lane boat ramp and a soft launch for kayaks added in 2023. No ramp fee.

name: Miami Beach Park
desc: Small county beach of about 400 feet on the Chesapeake at Bowleys Quarters, east of Middle River, with picnic tables and a playground. Open for swimming in summer.

name: Middle Branch Park
desc: Shoreline park on the Middle Branch of the Patapsco with a boardwalk, fishing piers, a rowing center and a long view back to the downtown skyline. On the Gwynns Falls Trail.

name: Mill Creek Falls Nature Preserve
desc: Red-blazed trail dropping 240 ft from the lot to a 10-ft waterfall where two creeks meet just above the Susquehanna. Also has a mile-long accessible crushed-stone loop.

name: Millers Head
desc: Short trail from the Skyland amphitheater over Bushytop to a stone platform at a former fire-tower site, with a broad view down to Page Valley and across to Massanutten.

name: Mint Springs Valley Park
desc: County park in a mountain hollow above Crozet with three small lakes, a swimming beach and steep trails up the slope. Swimming was suspended in 2026 for an algae bloom; check before going.

facts.fee: Beach fee in summer for non-residents

name: Moll Dyer Rock
desc: An 875-pound boulder tied to the legend of Moll Dyer, said to have frozen to death against it in 1697 after being driven out as a witch. Visitors look for her handprint in the stone.

name: Monocacy National Battlefield
desc: 1864 battlefield straddling the Monocacy River with farm-lane walking loops at the Worthington, Thomas and Best farms. Quiet river and field scenery just off I-270.

name: Monroe Run Overlook
desc: Roadside overlook near the crest of Meadow Mountain on New Germany Road, looking down the forested Monroe Run valley. Best in October.

name: Mont Alto State Park
desc: Pennsylvania's oldest state park: a 24-acre picnic grove on PA 233 with a distinctive old pavilion and a trout stream, surrounded by Michaux State Forest.

name: Montpelier Trails and Landmark Forest
desc: More than eight miles of free walking trails on James Madison's estate, through pastures and the 200-acre Landmark Forest, where oaks, beeches and poplars have stood largely undisturbed since the 1790s.

name: Morgan Ford Boat Landing
desc: Public landing on the main stem of the Shenandoah north of Front Royal. The 1925 single-lane low-water bridge here was replaced by a higher two-lane span in 2018; river access remains.

name: Morgan Run Natural Environment Area
desc: About 2,000 acres of state land around a catch-and-release trout stream feeding Liberty Reservoir, with field and forest trails shared with horses. Lots on Ben Rose Lane and Klee Mill Road.

name: Morven Park
desc: 1,000-acre estate on the edge of Leesburg with a Greek Revival mansion, boxwood gardens and wooded hiking trails on the ridge behind the house. Grounds free; mansion tours charged.

name: Motts Run Reservoir
desc: Wooded reservoir west of Fredericksburg run as a seasonal recreation area: boat rentals, bank fishing, a nature center and several miles of hiking trails. Check opening dates before going.

name: Mount Harmon Plantation
desc: Restored 18th-century tobacco plantation at the end of a two-mile tree-tunnel lane, on a 200-acre nature preserve with trails along the Sassafras River. Seasonal hours; admission charged.

name: Mount Marshall (North and South)
desc: Two Appalachian Trail summits either side of Skyline Drive mile 15.9. South Marshall's ledges are 0.8 mile from the lot; North Marshall (about 3,368 ft) has west-facing cliffs over Browntown Valley.

name: Mount Torry Furnace
desc: Stone iron furnace stack on the shoulder of VA-664 in George Washington National Forest, a few miles from Sherando Lake; it was burned in an 1864 Union raid and rebuilt. Roadside pull-off; free.

name: Muddy Run Recreation Park
desc: Power-company park around a recreation lake beside the pumped-storage reservoir, with a campground, boat rentals and trails.

name: Mudhole Gap Loop
desc: Long, gentle loop mostly on fire roads from the Elizabeth Furnace area: pools and runs along Little Passage Creek in Mudhole Gap, five fords, Strasburg Reservoir and views from Green Mountain.

name: Murphy Farm: John Brown's Fort Foundation
desc: Foundation marking where John Brown's Fort stood on the Murphy farm for some years before returning to town, with Civil War earthworks and a bluff-top view over the Shenandoah. Easy 1-3 mi round trip on the Murphy-Chambers Farm trail.

name: Murphy-Chambers Farm
desc: Farm-field loop to a bluff overlook above the Shenandoah River, past Civil War earthworks and the site where John Brown's fort once stood.

name: Nancy Hanks Memorial
desc: Small memorial far up a narrow hollow road on Mikes Run, at the traditional birthplace of Nancy Hanks, mother of Abraham Lincoln.

name: National Shrine Grotto of Our Lady of Lourdes
desc: Mountainside shrine above Mount St. Mary's with a replica of the Lourdes grotto, shaded garden paths, a pool and a valley view from the terrace.

name: Native Lands County Park
desc: Trail across the hillside site of the last Susquehannock town, with river views, running along the Mason-Dixon Trail between Klines Run Park and Long Level.

name: Negley Park
desc: Neighborhood park on a bluff across the Susquehanna from Harrisburg, with a head-on view of the skyline, the Capitol dome and the river bridges.

name: Netherlands Carillon lawn (Arlington Ridge Park)
desc: Hillside lawn below the carillon tower that lines up the Lincoln Memorial, Washington Monument and Capitol in one view. Tulip beds in spring; the Marine Corps War Memorial is next door.

name: New York Avenue Brickworks
desc: Brick beehive kilns of the United Brick Corporation, the only brickyard left in DC, on fenced National Arboretum land in the 2800 block of New York Ave NE. Public access is restricted; look from the road.

facts.access: You can only look at this one from outside (road, trail or water). The site itself is closed or fenced.

name: North East Community Park
desc: Town park at the head of the North East River with a waterfront walking path, fishing pier, kayak launch and wide views down the river toward the Bay.

name: North River Gorge
desc: Loop with a ridge of valley views and 4.2 miles along the North River, forded about ten times, with pools for cooling off. Go in late summer or early fall when the water is low.

name: Northside Park
desc: 58-acre bayside park at 125th Street with a paved loop path, lagoon footbridge and fishing pier on Assawoman Bay. The quiet side of town at sunset.

name: Nottingham County Park serpentine barrens
desc: Pitch pine and prairie grass growing on green serpentine bedrock that poisons ordinary forest, a landscape unlike the farmland around it, dotted with old chrome and feldspar pits.

name: Occoquan Regional Park
desc: 350-acre riverfront park across from the town of Occoquan: a 5 km loop trail, kayak rentals and boat launch, a preserved brick kiln from the Lorton prison brickyard and a suffragist memorial.

name: Occoquan Riverwalk and River Mill Park
desc: Boardwalk along the Occoquan River behind the shops of a small mill town, ending at a riverside park below the dam and a footbridge across to Fairfax County.

name: Odenton Natural Area
desc: Wooded county natural area on Higgins Drive with trails, picnic tables and grills. A quiet short walk if you are already in Odenton.

name: Old Ferry Landing, Assateague
desc: Bayside spot inside the national seashore for launching a kayak, crabbing and clamming in the shallows, and watching the sun set over Sinepuxent Bay.

name: Old Post Office Tower
desc: 270-ft observation deck in the 1899 clock tower on Pennsylvania Avenue, with open views down the Mall. Reopened Aug 2026, run by the Waldorf Astoria: Wed-Sat 9 to noon, entry from 12th St.

name: Old Rag Summit via Berry Hollow
desc: The back way up Old Rag: Berry Hollow fire road to the Saddle Trail and the summit boulders, skipping the rock scramble. Still a steep climb; same day-use ticket applies.

facts.fee: $30/vehicle park entry (7 days) plus $2 Old Rag day-use ticket Mar 1-Nov 30

name: Old Rag View Overlook
desc: Looks east-northeast at 3,585 ft to Old Rag, about three miles away across the hollows.

name: Old White Marsh Church Ruins
desc: Low brick walls of a colonial parish church that burned in the 1890s, in an old cemetery beside US-50 at Manadier Rd between Easton and Trappe. Roadside pull-in; free.

name: Oldtown Low-Water Toll Bridge
desc: Privately owned one-lane bridge sitting just above the Potomac, where a toll is collected for crossing to West Virginia. The C&O Canal towpath crosses its approach.

name: Olson Observation Tower
desc: Steel fire tower on Backbone Mountain that you can climb for a full-circle view over the Blackwater Canyon rim and the Cheat River country. Reached by a gravel forest road off US 219.

name: Opossum Lake
desc: Quiet fishing lake below Blue Mountain west of Carlisle with a shoreline trail and electric-motor-only boating.

name: Orange Grove Flour Mill Ruins and Swinging Bridge
in: Patapsco Valley State Park Glen Artney Area
desc: Stone walls and foundations of the Orange Grove flour mill, burned in May 1905, facing the cable Swinging Bridge that mill workers once crossed. On the paved Grist Mill Trail in the Avalon/Orange Grove area; park entry fee.

name: Oregon Road CCC and POW Camp Ruins
desc: Stone and concrete remains of CCC Camp S-52, built in 1933 on Sideling Hill, later quarters for conscientious objectors and in 1944 a camp for German POWs. In Buchanan State Forest off Oregon Rd, near the turnpike tunnel. Free.

name: Oxbow Natural Area
desc: County preserve around Laurel Oxbow Lake, a beaver-made impoundment of the Little Patuxent described as the largest naturally occurring body of fresh water in Maryland. Short trail to a viewing platform.

name: Oxford Conservation Park
desc: County park at the edge of Oxford with mown and gravel paths looping through planted meadows, young woodland and a pond. Flat, open and quiet.

name: Oxford-Bellevue Ferry
desc: Small car ferry across the Tred Avon River, started in 1683 and believed to be the oldest privately owned ferry service in the country. Runs spring to fall; closed December to March.

facts.fee: About $16 car and driver one way
