name: Oxon Cove Park and Oxon Hill Farm
desc: National Park Service working farm with barns and animals on a bluff above Oxon Cove. A paved hiker-biker trail runs down along the cove toward the DC line; river views and herons.

name: Palmer State Park
desc: Undeveloped state park on Deer Creek with no facilities: rough woodland trails, creek fishing, canoeing and the remains of a flint mill and iron works. Small pull-off parking only.

name: Paradise Furnace
desc: Squat 1830s stone iron furnace stack and the ironmaster's house beside Great Trough Creek in Trough Creek State Park, a gorge that also has an ice mine and a balanced rock. Free.

name: Pase Point
desc: Rock point above the junction of the Blackwater and North Fork canyons, reached by a quiet forest trail from the north-rim side of the park.

name: Patapsco Valley State Park - Hilton Area
in: Patapsco Valley State Park Orange Grove Area
desc: Hilltop section above the gorge in Catonsville with a campground, a nature center, a recycled-tire playground and trails that drop to the river and connect to the swinging bridge.

name: Patapsco Valley State Park - Hollofield Area
desc: Ridge-top area off Route 40 with an overlook of the Patapsco valley, a campground and trails down to the river and the remains of Union Dam.

name: Patricia Ann Byrom Forest Preserve Park
desc: 680 acres of steep Blue Ridge foothill forest with 6 miles of trails; the 4.3-mile Little Flat Mountain loop climbs to ridge views next to Shenandoah National Park.

name: Patterson Viaduct Ruins
in: Patapsco Valley State Park Orange Grove Area
desc: Surviving stone arch and abutments of an 1829 B&O Railroad viaduct wrecked by the 1868 flood, topped since 2006 by a footbridge over the Patapsco at Ilchester, at the upper end of the Grist Mill Trail.

name: Patuxent Branch Trail
desc: Rail trail up the Little Patuxent from Savage Park to Lake Elkhorn, mostly paved and wooded, crossing the river on the 1902 Guilford Pratt truss bridge.

name: Patuxent Ponds Park
desc: County park in the Patuxent River Greenway built around old ponds off Patuxent Road, with walking trails and bank fishing. Open sunrise to sunset.

name: Patuxent Research Refuge - North Tract
desc: Former Fort Meade training land, now refuge: about 15 miles of trails for walking and biking through forest and wetlands. Register at the contact station; 2026 notices show reduced open days, so call first.

name: Patuxent River Greenway - Bayard
desc: Undeveloped county greenway tract on Sands Road with walking trails and bank fishing on the Patuxent River, a short way upstream of Wootons Landing. Dawn to dusk.

name: Patuxent River State Park
desc: Largely undeveloped state park strung along the upper Patuxent on the Howard-Montgomery line: unmarked foot and horse trails, catch-and-release trout water and few people.

name: Patuxent Wetlands Park
desc: Roadside county park beside the Route 4 bridge over the Patuxent River: a pier and cartop launch straight into the Jug Bay marshes. Good put-in for paddling the wild rice in late summer.

name: Peirce Mill
desc: Stone gristmill from the 1820s, the only one left of the mills that once lined Rock Creek. Restored water wheel, a low dam cascade beside it and creekside trails in both directions.

name: Pen Mar Park
desc: County park beside the Mason-Dixon Line on the site of an old mountain resort: overlook pavilion facing west, picnic grounds and the Appalachian Trail. Open May through October, 9 am to sunset.

name: Pennhurst State School
desc: Brick halls of the notorious state institution closed in 1987; eight buildings were torn down in 2018-2020. Private. Entry only with tickets for daytime history tours, paranormal events or the fall haunted attraction.

facts.access: Open by guided tour or by arrangement only. Check before you go.

name: Peters Mountain: Table Rock (Appalachian Trail)
desc: Ridge walk on the Appalachian Trail from the PA 225 crossing to a rock ledge overlooking Clarks Valley.

name: Phillips Landing (Nanticoke Wildlife Area)
desc: Wooded point where Broad Creek meets the Nanticoke River, with a boat ramp, a short trail and a monument to Captain John Smith's 1608 exploration of the river.

name: Pickering Beach
desc: One-street bay community east of Dover and a designated horseshoe crab sanctuary. Public access is a small path to the sand; come on a May or June high tide for the spawning.

name: Pirate's Wharf Park
desc: 300-acre county park on the Wicomico River, opened in 2023, with just over two miles of accessible walking trails. The boat ramp, pier and river overlooks are under construction until about 2027.

name: Pocomoke River State Park - Milburn Landing
desc: The quieter side of the park across the river, with a boat ramp, a small campground and the Bald Cypress Nature Trail looping through loblolly pine and cypress swamp.

name: Point Lookout Civil War Sites
desc: Earthworks of Fort Lincoln and the site of a huge Union prison camp for Confederates, on a peninsula where the Potomac meets the bay; much of the camp has eroded into the water. State park; day-use fee.

name: Port Tobacco
desc: Colonial river port that silted up and emptied; now Maryland's smallest incorporated town (18 people in 2020) with a reconstructed courthouse on a quiet green and a few 1700s houses. Free to walk around.

name: Port Tobacco Historic Village
desc: What is left of a colonial river port that silted up and faded: a rebuilt courthouse and a handful of 18th-century houses around a green. One of the smallest incorporated towns in Maryland.

name: Port Tobacco River Park
desc: Three miles of easy trails with observation platforms over the Port Tobacco River marsh and a resident bald eagle nest that the county streams on a live camera.

name: Potomac Overlook Regional Park
desc: Wooded NOVA Parks property above the Potomac palisades with a nature center, gardens and loop trails. The Donaldson Run Trail continues downhill to the river and the Potomac Heritage Trail.

name: Potomac/Garrett State Forest
desc: Garrett State Forest is a state forest located in the state of Maryland northwest of Oakland. Garrett State Forest is the birthplace of forestry conservation in Maryland.

name: Public Landing
desc: Old bayside resort turned quiet county landing on Chincoteague Bay: a pier, boat ramp and a small beach on shallow water looking across to Assateague Island.

name: Raccoon Point Park
desc: Out-of-the-way county park on the Manokin River with a strand of bayside beach, a soft launch for kayaks and a pavilion. Open 7 am to 7 pm.

name: Rachel Carson Conservation Park
desc: 650 acres of quiet woods and meadows along the Hawlings River with more than 6 miles of natural-surface trails, rock outcrops and mountain laurel that blooms from late May into June.

name: Rackliffe House Trail
desc: Flat 1.3-mile loop through woods from the Assateague visitor center to a restored 1740s plantation house overlooking Sinepuxent Bay and the island.

name: Ragged Mountain Natural Area
desc: Rolling six-mile loop through mature forest around Ragged Mountain Reservoir on the edge of Charlottesville. Fishing and paddling are allowed; swimming and dogs are not.

name: Rappahannock County Park (Dark Sky Park)
desc: A 7.3-acre park off US 211 certified as an International Dark Sky Park in 2019. Public star parties are held the night before each new moon; by day there is a short trail and trout stream.

name: Raven Rock (Coopers Rock State Forest)
desc: Forest-road walk to a second clifftop over the Cheat gorge, with the same river view as the main overlook and a fraction of the visitors.

name: Raven Rock Falls
desc: Low-angle cascade sliding down a rock face beside the Gunpowder in the Hereford Area. Park by the York Road bridge and walk upstream along the south bank for about 30 minutes on uneven trail.

name: Ravens Roost Overlook (Blue Ridge Parkway)
desc: Parkway milepost 10.7: a cliff-edge ledge at 3,200 ft, about 1,800 ft above the Shenandoah Valley, facing west to Torry Ridge. A few minutes' walk from the car. About 153 miles from home.

name: Red Rock Wilderness Overlook Ruins
desc: Roofless brick carriage house, granary, ice house and well house of a vanished farm estate at the trailhead of a small regional park; trails go on to bluffs above the Potomac. Free gravel lot on Edwards Ferry Rd.

name: Redden State Forest - Headquarters Tract
desc: Loblolly pine forest north of Georgetown with more than seven miles of flat, sandy woods roads, starting near a rustic early-1900s railroad hunting lodge.

name: Riven Rock Park
desc: Harrisonburg city park on 27 wooded acres along the Dry River near Rawley Springs, with picnic shelters, short trails and wading in the river. Open mid-April to October 31, until 9 pm.

name: River Campus at Cool Spring Battlefield
desc: Former golf course on the Shenandoah River, now a Shenandoah University preserve: 3.4 miles of mostly paved cart paths past an 1864 battlefield, a heron rookery and river views. Dawn to dusk.

name: River Farm
desc: American Horticultural Society headquarters on land once owned by George Washington. Gardens and a meadow slope down to the Potomac; free, but check open days before going.

name: Riverside Park (GW Parkway)
desc: Small parkway pull-off where Little Hunting Creek meets the Potomac, a mile from Mount Vernon. Picnic tables on the bank, shoreline fishing and wide water views; Mount Vernon Trail passes through.

name: Riverside Preserve (Fauquier County)
desc: Fauquier County park with a short trail and walk-in access to the upper Rappahannock River for wading, fishing and launching small boats.

name: Robert Reed Downtown Waterfront Park
desc: Town park on Chincoteague Channel on Main Street with a boardwalk, docks and benches facing west over the water and the working boats.

name: Robinson Neck Preserve
desc: Nature Conservancy trail on Taylors Island, 1.35 miles each way through loblolly pine and over boardwalks to open marsh. Remote and silent; wet underfoot, buggy in summer. No dogs.

name: Rock Run Historic Area and Canal Remains
desc: Stone grist mill, a toll house for a river bridge that no longer exists and traces of the Susquehanna and Tidewater Canal, on the riverbank in Susquehanna State Park. Buildings open some summer weekends; grounds always.

name: Rockburn Branch Park
desc: County park with a network of wooded natural-surface trails popular with mountain bikers and trail runners, a skills park and links into Patapsco Valley State Park.

name: Rocky Gap Gorge (Canyon Overlook Trail)
desc: Short trail near the dam to a ledge over the gorge that Rocky Gap Run cut through the mountain, lined with hemlock and rhododendron.

name: Rocky Mount
desc: Rugged, little-used South District circuit with three separate climbs, crossings of Gap Run and a panoramic rock summit. Burned in the 2016 fire; expect brush and blowdowns. Park near mile 76.

name: Rocky Ridge County Park
desc: Wooded ridge park north of York with observation decks facing north and south, a fall hawk watch and miles of trail.

name: Roddy Road Covered Bridge
desc: One-lane king post covered bridge only 40 ft long, built in the 1850s over Owens Creek, with a small creekside park next to it.

name: Romancoke Fishing Pier
desc: County pier at the south end of Kent Island where MD 8 runs out, on the site of an old ferry landing. Long view down Eastern Bay; fishing, crabbing and a kayak launch.

name: Rosaryville State Park
desc: Wooded state park around the Mount Airy Mansion with a long perimeter loop shared by trail runners, mountain bikers and horses. Rolling singletrack and few people on weekdays.

name: Rose Haven Memorial Park
desc: Small county park in Rose Haven at the southern tip of the county near Herring Bay, listed as a cartop launch for canoes and kayaks. Sunrise to sunset.

name: Round Falls
desc: Semicircular stone mill dam on the Jones Falls that spills as a curved curtain of water, tucked below Falls Road beside the Jones Falls Trail with a small viewing platform.

name: Rumsey Monument Park
desc: Tall column on a bluff above the Potomac marking where James Rumsey demonstrated his steamboat in 1787. Short walk from Shepherdstown's main street.

name: Sachs Covered Bridge
desc: 100-ft lattice-truss covered bridge over Marsh Creek, crossed by troops of both armies in 1863. Open to walkers only.

name: Sailwinds Park and Dorchester Visitor Center
desc: Riverside park beside the US 50 bridge with a boardwalk, a strip of sand and the visitor center under its 100-foot sail canopy. Good view of the two-mile bridge; no swimming.

name: Sang Run State Park
desc: 264-acre park at a put-in for the Upper Yough's Class V whitewater, with an early-1800s homestead, the old Friends Store and river meadow trails.

name: Saxis Island Pier and Beach
desc: Watermen's village at the end of a long causeway through the Saxis marshes, with a public fishing pier and a small sandy beach on Pocomoke Sound facing the sunset.

name: Schaeffer Farms Trails
desc: Stacked loops of smooth singletrack through farm fields and woods in Seneca Creek State Park, built for mountain bikes and well suited to trail running. Lot at the end of Schaeffer Road.

name: Seneca Caverns
desc: Show cave in Germany Valley with guided tours going 165 ft underground. Seasonal: in 2026 it opened May 1 on Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays only.

name: Seven Bends State Park
desc: Day-use park on the meandering North Fork Shenandoah below Massanutten, with hand-carry boat launches, riverside paths and wooded upland trails. Virginia's 41st state park.

name: Seven Foot Knoll Lighthouse
desc: Round red screw-pile lighthouse built in 1855, the oldest of its kind in Maryland. It stood on a shoal at the mouth of the Patapsco and now sits on Pier 5 in the Inner Harbor, where you can walk right up to it.

name: Shady Side Park
desc: County park on the Shady Side peninsula listed as a cartop launch for canoes and kayaks. Sunrise to sunset.

name: Shady Side Wharf
desc: County wharf at the end of Woods Wharf Road on the West River side of Shady Side, open dawn to dusk for fishing and crabbing from the pier.

name: Shannondale Springs Wildlife Management Area
desc: Site of a mineral springs resort founded in 1820 on a bend of the Shenandoah River upstream of Harpers Ferry, now public hunting and fishing land with river access.

name: Sharps Island Light
desc: Cast-iron 1882 lighthouse left leaning like the Tower of Pisa by a 1977 ice floe, marking an island that washed away. Stands nearly 3 mi off the south end of Tilghman Island; seen only by boat.

facts.access: You can only look at this one from outside (road, trail or water). The site itself is closed or fenced.

name: Shenandoah Valley Overlook (Skyline Drive)
desc: First big pull-off south of the Front Royal entrance: faces north at 1,390 ft over the top of the Shenandoah Valley, with Signal Knob and the town of Front Royal below.

name: Shrine Mont Cathedral Shrine of the Transfiguration
desc: Open-air stone sanctuary consecrated in 1925, built of boulders hauled off the mountain behind it; the country's only outdoor Episcopal cathedral. Public Sunday services April to November.

name: Signal Knob Overlook (Skyline Drive)
desc: Faces west-northwest at 2,090 ft across the valley to Massanutten and Signal Knob, the Confederate lookout used before the Battle of Cedar Creek. Good at sunset.

name: Simpsonville Mill Ruins
desc: Stone walls and millrace of the Simpsonville mill on the Middle Patuxent River, on the trails below the Robinson Nature Center off Cedar Lane. Short walk; free when the grounds are open.

name: Sleepy Creek Lake
desc: 205-acre lake inside the 22,928-acre Sleepy Creek Wildlife Management Area, with primitive lakeside campsites and long gravel approach roads.

name: Sligo Creek Trail
desc: Paved trail of about 10 miles following Sligo Creek from Wheaton through Silver Spring and Takoma Park to the Northwest Branch in Hyattsville. Shaded, gently rolling, many neighborhood access points.

name: Smallwood State Park
desc: Park on Mattawoman Creek, a tidal Potomac tributary known for bass fishing and summer lotus beds. Marina and ramps, short trails, and the restored home of General William Smallwood.

name: Smoke Hole Caverns
desc: Commercial show cave on WV 28 west of Petersburg, open since 1940, with guided tours past dense formations.

name: Snead Farm
desc: White barn, stone root cellar and house foundation of an apple farm absorbed by the park. Easy fire-road walk from across the Dickey Ridge picnic area (Skyline Drive mile 5.1), or a longer loop. Park entry fee.

name: Snead Farm and Dickey Ridge Loop
desc: Loop from Dickey Ridge Visitor Center through old apple orchards to the white Snead barn, the last standing building of a pre-park farm. The 1.2-mile Fox Hollow loop starts at the same spot.

name: Snow Hill Park
desc: Newer county waterfront park on a former farm on the Patuxent River, with a public beach, unsupervised swimming, fishing and crabbing.

name: Soldiers Delight Choate Chrome Mine
desc: Timbered, fenced entrance of the Choate chromite mine and nearby pit workings in the serpentine barrens of Soldiers Delight Natural Environment Area. On the Choate Mine Trail from the Deer Park Rd overlook; free.

name: Solleys Cove Park
desc: County waterfront park on Carbide Road with a cartop launch for canoes and kayaks at the north end of the county. Sunrise to sunset.

name: South Shore Trail
desc: First finished piece of a planned Annapolis-to-Odenton rail trail: 1.6 paved miles between Millersville Road and Waterbury Road through quiet woods.

name: Southwest Area Park
desc: County park with Baltimore County's only public boat ramp on the Patapsco River (shallow-draft boats), a pier, nature trails, paved paths and a pond. No ramp fee.

name: Spanish Steps (Kalorama)
desc: Small 1911 staircase with a lion-head fountain joining S Street and Decatur Place on the slope above Dupont Circle. Shaded, little visited and a good place to sit and read.

name: Spitler Knoll Overlook
desc: Long west-northwest overlook at 3,285 ft on former mountain pasture, open to the whole evening sky over Page Valley.

name: Spocott Windmill
desc: A working English-style post windmill, the only one in Maryland, rebuilt in 1972 beside a one-room schoolhouse and a tenant house on the road to Hoopers Island. Grounds open daily.

name: Spriggs Farm Park
desc: Quiet natural area on the Magothy River with trails, picnic tables and a cartop launch down a steep 150-yard carry. Gated: request the free gate code from the county portal before going.

name: Spruce Knob Lake
desc: Small trout lake high on the west side of Spruce Mountain, with a walk-around trail and a campground nearby. Very dark night skies.

name: St. Clement's Island State Park
desc: Island in the Potomac where Maryland's first colonists landed in 1634, with a 40-foot cross, a rebuilt lighthouse and beaches. Reached only by boat; a seasonal water taxi runs from the museum.

name: St. Jones Reserve
desc: Estuarine research reserve with a one-mile trail that crosses the St. Jones River marsh on a long boardwalk and continues toward the Ted Harvey wildlife area.

name: St. Mary's College Ruins (Hell House)
desc: Seminary of 1868, closed 1972, burned 1997 and razed in 2006. Left in the woods above the Patapsco: a long stone staircase, foundations, a hillside basement and rubble. Unsigned paths near Ilchester Rd; scarce parking, unstable ground.

name: St. Michaels Nature Trail
desc: Short paved rail-trail across St. Michaels that crosses a creek on a covered footbridge and passes marsh and back yards. Easy walk or jog away from the busy main street.

name: Stafford Civil War Park
desc: Preserved earthworks of the Union Army's 1863 winter camp: artillery batteries, hut sites, a corduroy road trace and an old sandstone quarry, linked by a driving loop and short paths.

name: Stafford Flint Furnace
desc: Stone furnace that is the last trace of the river village of Stafford, at the mouth of Deer Creek in Susquehanna State Park. On the flat Lower Susquehanna Heritage Greenway Trail (old canal and rail bed) toward Conowingo Dam.

name: Staunton Dam
desc: Picnic area at a masonry dam built in the 1920s on the North River; its water runs through a tunnel under Lookout Mountain to supply Staunton. Next to Elkhorn Lake.

name: Stoney Creek Park
desc: Undeveloped county woodland on Locust Grove Road with walking trails through the trees near the head of Stoney Creek. Open sunrise to sunset.

name: Stony Man Mountain Overlook
desc: Large pull-off north of Skyland looking west over Page Valley, with the cliff profile of Stony Man's 'face' to the south.

name: Stony Run Trail
desc: Narrow stream-side walking path of about three miles following Stony Run through Roland Park, Wyman Park and Remington on the bed of the old Ma & Pa Railroad.

name: Strawberry Hill Nature Preserve
desc: Nonprofit preserve in the hills west of Gettysburg with streamside trails, ponds and rocky mountain forest, bordering Michaux State Forest.

name: Suitland Bog
desc: Fenced remnant of a rare magnolia bog with carnivorous pitcher plants, viewed from a boardwalk loop. Reached by a short trail off Regency Parkway; open dawn to dusk.

name: Sullivans Cove Natural Area
desc: Small county natural area off Bay Park Way in Severna Park with woodland trails around a bog at the head of Sullivans Cove. Open sunrise to sunset.

name: Summerhouse (U.S. Capitol grounds)
desc: Open-air hexagonal brick shelter built by Frederick Law Olmsted around 1880 on the Senate side of the Capitol lawn, with a fountain, stone benches and a window onto a small rock grotto.

name: Sunset Park, Ocean City
desc: Small bayside park on South Division Street facing west over the Isle of Wight Bay channel and the fishing fleet. Built for watching the sun go down.

name: Susquehanna Riverlands State Park (Schull's Rock)
desc: Wooded 1,044-acre state park created in 2022 where Codorus Creek meets the Susquehanna. The Mason-Dixon Trail runs 2.75 miles through it past a rock overlook. No restrooms; park off River Farm Road.

name: Swains Lock
desc: Lock 21, built of red Seneca sandstone, with its lockhouse, a primitive hiker-biker campsite and easy towpath access about 2 miles above Great Falls. Quieter than the Tavern, with no entrance fee.

name: Swan Harbor Farm
desc: County-owned bayfront farm south of Havre de Grace with a long tree-lined drive and open lawns on the upper Chesapeake. Often booked for events, so parts may be closed.

name: Swannanoa
desc: Marble Italian Renaissance villa built in 1912 on the crest of Rockfish Gap, long empty inside. Privately owned and gated; open only on scheduled tour days and events for a fee.

facts.access: Open by guided tour or by arrangement only. Check before you go.

name: Swatara State Park
desc: 3,520-acre park along 8 miles of Swatara Creek with a long rail trail, old canal remains and a roadside shale pit where visitors may dig for fossils.

name: Sweet Run State Park
desc: Virginia's 42nd state park (dedicated 2023): 884 acres of meadows, woods, streams and old farmsteads in the 'Between the Hills' valley near Harpers Ferry.

name: Switzer Lake (Skidmore Fork)
desc: Clear reservoir in a deep forested valley off US 33 below High Knob. Canoe launch, electric motors only, no swimming (it is a water supply); primitive campsites lie farther up the rough road.

name: Taber State Forest
desc: Delaware has three state forests, one in each county, totaling more than 19,000 acres (77 km2). These natural resource areas are managed by the Delaware Department of Agriculture Forest Service.

name: Taylors Island
desc: Low island of marsh, loblolly pine and a few old churches across the Slaughter Creek bridge, where a small cannon captured from the British in 1814 sits by the road. Very little traffic.

name: Ted Harvey Conservation Area - Logan Lane Beach
desc: Secluded Delaware Bay beach reached by a 0.2-mile walk along a dike from the parking area in a state wildlife area south of Kitts Hummock. Usually empty.

facts.fee: Delaware Conservation Access Pass or fishing/hunting license needed to park

name: The Awakening (National Harbor)
desc: Five-piece aluminum sculpture of a giant struggling out of the ground, set in a small man-made beach on the Potomac at National Harbor. The waterfront faces west toward Alexandria at sunset.

name: The Cliffs Ruins
desc: Stone shell of a 1753 Georgian country house, vandalized and gutted by fire in the 1980s, covered in graffiti in the woods of East Fairmount Park near 33rd and Oxford Sts. Open parkland; keep out of the walls.

name: The Narrows and Lovers Leap
desc: Water gap where Wills Creek, the National Road and the railroads squeeze between quartzite cliffs. Lovers Leap on the rim is reached by an unmarked path and closes for falcon nesting.

name: The Trough (South Branch Potomac)
desc: Six-mile roadless gorge of the South Branch between Romney and Moorefield, known for bald eagles. Seen only by canoe or kayak, or from the excursion train that runs through it.

name: Thomas Stone National Historic Site
desc: Haberdeventure, the plantation home of a signer of the Declaration of Independence, set in more than 300 acres of fields and woods with a couple of miles of quiet walking paths.

name: Thompson Island Nature Preserve
desc: Flat woodland trail, 0.7 miles each way, out to the edge of the marsh on Rehoboth Bay at the back of Rehoboth Beach. A quiet contrast to the boardwalk a mile away.

name: Thornton Hollow Overlook
desc: East-facing window at 2,460 ft into Thornton Hollow, with Mount Marshall to the left and Oventop Mountain to the right. A sunrise stop.

name: Thorofare Mountain Overlook
desc: Highest overlook in the park (3,595 ft), looking east to Thorofare Mountain, Hazel Mountain and the slope of Old Rag. A sunrise stop.

name: Three Notch Trail
desc: Paved rail-trail being built in sections along the old railroad through northern St. Mary's County. Flat and straight; the Charlotte Hall segments are the longest continuous run.

name: Thurmont Vista (Catoctin Mountain Park)
desc: Cleared overlook facing east over Thurmont and the Monocacy Valley, reached by a short uphill trail from its own lot on Park Central Road.

name: Todd Lake Recreation Area
desc: Small mountain lake with an accessible sand beach, picnic fields and a historic campground; the Trimble Mountain loop starts nearby. Seasonal: reopened May 15 in 2026, runs to late October.

name: Tolliver Falls
desc: Small ledge fall on Tolliver Run in a shaded hemlock hollow, the quietest stop on the Swallow Falls canyon loop.

name: Trayfoot Mountain and Paine Run Loop
desc: South District loop over Blackrock Summit's boulder field and along Trayfoot Mountain to Buzzard Rock, returning beside Paine Run. Ridge sections can be overgrown.

name: Tregaron Conservancy
desc: Woodland garden of a 1912 estate between Cleveland Park and Woodley Park: lily pond, stone bridges and restored paths that connect to the paved Klingle Valley Trail. Open daily, free.

name: Tri-State Marker (Delaware-Maryland-Pennsylvania)
desc: A 19th-century boundary stone in the woods at the exact point where three states meet, reached by a short hike on the Tri-State Marker Trail in the White Clay Creek preserves.

name: Trimble Mountain Loop
desc: Short loop over two wooded summits beside Todd Lake, with views of Big Bald and Little Bald knobs and a finish across the dam above the lake.

name: Trolley Line #9 Trail
desc: 1.25 mi paved trail on an abandoned streetcar line between Catonsville and Ellicott City, running through a deep hand-cut rock cut and down a boardwalk to Oella and the Patapsco. Free; lots at either end.

name: Truxtun Park
desc: City park on a wooded bluff above Spa Creek with natural-surface trails along the creek, a public boat ramp and kayak access close to downtown Annapolis.

name: Turk Mountain
desc: Short climb to a 2,981-ft quartzite summit with talus slopes and a wide view west over Waynesboro and the valley. Quiet compared with the Central District.

name: Turkey Hill Trail and overlooks
desc: Strenuous ridge trail with river overlooks at both ends; the northern one looks over the Conejohela Flats, a waterfowl stopover. Loop back on the level Enola Low Grade rail trail.

name: Tuscarora State Forest
desc: Tuscarora State Forest is a Pennsylvania state forest in Pennsylvania Bureau of Forestry District #3. The main office is located in Blain in Perry County, Pennsylvania in the United States.

name: Tyaskin Park
desc: Small county park on Wetipquin Creek near the Nanticoke with a little sandy beach, pier and boat ramp. Rarely more than a few cars.

name: Underground Railroad Experience Trail (Woodlawn Manor)
desc: Trail from the stone barn at Woodlawn Manor through woods and field edges toward Sandy Spring, with markers on how freedom seekers used the landscape. About 4 miles out and back.

name: Union Arch Bridge (Cabin John Bridge)
desc: 1864 stone bridge carrying the Washington Aqueduct and MacArthur Boulevard over Cabin John Creek. Its 220-ft span was the longest single masonry arch in the world until 1903.

name: Union Dam Ruins
in: Patapsco Valley State Park Rockhaven Area
desc: Remnants of the Union Manufacturing Co. dam on the Patapsco and the embankment of the long millrace it fed toward Oella, in the Hollofield area of Patapsco Valley State Park below US-40. Reached on foot by park trails.

name: USAS American Mariner
desc: USAS American Mariner was a United States Army research vessel from January 1959 to 30 September 1963. She was originally assigned to the DAMP Project by the Advanced Research Projects Agency (ARPA) to attempt to collect radar signature data on incoming intercontinental ballistic missiles in the…

name: Utica Mills Covered Bridge
desc: Burr truss covered bridge first built in 1834 over the Monocacy; the half that survived an 1889 flood was moved here to Fishing Creek. Still open to cars.

name: Veach Gap and South Fork Overlook
desc: Gradual climb on an old road through Veach Gap to the Massanutten east ridge, where three overlooks look down on the bends of the South Fork Shenandoah and across to the Blue Ridge.

name: Violettes Lock (Lock 23)
desc: Double lock of red Seneca sandstone beside the rubble of Dam 2, where the Potomac spreads wide. Canoe and kayak ramp, put-in for the Seneca Breaks paddle loop; open sunsets over the water.

name: Virginia Furnace
desc: Water-powered stone blast furnace on Muddy Creek, kept since 1933 as a small DAR roadside park on WV-26 north of Albright. Pull-off parking; free.

name: Virginius Island ruins
desc: Flat walk from Lower Town among the stone foundations, mill races and walls of a 19th-century factory village on a 12-acre island in the Shenandoah.

name: Walnut Creek Park
desc: Albemarle County park south of Charlottesville with a summer swimming beach on its lake and 15 miles of trails for hiking, running and mountain biking.

facts.fee: Beach fee in summer for non-residents

name: Walnut Street Bridge
desc: Iron truss bridge over the Susquehanna that lost three western spans to an ice flood in 1996 and was never rejoined. Walk the surviving half from downtown to City Island and look across the gap at the stranded far end. Free.

name: Walton Beach Nature Preserve
desc: Small town-owned preserve at the north end of North Beach where the marsh meets the Bay: a short path, benches and a strip of natural shoreline away from the paid beach.

name: Warrenton Branch Greenway
desc: Paved rail-trail from the old depot yard in Old Town Warrenton, with a restored caboose at the trailhead and two bridges; extended to about 2.2 miles each way.

name: Washington Monument, Mount Vernon Place
desc: The first major monument to George Washington, finished in 1829. A 227-step spiral stair climbs inside the column to a lookout over Mount Vernon's squares and the city. Small fee to climb; limited days.

name: Watersedge Park
desc: 9.5-acre county park at the end of Bullneck Road in Dundalk with a recreation pier, shoreline access, picnic pavilions and ball fields.

name: Watkins Regional Park
desc: Large county park with a nature center, wooded loop trails, a campground, the Old Maryland Farm and an antique carousel and miniature train that run in summer.

name: Wellington Beach
desc: Small county beach just north of Crisfield, near the Janes Island channel, with a fishing pier, kayak launch, restrooms and a playground.

name: Wenona Harbor, Deal Island
desc: The end of the Deal Island road: a watermen's harbor on Tangier Sound stacked with crab pots, where a few working skipjacks still tie up.

name: White Rocks (South Mountain)
desc: Steep trail to a spine of white quartzite at the northern tip of South Mountain, with views over the Cumberland Valley; the spur joins the Appalachian Trail on the ridge.

name: Whitehaven Ferry
desc: Free three-car cable ferry across the Wicomico River at a village of old houses, on a crossing in use since the 1680s. Runs daily except Christmas, weather and tide permitting.

name: Whitney State Forest
desc: 148 acres of quiet woods three miles south of Warrenton with 7 miles of interlaced forest trails and gated roads; an easy perimeter loop for a walk or trail run.

name: Wilde Lake
desc: Columbia's first man-made lake (1966), 22 acres circled by a 1.46-mile walking path, with a stepped dam spillway at the east end.

name: Wildwood Park
desc: Marshy lake on the north edge of Harrisburg circled by a flat loop of paved path and boardwalk, with a nature center. Good for herons, egrets and lotus blooms.

name: Wilkes Street Tunnel
desc: Short stone-and-brick railroad tunnel from the 1850s under Wilkes St in Old Town, now a foot and bike path running from S. Royal St toward the Potomac waterfront. Free, always open.

name: William H. Kain County Park (Lake Redman)
desc: Two water-supply lakes just south of York with boat rentals, a bird-viewing area and miles of shoreline trail.

name: William Paca Garden
desc: Restored two-acre 18th-century pleasure garden behind the William Paca House: terraces, parterres, a fish-shaped pond and a summerhouse hidden inside the historic district. Admission charged.

name: Wilmer Park
desc: Lawn and promenade on the Chester River at the foot of Chestertown's colonial waterfront, next to the college boathouse. Good for a short riverside walk.

name: Wilson Bridge
desc: Five-arch limestone bridge of 1819 over Conococheague Creek, 210 ft long and the longest of the county's old stone bridges. It carried the National Road.

name: Wilson Point Park
desc: County waterfront park on Dark Head Creek in Middle River with a double boat ramp, piers, a floating dock, a boardwalk and a path system. No ramp fee.

name: Wilson's Bridge
desc: Five-arch, 210 ft limestone bridge built in 1819 for the National Pike over Conococheague Creek; closed to traffic after Tropical Storm Agnes damaged it in 1972. Beside US-40 west of Hagerstown with a small pull-off; walk onto it.

name: Wincopin Trails
desc: Color-coded natural trails off Vollmerhausen Road dropping through woods to the meeting of the Middle and Little Patuxent rivers, with river overlooks and old bridge abutments.

name: Windy Run Park
desc: Short wooded trail from an Arlington neighborhood down Windy Run to the Potomac Heritage Trail, where the stream falls over a rock ledge beside the river. Steep, rocky footing near the bottom.

name: Wolf Gap Recreation Area
desc: Free primitive campground on the VA/WV line, once the site of a 1930s African American CCC camp. Big Schloss (north) and Tibbet Knob (south) both start from the lot.

name: Wolf's Hollow County Park
desc: Wooded hollow along Octoraro Creek with several miles of trail, a small waterfall and old mill ruins. Just east of the Lancaster County line.

name: Woodend Nature Sanctuary
desc: 40-acre headquarters of Nature Forward around a 1920s mansion: meadow, pond, restored stream and a short nature trail. Free; no dogs.

name: Woodland Beach
desc: Faded Victorian resort village at the end of a marsh causeway on Delaware Bay, with a small public beach and a long fishing pier.

name: Woodland Ferry
desc: Free cable ferry carrying a few cars across the Nanticoke River at a crossing that dates to the 1740s. It runs limited weekday hours and is often out of service, so check before going.

name: Woodland Trail (Chincoteague NWR)
desc: Paved 1.6-mile loop through loblolly pine forest with an overlook where the ponies often graze the marsh. Delmarva fox squirrels live in the pines.

name: Wootons Landing Wetland Park
desc: Restored wetlands on a former gravel mine beside the Patuxent River, with a level loop trail around the ponds and a cartop launch on the river. Quiet and good for herons and waterfowl.

name: Workhouse Arts Center (former Lorton prison)
desc: Brick quadrangle of the 1910 DC workhouse where suffragists were jailed in 1917, now artist studios and a prison museum. Grounds are free to walk; galleries keep limited hours.

name: Wrightsville Lime Kilns
desc: Bank of 19th-century stone lime kilns preserved beside the Susquehanna in Wrightsville, just north of the west end of the long concrete arch bridge. Roadside; free.

name: Wye Oak State Park and Wye Mill
desc: Tiny park around the stump of the Wye Oak, a 460-year-old white oak that was the largest in the country until a 2002 storm felled it. A clone grows on the spot; a working 1682 grist mill is next door.

name: Yankauer Nature Preserve
desc: Audubon preserve with easy loop trails through cedar and hardwood forest to a bluff above the Potomac. Good spring wildflowers.

name: Alan Seeger Natural Area
desc: Alan Seeger Natural Area is located in Huntingdon County, Pennsylvania, United States, approximately nine miles south of Boalsburg, within Rothrock State Forest in the Appalachian Mountains. It is traversed by the long-distance Standing Stone Trail, and includes other short trails.

name: Awbury Arboretum
desc: Awbury Arboretum 55 acres (22 ha) is a nonprofit arboretum and estate located at 1 Awbury Road in Germantown, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. Its grounds are open daily without charge. Established in 1916, it then became a nonprofit organization in 1984.

name: Bear Rocks
desc: Bear Rocks is a widely recognized symbol of West Virginia wilderness and among the most frequently photographed places in the state. It is a well-known landmark on the eastern edge of the plateau that includes the Dolly Sods Wilderness.

name: Beechdale Bridge
desc: The Beechdale Bridge, also known as the Burkholder Bridge, is a historic covered bridge in Brothersvalley Township, Somerset County, Pennsylvania. Township Route 548 crosses Buffalo Creek on the bridge, southwest of Berlin.

name: Bickle Knob
desc: Bickle Knob is a mountain summit located east of Elkins in Randolph County, West Virginia, USA. Easily accessible during warm-weather months, Bickle Knob is also home to one of the few remaining observation towers in Monongahela National Forest.

name: Buttermilk Falls Natural Area
desc: Buttermilk Falls Natural Area is located in Clyde, Indiana County, Pennsylvania, United States. They are 46 feet (14 m) high. There is also a short trail to a location behind the falls.

name: Custis Trail
desc: The Custis Trail is a hilly 4.5 miles (7.2 km)-long shared use path in Arlington County, Virginia. The asphalt-paved trail travels along Interstate 66 (I-66) between Rosslyn and the Washington and Old Dominion Railroad Trail (W&OD Trail) at Bon Air Park.

name: Elliott Knob
desc: Elliott Knob is one of the highest mountains in the northern portions of the U.S. state of Virginia. At 4,463 ft (1,360 m), the peak is located on the ridge known as Great North Mountain. A subpeak known simply as "Hogback" (4,447 ft (1,355 m)) is located 0.5 mi (0.80 km) to the southwest.

name: Ferncliff Peninsula Natural Area
desc: Ferncliff Peninsula Natural Area is a 100-acre (40 ha) peninsula with a unique habitat with many rare and unusual, for Pennsylvania, plants. It is part of Ohiopyle State Park, near Ohiopyle, Pennsylvania.

name: Flagpole Knob
desc: Shenandoah Mountain is a mountain ridge approximately 73 miles (117 km) long in Virginia and West Virginia. The steep, narrow, sandstone-capped ridge extends from northern Bath County, Virginia to southern Hardy County, West Virginia.

name: Four Mile Run Trail
desc: The Four Mile Run Trail is a 7-mile long, paved shared use path in Arlington County and Falls Church. It runs along Four Mile Run from Benjamin Banneker Park in Falls Church to the Mount Vernon Trail near Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, where Four Mile Run empties into the Potomac River.

name: Ghost Town Trail
desc: The Ghost Town Trail is a rail trail in Western Pennsylvania that runs 36 miles (58 km) between Black Lick, Indiana County, and Ebensburg, Cambria County.

name: Herline Covered Bridge
desc: The Heirline Covered Bridge is an historic wooden covered bridge which is located in Harrison Township and Napier Township in Bedford County, Pennsylvania. It crosses the Juniata River, and is one of fifteen historic covered bridges which are located in Bedford County.

name: Kesler Tunnel
desc: Kessler Tunnel is an abandoned railroad tunnel in Allegany County, Maryland, located about 8.5 miles (13.7 km) east-northeast of Oldtown. It was built by the Western Maryland Railway (WM) in 1906. It was constructed with concrete arch portals and the roof has wood planking.

name: Longwood Gardens
desc: Longwood Gardens is a public garden that consists of more than 1,100 acres (445 hectares; 4.45 km2) of gardens, woodlands, and meadows in the Brandywine Creek Valley in Kennett Square, Pennsylvania, United States.

name: Lower Humbert Covered Bridge
desc: The Lower Humbert Covered Bridge, or the Faidley Covered Bridge, is an 126-foot-6-inch (38.56 m) Burr Arch truss covered bridge that crosses Laurel Hill Creek, in Lower Turkeyfoot Township, Somerset County in the U.S. state of Pennsylvania.

name: Massanutten Trail
desc: The Massanutten Trail is a 71-mile (114 km) National Recreation Trail located in George Washington National Forest in western Virginia, specifically the central Shenandoah Valley. Much of the path is steep and rugged terrain, and presents many mountain vistas.

name: Nanjemoy Natural Resources Management Area Purse Area
desc: Purse State Park is a former Maryland state park located on the Potomac River in Charles County that has been subsumed into the 1,365-acre (552 ha) Nanjemoy Wildlife Management Area.

name: Original Sand Patch Tunnel
desc: Sand Patch Grade is an approximately 100-mile-long (160 km) section of railroad track known for its steep grades and curves through the Allegheny Mountains of Pennsylvania and western Maryland.

name: Salisbury University Arboretum
desc: The Salisbury University Arboretum, also known as The Glenda Chatham Clarke Arboretum, is an arboretum on the campus of Salisbury University in Salisbury, Maryland. The collection was begun in 1985.

name: Seneca Creek Greenway
desc: The Seneca Creek Greenway Trail is a 24.2-mile (38.9 km) long trail that runs along Seneca Creek from the Potomac River to Watkins Road, with some parts maintained by the state of Maryland and some parts maintained by Montgomery County, MD

name: Shavers Mountain
desc: Shavers Mountain, is a high and rugged ridge situated in the Allegheny Mountains of eastern West Virginia. It is about 35 miles (56 km) long, north to south, and several of its peaks exceed 4,000 feet (1,200 m) in elevation.

name: Stickpile Tunnel
desc: Stickpile Tunnel, also known as Greenridge Tunnel, is an abandoned railroad tunnel in Allegany County, Maryland, located about 2.5 miles (4.0 km) southwest of Little Orleans. It was built by the Western Maryland Railway (WM) in 1906.

name: The Priest
desc: The Priest (DePriest) is a mountain in Nelson County, Virginia. The peak of the mountain is the highest point in the county.

name: Fort Necessity National Battlefield
desc: Fort Necessity National Battlefield is a National Battlefield in Fayette County, Pennsylvania, United States, which preserves the site of the Battle of Fort Necessity.

name: Great Eastern Trail - C&O Canal
desc: The Great Eastern Trail is a network of hiking trails forming a long-distance route in the eastern United States. North of Georgia, the route runs parallel to, and slightly to the west of, the Appalachian Trail.

name: Great Shoals Light
desc: Great Shoals Light was a screw-pile lighthouse in the Chesapeake Bay at the mouth of the Wicomico River.

name: Janes Island Light
desc: The Janes Island Light was a screw-pile lighthouse located near Crisfield in the U.S. state of Maryland. Twice destroyed by ice, it was replaced in 1935 with an automated beacon.

name: Mom Rinker's Rock
desc: Mom Rinker's Rock is a scenic outlook in Wissahickon Valley Park along the Wissahickon Creek in the city of Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, United States. It is located on a ridge on the eastern side of the park just a little north of the Walnut Lane Bridge, close by the statue dedicated to Toleration.

name: Sharkfin Shoal Light
desc: The Sharkfin Shoal Light was a screw-pile lighthouse located at the mouth of the Nanticoke River in the Chesapeake Bay, US.

name: Baumgardner's Mill Covered Bridge
desc: The Baumgardener's Covered Bridge is a covered bridge that spans Pequea Creek in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, United States. A county-owned and maintained bridge, its official designation is the Pequea #10 Bridge. Note: The mill was constructed in 1800.

name: Bitzer's Mill Covered Bridge
desc: The Bitzer's Mill Covered Bridge is a covered bridge that spans the Conestoga River in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, United States. It is the oldest bridge in the county still in use. A county-owned and maintained bridge, its official designation is the Big Conestoga #2 Bridge.

name: Bowser’s Covered Bridge
desc: The Osterburg Covered Bridge, also known as Bowser's Covered Bridge, is a wooden covered bridge at East St. Clair Township in Bedford County, Pennsylvania. It is a 90-foot-long (27 m), Burr Truss bridge with a shallow gable roof.

name: Bucher's Mill Covered Bridge
desc: The Bucher's Mill Covered Bridge or Butcher's Mill Covered Bridge is a covered bridge that spans Cocalico Creek in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, United States. After the Landis Mill Covered Bridge, it is the second shortest covered bridge in the county.

name: Colemanville Covered Bridge
desc: The Colemanville Covered Bridge is a covered bridge that spans Pequea Creek in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, United States. After Hunsecker's Mill Covered Bridge, it is Lancaster County's second-longest single-span covered bridge still being used.

name: Conway Robinson Memorial State Forest
desc: Conway Robinson State Forest is a state forest in Prince William County, Virginia, near Manassas National Battlefield Park. It serves as a wildflower and wildlife sanctuary.

name: Cuppett's Covered Bridge
desc: The Cuppett's Covered Bridge, which was built by Cuppett brothers William & Philip on September 14, 1882, is a historic covered bridge that is located in Napier Township, Bedford County, Pennsylvania.

name: Delaware Canal State Park Access Area
Delaware Canal State Park: Bristol Lagoon
Dellville Covered Bridge
desc: The Dellville Covered Bridge is a wooden covered bridge located in Dellville Pennsylvania. It is a 174-foot-long (53 m), three span, burr truss bridge over Shermans Creek, built to replace a previous covered bridge constructed in 1889 by Andrew Clouser.

name: Erb's Covered Bridge
desc: The Erb's Covered Bridge is a covered bridge that spans Hammer Creek in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, United States. A county-owned and maintained bridge, its official designation is the Hammer Creek #1 Bridge.

name: Erwinna Covered Bridge
desc: The Erwinna Covered Bridge is a wooden covered bridge that spans Swamp Creek in Erwinna, Pennsylvania, United States. The bridge was constructed using a lattice-type design. The National Register of Historic Places lists the date built as 1871, while county records say 1832.

name: Fair Hill Covered Bridge
desc: Foxcatcher Farm Covered Bridge, also known as Big Elk Creek Covered Bridge and Fair Hill Covered Bridge, is a Burr truss wooden covered bridge near Fair Hill, Maryland, United States.

name: Fischtner Covered Bridge

name: Geiger Covered Bridge
desc: Geiger Covered Bridge is a historic wooden covered bridge located at North Whitehall Township, Lehigh County, Pennsylvania. It is a 112-foot-long (34 m), Burr Truss bridge, constructed in 1860. It has vertical plank siding and an entry portal of stepped square planks.

name: Gibson's Covered Bridge
desc: Gibson's Covered Bridge, also known as Harmony Hill Bridge, is an historic, wooden, covered bridge which is located in East Bradford Township and West Bradford Township, Chester County, Pennsylvania. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1980.

name: Halls Mill Covered Bridge
desc: The Halls Mill Covered Bridge is an historic, wooden covered bridge which is located in Hopewell Township in Bedford County, Pennsylvania. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1980.

name: Heikes Covered Bridge

name: Jackson's Sawmill Covered Bridge

name: Jacksons Mill Covered Bridge

name: Jones Road Decommissioned Airstrip, Patuxent River State Park

name: Keller's Mill Covered Bridge

name: Kennedy Bridge

name: Knecht's Covered Bridge
desc: Knecht's Covered Bridge is a historic covered bridge in Springfield Township, Bucks County, Pennsylvania. It crosses Cooks Creek on Knecht Bridge Road south of Springtown. Built in 1873 in the town truss style, the bridge is 110 feet long and 15 feet wide.

name: Landis Mill Covered Bridge
desc: The Landis Mill Covered Bridge is a covered bridge that spans the Little Conestoga Creek in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, United States. A county-owned and maintained bridge, its official designation is the Little Conestoga #1 Bridge.

name: Leaman's Place Covered Bridge
desc: The Leaman's Place Covered Bridge is a covered bridge that spans Pequea Creek in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, United States. A county-owned and maintained bridge, its official designation is the Pequea #4 Bridge. The bridge is also known as Eshelman's Mill Covered Bridge and Paradise Bridge.

name: Lime Valley Covered Bridge
desc: The Lime Valley Covered Bridge or Strasburg Bridge is a covered bridge that spans Pequea Creek in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, United States. A county-owned and maintained bridge, its official designation is the Pequea #8 Bridge.

name: Manasses Guth Covered Bridge
desc: Manasses Guth Covered Bridge is a historic wooden covered bridge located at South Whitehall Township, Lehigh County, Pennsylvania. It is a 108-foot-long (33 m), Burr Truss bridge, constructed in 1858, and rebuilt in 1882. It has vertical siding.

name: Neff's Mill Covered Bridge
desc: The Neff's Mill Covered Bridge or Bowman's Mill Covered Bridge is a covered bridge that spans the Pequea Creek on the border between West Lampeter Township and Strasburg Township in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, United States.

name: New Baltimore Bridge
desc: The New Baltimore Bridge is a historic covered bridge in Allegheny Township, Somerset County, Pennsylvania. Township Route 812 crosses the Raystown Branch Juniata River on the bridge. The Queenpost truss bridge was built in 1879 and is 86 feet 6 inches (26.37 m) in length and 12 feet (3.7 m) wide.

name: New Germantown Covered Bridge
desc: The New Germantown Covered Bridge is a historic wooden covered bridge located in Jackson Township, Perry County, Pennsylvania, near New Germantown. Constructed in 1891, it is a 74-foot-long (23 m) King post bridge and crosses Shermans Creek.

name: Pine Valley Covered Bridge

name: Pinetown Bushong's Mill Covered Bridge
desc: The Pinetown Bushong's Mill Covered Bridge is a covered bridge that spans the Conestoga River in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, United States. A county-owned and maintained bridge, its official designation is the Big Conestoga #6 Bridge.

name: President's House
desc: President's House in Philadelphia was the third U.S. presidential mansion, following the first two in New York City. President George Washington occupied the Philadelphia house from November 27, 1790 to March 10, 1797.

name: Red Run Covered Bridge

name: Rex Covered Bridge

name: Ryot Covered Bridge
desc: The Ryot Covered Bridge is an historic wooden covered bridge in West St. Clair Township in Bedford County, Pennsylvania, United States. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1980.

name: Schenck's Mill Covered Bridge
desc: The Schenk's Mill Covered Bridge or Shenk's Mill Covered Bridge is a covered bridge that spans the Big Chiques Creek in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, United States. A county-owned and maintained bridge, its official designation is the Big Chiques #4 Bridge.

name: Schuylkill River Park Community Garden
desc: The Schuylkill River Park Community Garden (SRPCG) is a unique approximately 70 plot (over 22,000 square feet (2,000 m2) of land) community garden located at 25th and Manning Streets in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.

name: Shofuso Japanese House and Garden
desc: Shofuso (Japanese: 松風荘, lit. 'pine breeze villa'), also known as Japanese House and Garden, is a 17th century-style Japanese house and garden in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, United States.

name: Siegrist's Mill Covered Bridge

name: Thomas Mill Covered Bridge
desc: The Thomas Mill Covered Bridge, aka the Thomas Mill Bridge or the Thomas Mill Road Covered Bridge, is a historic, single-span, wooden covered bridge across the Wissahickon Creek in Wissahickon Valley Park in Northwest Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.

name: Uhlerstown Covered Bridge
desc: The Uhlerstown Covered Bridge spans the Delaware Canal in the village of Uhlerstown in Tinicum Township, Bucks County, Pennsylvania. The historic bridge was built in 1856, and was reconstructed using original materials in 1985.

name: United States Botanic Garden

name: Wertz's Covered Bridge

name: White Rock Forge Covered Bridge

name: Whites Woods Nature Center

name: Appalachian Trail

name: Maintop Mountain

name: Mount Porte Crayon

name: Nakedtop

name: Negro Mountain Tunnel

name: Belvoir Manor

name: German-American Friendship Garden

name: Olson Lookout Tower

name: Potomac Heritage National Scenic Trail (right bank)

name: Cynwyd Heritage Trail
